At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world. Together, we are writing the next episode - pushing the boundaries of storytelling, global fandom and making the unimaginable a reality. We are a dream team obsessed with the uncomfortable excitement of discovering what happens when you merge creativity, intuition and cutting-edge technology. Come be a part of what’s next.


Content & Business Products (CBP) Overview

The Content & Business Products (CBP) teams are fundamental to Netflix's mission to entertain the world. This organization is responsible for building the products and services that optimize and automate the entire content creation lifecycle, from initial concept and financial planning to global launch and promotion.


CBP is the engine behind “pitch to play,” enabling our teams to create, manage, and distribute content at scale. In addition, we build and maintain critical enterprise products that ensure efficient operations across key internal departments, including Finance, Talent, N-Tech and Customer Support.


Role Overview

We're looking for an accomplished Senior Manager, Enterprise Program Operations to lead and grow the team responsible for the operational health, reliability, and continuous improvement of the programs, products, and platforms that power Content & Business Products. In this pivotal role, you'll oversee program management and operations across NTech - the operational arm of internal support, including AV, IT operations, and ITAM, serving as the frontline for our enterprise tools and services and Customer Service, representing the support and operations that serve Netflix members. You'll also lead technology integration for M&A activity, bringing acquired teams, tools, and systems smoothly into Netflix's enterprise environment. Across all of this, you'll ensure that the systems and support functions underpinning our core business -Finance, Legal, Talent, Customer Service, and IT  run reliably at scale, and that operational issues are anticipated, prevented, and resolved quickly when they occur.


As a seasoned operations and program leader, you'll build and mentor a team spanning technology operations, general program management, and frontline support functions, establishing the processes, tooling, and governance that keep our enterprise products and services running smoothly. You'll act as a key partner to Engineering, Product, IT, Customer Service, and business stakeholders across CBP, and a steady hand during M&A integrations, translating operational learnings into proactive improvements that balance the pace of delivery with the reliability our internal and external users depend on.


Responsibilities

  • Lead and Mentor a High-Performing Team: Recruit, hire, develop, and retain a world-class team of program managers and operations professionals spanning NTech, Customer Service, and enterprise program functions. Provide coaching, mentorship, and career development opportunities, fostering a culture of continuous learning and accountability.
  • Enterprise Program Leadership: Oversee planning and execution of programs across NTech - AV, IT operations, and ITAM, the frontline for our enterprise tools and services — and Customer Service, the support and operations serving Netflix members. Ensure alignment with CBP and company-wide objectives.
  • Technology M&A Integration: Own the operational and technical integration of acquired companies, teams, and tools into Netflix's enterprise environment. Lead cross-functional integration planning, stakeholder coordination, and timeline management to bring new technology into our systems and processes smoothly.
  • General Program Management: Define, implement, and optimize scalable program management processes, governance, and best practices across the CBP portfolio. Drive roadmap planning, OKR reviews, and continuous improvement in program execution.
  • Cross-Functional Partnership: Act as a central point of contact and trusted partner for Engineering, Product, IT, Customer Service, Finance, Legal, and Talent stakeholders. Facilitate effective communication, triage, and decision-making across programs and operational events.
  • Operational Excellence: Define and track operational KPIs and SLAs for NTech and Customer Service operations. Drive continuous improvement in incident management, support quality, and service delivery.
  • Risk Management and Mitigation: Proactively identify, assess, and mitigate technical, operational, and organizational risks - including those introduced during M&A integrations. Develop contingency and escalation plans, and drive resolution of critical issues to closure.
  • Influence and Communication: Communicate program status, operational risk, and integration progress clearly to audiences ranging from individual contributors to executive leadership.
  • Resource Planning: Collaborate with Engineering, Product, and business leadership to forecast and allocate staffing, tooling, and integration budget needs across NTech, Customer Service, and program management, identifying capacity constraints ahead of key launches, seasonal peaks, and acquisitions.

Qualifications

  • 10+ years of experience in technical program management, IT/enterprise support operations, or customer service operations, with at least 4 years in a leadership role managing and mentoring a team.
  • Proven track record leading large-scale, cross-functional programs, including operational support for frontline functions such as AV, IT operations, ITAM, or service desk.
  • Experience integrating 3P technology, tools, teams, or processes into a organization's enterprise environment.
  • Experience partnering with or leading Customer Service business and operations functions.
  • Demonstrated experience building, growing, and leading high-performing operations or program management teams.
  • Exceptional cross-functional collaboration and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence without direct authority.
  • Strong understanding of enterprise systems, software development lifecycles, and program management methodologies and best practices.
  • Excellent communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to thrive in a dynamic, ambiguous, and rapidly evolving environment.

What Sets You Apart

  • A strategic leader who sets direction across NTech, Customer Service, and enterprise program operations while empowering and growing a high-performing team.
  • An influential partner adept at navigating complex, cross-functional programs and technology integrations, and making critical operational trade-offs.
  • A proactive force who brings organization to ambiguity — including the ambiguity of M&A integration — and anticipates operational risk before it impacts the business.
  • A true culture champion who embodies organizational values and drives executional excellence.

As a part of the Gemini User Signals team, a Research Scientist will help drive the post-training strategy of our most advanced models, dedicated to establishing the "flywheel" of alignment, converting complex user interactions and feedback into training signals that fundamentally improve model behavior. In this role, you will lead research into reward modeling, preference optimization, and data-centric strategies to close the loop between user deployment and model training. You will help define the horizontal recipes that allow us to scale these insights across different modalities and model families.Artificial intelligence will be one of humanity’s most transformative inventions. At Google DeepMind, we are a pioneering AI lab with exceptional interdisciplinary teams focused on advancing AI development to solve complex global challenges and accelerate high-quality product innovation for billions of users. We use our technologies for widespread public benefit and scientific discovery, ensuring safety and ethics are always our highest priority.

We are pushing the boundaries across multiple domains. Our global teams offer varied learning opportunities and career pathways for those driven to achieve exceptional results through collective effort.

Responsibilities

  • Design and implement mechanisms to harvest, filter, and utilize high-quality user signals (implicit and explicit) to iteratively improve Gemini models.
  • Develop and refine reward models and critique models that accurately capture user intent and satisfaction, serving as the foundation for Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) and other alignment techniques.
  • Create and validate "horizontal" post-training recipes that can be robustly applied across different model sizes and modalities (including text and audio).
  • Investigate novel methods for weighting, synthesizing, and selecting data to maximize the impact of user signals on model performance.
  • Establish rigorous evaluation frameworks to measure the correlation between offline metrics (reward model accuracy) and online user satisfaction.

Qualifications

Minimum qualifications:

  • PhD in Machine Learning, natural language processing, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).
  • Experience with software development using Python and one or more deep learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch or JAX).
  • Research experience in post-training, reinforcement learning (RL), agentic RL, preference learning, or reward modeling.
  • First-author (or co-author) publication in one or more peer-reviewed machine learning or natural language processing (NLP) conferences (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP).

Preferred qualifications:

  • First-author publications at top ML/NLP venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP).
  • Experience with modern alignment and post-training methods (e.g., RLHF, DPO, PPO, rejection sampling, or self-play).
  • Experience modeling multi-turn interaction data, agent trajectories/logs, or user feedback (implicit and explicit signals).
  • Experience training or evaluating reward models, critique models, or automated evaluators (e.g., LLM-as-a-judge).
  • Experience in agentic post-training.

Join DeepMind’s mission to solve intelligence and benefit humanity by building the next generation of agentic AI. As a Software Engineer on the Gemini App Skills Platform, you will be a key contributor to the extensible execution layer that transforms Gemini from a conversational assistant into an action-oriented, universal agent.

In this role, you will architect the systems that allow Gemini to discover, retrieve, and execute modular capabilities (skills) across Google, DeepMind, and third-party ecosystems. Your work will bridge foundation model intelligence and real-world execution spanning dynamic context engineering (system instructions), low-latency routing algorithms, and automated evaluation frameworks. While this role focuses heavily on Large Language Model (LLM) behavior and evaluation, you will dive directly into Gemini app’s production serving infrastructure (primarily C++) and Python evaluation pipelines to make high-impact, hands-on architectural enhancements. You will have an opportunity to operate at the center of Google’s flagship AI product. You will see your code, prompts, and evaluation standards actively shape the user experience for hundreds of millions of users across web, mobile (Android/iOS), and Chrome, helping define how people and AI interact with software.

Artificial intelligence will be one of humanity’s most transformative inventions. At DeepMind, we are a pioneering AI lab with exceptional interdisciplinary teams focused on advancing AI development to solve complex global challenges and accelerate high-quality product innovation for billions of users. We use our technologies for widespread public benefit and scientific discovery, ensuring safety and ethics are always our highest priority.

We are pushing the boundaries across multiple domains. Our global teams offer diverse learning opportunities and varied career pathways for those driven to achieve exceptional results through collective effort.

Responsibilities

  • Design and build intelligent skill discovery, hybrid routing architectures, and low-latency C++ serving components across Gemini on web, mobile, and Chrome.
  • Pioneer dynamic system instructions, prompt representations, and semantic retrieval schemas that enable Gemini to seamlessly navigate expanding skill catalogs without attention dilution or quality regressions.
  • Design automated evaluation frameworks (auto-raters, simulated environments, and benchmarking suites) to rigorously measure single-turn triggering precision, multi-turn tool, and parameter validity.
  • Perform in-depth loss analysis on production telemetry, drive iterative prompt/model hill-climbing to surpass quality thresholds, and set standards for system reliability and clean architecture across the organization.
  • Partner closely with DeepMind Research, Search, Vertical teams (e.g., local, shopping), and external Engineering teams to onboard new modular capabilities onto the platform.

Qualifications

Minimum qualifications:

  • Experience developing software with large language models, agentic workflows, tool use, or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).
  • Experience designing evaluation datasets, automated rating systems, or conducting error analysis and prompt optimization for generative models.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience collaborating cross-functionally across research, product, and platform engineering teams to take novel AI features from prototype to production.
  • Demonstrated ability to design experimental setups, analyze model telemetry, and define reproducible metrics for complex features.

Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) combines software and systems engineering to build and run large-scale, massively distributed, fault-tolerant systems. SRE ensures that Google's services—both our internally critical and our externally-visible systems—have reliability, uptime appropriate to users' needs and a fast rate of improvement. Additionally SRE’s will keep an ever-watchful eye on our systems capacity and performance.


Much of our software development focuses on optimizing existing systems, building infrastructure and eliminating work through automation. On the SRE team, you’ll have the opportunity to manage the complex challenges of scale which are unique to Google, while using your expertise in coding, algorithms, complexity analysis and large-scale system design.

SRE's culture of intellectual curiosity, problem solving and openness is key to its success. Our organization brings together people with a wide variety of backgrounds, experiences and perspectives. We encourage them to collaborate, think big and take risks in a blame-free environment. We promote self-direction to work on meaningful projects, while we also strive to create an environment that provides the support and mentorship needed to learn and grow.

To learn more: check out our books on Site Reliability Engineering or read a career profile about why a Software Engineer chose to join SRE.

We prioritize security, efficiency, and reliability across everything we do - from developing our latest TPUs to running a global network, while driving towards shaping the future of hyperscale computing. Our global impact spans software and hardware, including Google Cloud’s Vertex AI, the leading AI platform for bringing Gemini models to enterprise customers.

Responsibilities

Google's software engineers develop the next-generation technologies that change how billions of users connect, explore, and interact with information and one another. Our products need to handle information at massive scale, and extend well beyond web search. We're looking for engineers who bring fresh ideas from all areas, including information retrieval, distributed computing, large-scale system design, networking and data storage, security, artificial intelligence, natural language processing, UI design and mobile; the list goes on and is growing every day. As a software engineer, you will work on a specific project critical to Google’s needs with opportunities to switch teams and projects as you and our fast-paced business grow and evolve. We need our engineers to be versatile, display leadership qualities and be enthusiastic to take on new problems across the full-stack as we continue to push technology forward.

In this team, you are a Software Engineer (SWE) in a team that builds state of the art video content understanding for YouTube Trust & Safety, with a focus on the efficient enforcement via automated decisions and ranking for review by a human or Large Language Model (LLM) expert.

At YouTube, we believe that everyone deserves to have a voice, and that the world is a better place when we listen, share, and build community through our stories. We work together to give everyone the power to share their story, explore what they love, and connect with one another in the process. Working at the intersection of cutting-edge technology and boundless creativity, we move at the speed of culture with a shared goal to show people the world. We explore new ideas, solve real problems, and have fun — and we do it all together.

Responsibilities

  • Analyze and understand gaps in our Video and Channels content understanding.
  • Build classifiers for YouTube videos and livestreams using various modalities (video, image, audio, audio transcripts, metadata).
  • Build efficient infrastructure to orchestrate classifiers and take enforcement actions.
  • Utilize human review and Gemini compute capacity to maximize safety on the platform.
  • Collaborate with research, operations, and product teams and Design, build, productionize, and maintain your solutions.

Qualifications

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.
  • 2 years of experience with software development in one or more programming languages (C++, Python, SQL), or 1 year of experience with an advanced degree.
  • 1 year of experience with one or more of the following: Speech/audio (e.g., technology duplicating and responding to the human voice), reinforcement learning (e.g., sequential decision making), ML infrastructure, or specialization in another ML field.

As a GenAI Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) at Google Cloud, you are an embedded builder who bridges the gap between frontier Artificial Intelligence (AI) products and production-grade reality within customers. Unlike traditional advisory roles, you function as an "innovator-builder," moving beyond high-level architecture to code, debug, and jointly ship bespoke agentic solutions directly within the customer’s environment. You will address blockers to production including solving the integration complexities, data readiness issues, and state-management challenges that prevent AI from reaching enterprise-grade maturity. You will serve a dual purpose, providing white glove deployment of complex AI systems and acting as a critical feedback loop, transforming real-world field insights into Google Cloud’s future product road map. You will embed with the engineering organizations of our largest customers and take Google's developer AI Gemini Code Assist, anti-gravity Integrated Development Environment (IDE), Software Development Kit (SDK), Command Line Interface (CLI) and the agentic surfaces beneath them from the first conversation to a production-grade workflow. You will find what actually slows an engineering organization down, design the system that fixes it, and own it end-to-end like discovery, build, roll-out, hardening, and the long tail of making it reliable.

It's an exciting time to join Google Cloud’s Go-To-Market team, leading the AI revolution for businesses worldwide. You’ll excel by leveraging Google's brand credibility—a legacy built on inventing foundational technologies and proven at scale. We’ll provide you with the world's most advanced AI portfolio, including frontier Gemini models, and the complete Vertex AI platform, helping you to solve business problems. We’re a collaborative culture providing direct access to DeepMind's engineering and research minds, empowering you to solve customer challenges. Join us to be the catalyst for our mission, drive customer success, and define the new cloud era—the market is yours.

Responsibilities

  • Serve as a developer for complex AI applications, transitioning from rapid prototypes to production-grade agentic workflows (e.g., multi-agent systems, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers) that drive measurable Return on Investment (ROI).
  • Architect and code the connective tissue between Google’s AI products and customer's live infrastructure, including APIs, legacy data silos, and security perimeters as part of an expert team.
  • Design and deploy production-grade agentic developer workflows on Google Cloud's AI stack, executing large-scale refactors, language migrations, Specification-to-Pull Request pipelines, and automated review/incident-to-fix loops.
  • Embed with customer's staff engineers and leaders to identify core SDLC bottlenecks, such as legacy migrations, test coverage, review latency, or onboarding friction, and define success metrics.
  • Integrate Google’s agentic systems into the customer's existing ISV and tools (e.g., Teamwork Graph, GitLab, ServiceNow, Slack) leveraging MCP and A2A protocols.

Qualifications

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 8 years of experience in cloud computing or a technical customer-facing role.
  • Experience deploying, scaling, and debugging Large Language Model (LLM) or agent-based systems in production environments (including tools, memory, orchestration, evaluation, tracing, and cost/latency profiling).
  • Experience with end-to-end technical ownership of engineering projects with executive stakeholders.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Master’s degree or PhD in AI, Computer Science, or a related technical field.
  • Experience implementing multi-agent systems using frameworks (e.g., LangGraph, CrewAI, Agent Development Kit (ADK)) and complex patterns (e.g., ReAct, self-reflection, hierarchical delegation).
  • Experience with agentic frameworks and harness layers, such as Google's Agent Development Kit (ADK) or equivalent, protocol-level interoperability (MCP, Agent-to-Agent (A2A)) across third-party Independent Software Vendor (ISV) platforms (e.g., ServiceNow), and security ecosystem in DevSecOps.
  • Knowledge of LLM-native metrics (e.g., tokens/sec, cost-per-request) and techniques for optimizing state management and granular tracing.

如果龙头公司纷纷选择 Google Cloud，这将对云计算技术在全球范围的推广产生巨大推动作用。当有教育机构、政府机构和其他企业签约使用 Google Cloud 产品后，您就要开始协助他们提高工作效率、移动办公能力和协作能力。您要倾听客户的诉求，为他们提供最有帮助的解决方案；为客户解决关键技术问题，助力 Google 销售人员开展工作；与产品营销管理团队和工程团队保持联络，及时了解行业趋势，并为改进 Google Cloud 产品出谋划策。

作为一名专攻数据分析的客户工程师 (CE)，您要与技术销售团队通力合作，向客户展现 Google Cloud 的独特优势；担任技术专家，负责加速取得技术胜利，并推动复杂、专业工作负载的采用；利用自己在我们产品领域所具备的专业知识，与平台 CE 合作设计数据基础架构，并开发最简可行产品 (MVP)，以便向客户推广高度专业化的新解决方案；解决以分析为中心的客户问题，并提供关键的反馈环，帮助客户消除障碍并积极影响产品开发。

在此职位上，您要了解客户的业务要求和技术要求，并演示基于 Google Cloud 的实用解决方案。您要综合运用销售专业知识、市场知识和直接技术对接能力，展现 Google Cloud 产品组合的价值。

We are looking for a Cloud Solution Architect (CSA) to join the Mission Critical team, working alongside our sr architects on the repeatable intellectual property they deliver to those customers. Your focus is making that IP better: integrating AI so each delivery takes less effort, sharpening the risks it exposes, and making what the customer receives clearer and more useful. During your ramp, you are not accountable for customer delivery; your customer exposure is structured observation alongside sr architects, which is how you build toward customer readiness. 

 

This opportunity will allow you to develop deep hands-on skills in AI and Azure engineering, learn how repeatable IP is designed, tested and shipped to a global delivery team, and build the technical judgment that leads to Mission Critical customer work. This role is 100% onsite at a Microsoft office. 

 

 

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond. 



Responsibilities

With direct coaching and guidance from more experienced peers: 

  • Improve the repeatable IP our architects already deliver: integrate AI so each delivery takes less effort, sharpen the risks it exposes, and make the customer-facing output clearer and more actionable. 

  • Turn field feedback into improvements: reproduce the reported problem in a lab, make the correction, write the check that proves it is fixed, and record what changed and why. 

  • Build and test the automation, queries, prompts, agents and templates that let a deliverable be executed consistently by many architects rather than rebuilt each time. 

  • Run the defined analysis behind a deliverable, such as behavior drift and integrity baselines, consumption and unit cost, or output quality scoring, validate the result against the documented method, and escalate anything that looks wrong. 

  • Write the material that makes IP usable by someone else: delivery guides, runbooks, worked examples, test data and acceptance checks. 

  • Act as customer zero for our own AI tooling and agents, stress-testing them internally before they are used in any customer environment, and reporting what breaks. 

  • Build Mission Critical, Azure and AI platform depth through structured onboarding, accreditation, teach backs and supervised observation of sr architect delivery, incorporating coaching feedback as you progress toward customer readiness. 

  • Builds familiarity around how to execute work in compliance with industry and Microsoft guidelines and procedures

Overview
Are you a customer-obsessed, AI-curious problem-solver who thrives in an inclusive, collaborative global team? Join Engineering Operations (EngOps), the organization driving operational excellence across the Microsoft Cloud to strengthen quality, reliability, security, and customer trust.
 
Our mission is to prevent issues before they happen by turning operational signals into action through AI-powered automation, enabling measurable customer impact at cloud scale. Our culture of empowerment, inclusion, and growth mindset defines how we work.
 
Within EngOps ACES, the Agent Fleet Operations (AFO) team is looking for an AI-first software engineer to join the Cloud Operational Demand Engineering (CØDE) organization and help advance our mission of driving operational demand to zero. We're seeking a hands-on engineer with a DevOps background — CI/CD and release engineering, safe deployment, observability, and always-on production operations — who pairs that discipline with AI engineering skills and a learn-it-all mindset.
 
You are passionate about applying AI to solve real customer problems and energized by the challenge of eliminating operational toil.
In this role, you will build and ship production AI solutions that reduce operational demand and improve customer outcomes. You will contribute to the technical execution that turns unresolved cases into autonomously resolved, customer-delighting outcomes — and help build the release, observability, and reliability practices that let a fleet of agents run safely in the customer path.
 
Role summary
As an individual contributor, you will be hands-on building and improving the agentic patterns that reduce operational demand and improve customer satisfaction. This is a DevOps and production-operations engineering role applied to autonomous AI: you own the delivery, quality, and production health of the components you build, not just their design. This role suits an engineer who has built and shipped production-scale AI systems — and ideally the CI/CD, safe-deployment, and reliability practices around them — and who wants to go deep on agentic resolution while collaborating closely across the team.
 
Team charter
Build, operationalize, and scale AI-native support experiences for Broad Commercial customers by transforming supportability knowledge into reusable, versioned, testable, and measurable assets that power product experiences, support engineers, and autonomous agents. The team reduces support demand, engineering toil, and time-to-resolution through AI-driven resolution capabilities that continuously learn from customer signals, unresolved cases, and operational insights.
 
AFO operates a fleet of autonomous agents that resolve customer support cases with human oversight. This is a production DevOps discipline, not a set of prototypes: agents run continuously in the customer path and released, observed, and improved with the same rigor as any always-on service. You and your team will build and run this system across several planes of a single AIOps suite:
• Fleet execution and live safety: operating the agents that execute individual cases end to end — evidence acquisition, diagnosis, reasoning, response composition, and safe escalation — alongside the live-safety services that continuously watch sentiment, risk, and unsafe or irreversible actions and can pause autonomy or transfer a case to a human.
• Evaluation and repair: running the evaluation systems that judge per-turn and completed-case quality, and the repair pipelines that turn failures into durable fixes — documentation, diagnostics, prompt/routing/policy changes, reusable skills, or product work items routed to the right engineering team.
• A control and learning plane: owning the lifecycle state machine that moves every change from observed → detected → diagnosed → repair candidate → independently evaluated → approved → shadowed → canaried → released → production-verified, with explicit expand, pause, revise,
 


Responsibilities
  • Build agentic resolution capabilities for AFO
  • Build and improve agentic patterns that raise autonomous resolution rate, accuracy, and customer satisfaction, contributing to the team's technical execution.
  • Deliver engineering for Agentic AI solutions
  • Deliver end-to-end features across autonomous AI systems, including orchestration, reasoning, retrieval, action execution, and human escalation workflows. Take capabilities from prototype through production across support surfaces while partnering effectively across dependent engineering teams.
  • Contribute to technical direction and engineering standards
  • Help shape the technical foundation for agent development by implementing architectures, design patterns, evaluation frameworks, and reusable platform capabilities.
  • Apply and help improve standards for prompts, tool interfaces, testing, versioning, code quality, CI/CD, and safe deployment practices (shadow, canary, progressive rollout, automated rollback) so agent behavior remains reliable, observable, and scalable.
  • Build evals that improve customer confidence that our agents are trustworthy in understanding customer sentiment and intent and in validating agentic actions.
  • Contribute to production health and reliability
  • Help run the service with a DevOps/SRE operating model. Support availability, latency, cost per resolution, SLOs and error budgets, regression detection, incident response, and the on-call rotation for a fleet of agents acting autonomously in the customer path. Build the observability needed to explain why an agent did what it did, and drive durable fixes rather than repeated mitigations.
  • Build and maintain evaluation systems
  • Contribute to the evaluation framework that determines whether agents are safe and effective in production. Build and maintain golden datasets, rubrics, judge agents, frozen anchors, and offline/online evaluation pipelines. Use evaluation signals to gate releases and continuously improve quality through production feedback loops.
  • Contribute to measurable business impact
  • Help move key business outcomes, including support demand reduction, autonomous resolution rate, resolution quality, time-to-resolution, engineer productivity, and customer satisfaction. Ensure the capabilities you build are measurable and directed toward the highest-impact opportunities.
  • Turn Customer Signals into Engineering Insight
  • Build mechanisms that convert unresolved cases, customer feedback, and dissatisfaction signals into actionable engineering insights. Help ensure recurring failure patterns improve future agent capabilities and route product fixes back to the appropriate engineering teams.
  • Grow your craft and share learnings
  • Deepen your agentic AI and DevOps craft, and extend the team's impact by sharing proven patterns, tools, and operational learnings with your peers.

 



Qualifications
Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field AND +8 years technical engineering experience in software engineering, applied AI/ML, or distributed systems, OR equivalent experience.
• 8+ years of IT experience and 3+ years of experience using Agentic AI
• Demonstrated hands-on experience building and shipping AI or machine learning systems in production.
• Demonstrated DevOps or SRE background: hands-on experience with CI/CD and release engineering, safe-deployment practices (e.g., blue/green, canary, progressive rollout, automated rollback), observability and monitoring, and participation in production incident response and on-call for always-on services.
 
Preferred qualifications
• Master's degree in Computer Science, AI, or a related field.
• Experience building and shipping multi-agent orchestration systems or agentic AI services in production.
• Experience with AI evaluation frameworks: rubrics, golden datasets, judge agents, offline and online evaluation.
• Experience with Azure AI Foundry, Azure OpenAI, or comparable enterprise AI platforms.
• Familiarity with agent security patterns: prompt injection defense, tool access controls, data boundary enforcement.
• DevOps/SRE toolchain depth: CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure-as-code, deployment automation, and progressive-delivery tooling (shadow, canary, feature/rollout gating, automated rollback).
• Observability engineering: building tracing, metrics, and logging for distributed or agentic systems and using them to drive durable fixes rather than repeated mitigations.
• Reliability practice: working with SLIs/SLOs and error budgets and taking part in the operational rhythm (live-site reviews, post-incident reviews, repair-item and corrective-action tracking) that keeps a fleet healthy.
• Experience contributing to cross-org or co-development engineering delivery with partner teams.
• Business acumen, with the ability to connect engineering work to measurable customer and business outcomes.
• Background in customer support engineering, supportability, or customer experience platforms.
• Experience operating always-on production services, including on-call participation and incident response.

Overview

Microsoft is on a mission to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. Our culture is centred on embracing a growth mindset, a theme of inspiring excellence, and encouraging teams and leaders to bring their full potential each day. In doing so, we create life-changing innovations that impact billions of lives around the world. You can help us achieve our mission.
 
Do you want to work in a company that is transforming the world? How about working on some of the most complex technology policy issues around, such as cross-jurisdictional law enforcement access, data sovereignty, or addressing emerging cyber threats?
 
We have an immediate opening for a highly motivated and experienced government affairs professional to join Microsoft’s Global Affairs team (CELA) in Nigeria. This is a senior Government Affairs role providing front-line government relations and regulatory affairs support for Microsoft’s interests in Nigeria and across priority West Africa markets.
 
The role sits at the intersection of technology, public policy, and government relations, with a focus on shaping technology policy, strengthening Microsoft’s relationships with governments and regulators, and advising internal leaders on critical public policy issues.
 
The successful candidate will engage with policymakers, industry bodies, and key stakeholders across areas including digital transformation and national technology agendas, cybersecurity and emerging threats, data sovereignty and cross-border data flows, technology regulation, legislation and compliance, and broader political and regulatory developments impacting Microsoft.
 
This is an Individual Contributor role, allowing you to focus your impact on the outcomes you are driving without a requirement for people management.
 
Who This Role Suits
This role is well suited to someone with significant experience in government affairs, public policy, or regulatory engagement, whether gained in government, a multinational company, a law firm, or an industry association. It would particularly suit someone who has worked independently or led policy efforts within a defined scope and is now looking to expand their impact in a global, complex, and high-visibility environment. The successful candidate will have a demonstrated ability to build relationships, navigate ambiguity, and influence key stakeholders both internally and externally.
 
Why This Role Matters
This role sits at a crucial point for Microsoft in Nigeria while also supporting Government Affairs priorities across West Africa. The successful candidate will directly shape how Microsoft navigates emerging regulatory environments, contributes to national digital transformation agendas, and ensures Microsoft’s voice is represented in key policy discussions.


Responsibilities

Strategy/Program Management  

  • Provides strategic vision and leadership for developing and executing top-priority program frameworks for achieving policy and political goals.  
  • Leads the formation of Microsoft’s policy agenda and positions on a broad range of issues, including designing and executing strategic campaigns, and identifying strategic opportunities for Microsoft to advance its long-term goals.   
  • Provides advice and counsel to executive management on unusually complex and critical issues or matters of concern to Microsoft and the industry.   
  • Anticipates and addresses novel issues and opportunities facing Microsoft and the industry in a rapidly changing and ambiguous environment and leads the development of associated strategies.   
  • Directs strategies to ensure regulations and legislation positively impact Microsoft's products, operations, associates, and customers by collaborating with coalitions and relevant interest groups to achieve desired regulatory or legislative outcomes; negotiates and aligns complex or conflicting policy with Microsoft's goals and strategy; monitors and responds to complex regulatory issues and new policies.   

 

Subject Matter Expertise and Influence 

  • Develops and implements strategies for leveraging partnerships with external partners and key influencers to significantly impact the advancement of Microsoft’s policy and political agenda.  
  • Maintains relationships with key influencers to gather and apply intelligence findings through a network of key senior executives and external stakeholders regarding highly strategic or sensitive issues affecting Microsoft’s long-term objectives or future issues.  
  • Advises and partners with senior executives and key/senior-level external stakeholders to gain buy in on policy positions by providing expertise, strategic vision and anticipating future issues; prepares senior and executive stakeholder for public testimony on complex issues.  
  • Provides thought leadership and champions cutting-edge initiatives and solutions that significantly impact the advancement of Microsoft’s long-term objectives and priorities.  

 

Representing Microsoft  

  • Determines strategy for developing internal/external events to drive Government Affairs objectives and social media engagement.   
  • Drives the communication framework and messaging development for Government Affairs to drive and enhance company reputation.  

 

External Relationships 

  • Leads efforts to create strategic partnerships and coalitions with highly complex governmental and non-governmental thought leaders (e.g., peer and industry organizations, think tanks, academics, businesses, community leaders) to align stakeholder interests to Microsoft and optimally position them as advocates for Microsoft policy, political, and business priorities; drives strategic long-term, meaningful relationships with key political leadership and trade/think tanks and looks for opportunities to partner on public policy issues.
  • Provides thought leadership for identifying and unblocking potential regulatory issues that prevent access to market opportunities; strategically partners with the Public Sector and other key business/client leads. 

 

Internal Collaboration 

  • Designs, leads, and collaborates on cross-group projects that are of strategic importance to Microsoft, or that involve senior executive participation, to develop scalable and sustainable solutions.  
  • Leads the resolution of competing policy approaches by collaborating with Microsoft senior executives within legal and non-legal organizations (e.g., how Legal and Engineering would deal with accessibility) to ensure a coordinated approach on issues with Microsoft-wide impact or high external visibility. 
  • Collaborates with, and influences, executive-level stakeholders across the company to educate on government/regulatory requirements and policy landscape implications, guide business and product strategies, identify partnerships to grow the business and ensure alignment of objectives, priorities, and resources.

You will be a key point of contact for specialty vendors, ensuring high-quality service delivery, adherence to budget, invoicing, and compliance with Apple's policies and procedures. This role also supports corporate and on-site events, ensuring specialty surfaces are pristine ahead of each event and restored afterward, which regularly requires work before and after standard business hours.

Contributes to an inclusive environment through respecting each other’s differences and having the curiosity to learn. Foster and maintain excellent relationships with various stakeholders.
Oversee and manage all aspects of specialty surface care, including regular audits, maintenance, repair, and long-term preservation of specialty materials.
Provide direct oversight of specialty vendors performing all required maintenance and manage all aspects of implementing and delivering their services.
Manage and procure existing and new vendors.
Direct vendors to ensure they comply with Apple policies and procedures.
Support corporate and on-site events by coordinating cleaning, polishing, and restoration of specialty surfaces both ahead of and following each event, partnering with the Events team on schedules and access.

About the Role

Storage plays an essential role at Anthropic across research, development, product, and running the business. Our exabyte-scale, multi-cloud storage infrastructure underpins training, CI, sandboxing, inference, warehousing, and long-term data retention. Our storage needs are growing rapidly with Claude. To keep up, we're looking for engineers who have designed, secured, operated, scaled, governed, and optimized blob storage platforms at hyper-scale. 

 

You'll join a welcoming, collaborative, high-trust, high-velocity team that is devoted to our users and Anthropic's mission. You'll bring deep experience, essential technical guidance, user-centric product sense, and hands-on significant contributions to help us evolve Anthropic's storage capabilities while absorbing increasing volume and complexity. You'll own high-stakes architectural decisions and deliverables to make stored data securely and speedily accessible across varying infrastructures and regions. You'll collaborate closely with other orgs to drive world-class security, usability, reliability, and capacity/cost efficiency: both for the data we store, and the ways we make it accessible to power a wide range of workflows.

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE JOB

The Director of Production, Optics will own all production outcomes for Optics production for the Imaging Business Line. the production organization responsible for building and delivering precision optical assemblies for advanced defense systems. This role requires both frontline technical leadership and strong people management — you will be responsible for the team, the output, and the operational health of the optical production value stream. Success demands consistent achievement across team development, on-time delivery, quality, cost, and continuous improvement, ensuring execution of mission-critical optical products.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Production Ownership & Strategy: Own all production outcomes for the Optics Production across Imaging product lines, including ramp plans, headcount, and the standing up of new manufacturing lines. Develop and execute a long-term strategy to rapidly scale production volumes to full-rate production.
  • Leadership & Team Management: Serve as a strategic leader and tactical do-er, driving all people and resources across production to achieve outcomes. Lead cross-functional teams (including Production, Supply Chain, Quality, and Manufacturing Engineering) through strong leadership, advocacy, and a consistent on-site presence, holding them accountable to meeting demands, deadlines, and goals.
  • Operational Excellence: Drive processes and systems needed throughout the product development lifecycle to mature products to full-rate production. Establish and manage the team to key performance indicators (KPIs) for financial, quality, and on-time delivery to optimize manufacturing operations' impact on the business.
  • Own Production Operations: Oversee the production of optical product lines, managing a team of technicians and production staff to ensure efficient assembly, test, and delivery of imaging and optical hardware. Drive daily and weekly production execution across optical assembly lines and the supporting supply base, ultimately owning all production outcomes across delivery, cost, and quality targets in the Operating plan.
  • Value Stream Management: Own visibility and flow across the end-to-end value stream — from supplier material deliveries through internal optical assembly, test, and shipment. Identify bottlenecks, drive root-cause resolution, and implement process improvements to increase throughput and reduce cycle time.
  • Process & Technology Advancement: Advise on development and oversee the implementation of digital technologies, from PLM and ERP to our custom MES and QMS systems, that enable our production operations to efficiently scale while meeting customer requirements. Shape corporate tools and processes to support the unique needs of aerospace production.
  • Champion Quality & Safety: Ensure quality and safety standards are followed across clean room and optical assembly environments, minimizing defects and fostering a safe working environment.
  • Drive Continuous Improvement: Lead 5S, Lean manufacturing, and other continuous improvement initiatives to enhance efficiency, optimize workflows, and scale production capacity.
  • Strategic Communication: Provide regular updates to senior leadership on production status, risks, and resource needs. Facilitate cross-functional collaboration with engineering, supply chain, quality, and program management.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Optical Engineering or a related field.
  • 8+ years of experience in optical or complex electro-mechanical production, with 3+ years in a senior production leadership.
  • Demonstrated experience standing up, scaling and managing production of optical assemblies, precision hardware, or imaging systems — defense, aerospace, or adjacent industries strongly preferred.
  • Working knowledge of optical assembly processes, clean room manufacturing environments, and optical test and inspection methods.
  • Proven expertise with ERP, MRP, and MES systems, coupled with a strong understanding of Lean manufacturing, NPI, and change management (ECOs).
  • Ability to interpret complex technical documentation (drawings, schematics, work instructions) and troubleshoot processes and equipment.
  • Demonstrated success in employee development, coaching, and mentorship.
  • Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, highly organized, and detail-oriented.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

    • Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com. 

  • Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

  • What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

ABOUT THE JOB 

The EHS Integration Lead drives the integration of EHS into engineering, product development, manufacturing development, and other technical business processes by building cross-functional relationships, establishing scalable integration mechanisms, and translating enterprise EHS strategy into engineering execution. Where technical safety engineers determine how a specific hazard is managed, this role determines how EHS becomes embedded in the way an engineering organization already works. That means understanding engineering workflows, development processes, decision points and constraints well enough to integrate with them rather than imposing a separate EHS process alongside them.

EHS Integration Leads own defined integration domains. Depending on organizational need and individual strengths, that ownership may center on the Prevention through Design program and the design standards that carry it, or on enterprise risk management and the engineering relationships that drive its adoption. This role also provides technical and program leadership to technical safety engineers working within its domain, exercised through the program and its standards rather than through reporting lines.

Position is on-site at Costa Mesa, CA, with regular travel to manufacturing and program sites.

WHAT YOU’LL DO 

    • Engineering Relationships and Interface

      • Serve as a primary EHS Integration interface to Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Product, Program Management, Quality, Facilities and Operations, building trusted working relationships across those organizations and with EHS Operations and the EHS technical disciplines.
      • Partner with engineering teams to understand their workflows, development processes, decision points, constraints and technical needs, and integrate with them rather than introducing a separate EHS process.
      • Proactively identify opportunities where earlier EHS engagement adds value in the development lifecycle, and make that case in engineering terms.
      • Represent engineering realities, constraints and priorities back into the EHS organization so that EHS strategy remains executable.
      • Coordinate EHS technical resources onto projects requiring specialized safety engineering support, ensuring the appropriate discipline expert is engaged.

    • Prevention through Design and Design Standards

      • Drive implementation of Prevention through Design principles across product, manufacturing, equipment, facility and process development.
      • Support implementation and continued development of the EHS Design Process, including its integration with engineering phase gates and development milestones.
      • Support development, revision and consistent application of the enterprise EHS design standards, design checklists and supporting criteria.
      • Translate EHS requirements, risk information, lessons learned and regulatory obligations into usable engineering requirements and design criteria.
      • Influence manufacturing process, equipment selection and facility layout decisions to eliminate or reduce hazards before implementation, participating in design trades so that elimination options enter the decision rather than being reviewed afterward.
      • Facilitate early hazard identification and structured risk-management activities with engineering teams and EHS technical subject-matter experts, participating in selected product-development and manufacturing-development reviews until scalable ownership models are established.
      • Ensure operator task, maintenance access and human interaction are considered in design decisions, in partnership with the human factors and ergonomics function.

    • Enterprise Risk Register and Risk Assessment Process

      • Support development of the base model for the enterprise risk register, including its structure, application of the enterprise hazard taxonomy, and the data ownership and entry conventions required for risk information to aggregate consistently and remain trustworthy across programs, sites and regions.
      • Establish and document the process by which risk assessments are requested, scoped, performed, reviewed, recorded and closed, consistent with the enterprise risk assessment procedure.
      • Support risk assessment delivery across programs, manufacturing lines and facilities in partnership with EHS technical subject-matter experts and EHS Operations, contributing facilitation and consistency while technical determinations remain with the relevant discipline.
      • Drive adoption of the register across engineering, program and operations teams so that it becomes the reference source for design-phase and operational risk information.
      • Use register data to identify recurring hazard patterns and translate them into design standards, requirements and lessons learned.

    • Integration Mechanisms, Tooling and Adoption

      • Work with engineering stakeholders to define when EHS engagement is required, what information is required, who participates, and what constitutes closure.
      • Identify gaps in existing engineering workflows and develop integration strategies to close them, rather than relying on informal engagement.
      • Develop scalable processes and mechanisms that reduce dependence on individual relationships and manual EHS intervention.
      • Own the technical tooling dedicated to this domain, including analysis, modeling and design-review tooling specific to the discipline, and define its roadmap.
      • Partner with enterprise software, digital and data resources, who own enterprise platforms and software development, to integrate EHS tooling into engineering and manufacturing workflows and to specify requirements for automation, data exchange and AI-enabled capability.
      • Establish feedback loops connecting Engineering, EHS Operations, incident data, risk assessments and audit findings into future designs, and track adoption and effectiveness of Prevention through Design and EHS engineering-integration initiatives.
      • Assume ownership of a defined integration domain such as the Prevention through Design program, enterprise risk management, the Product Development Process, the Manufacturing Development Process, or engineering change, and provide technical and program leadership to technical safety engineers working within that domain.

ABOUT THE TEAM
Anduril’s Maritime Division has assembled a diverse team of experts in software, robotics, artificial intelligence, sensor fusion, and data analysis to create software and hardware solutions that radically evolve the capabilities of our customers. We are fielding the next generation of autonomous systems to tackle the extremely challenging industry demands of maritime operations. Anduril has brought to market a unique, ultra-long-range, full-ocean-depth underwater vessel platform and a completely refreshed maritime vehicle and flexible manufacturing architecture that scales from "small" to "extra-large" vehicle sizes. Today, Anduril is executing on billion-dollar contracts while simultaneously performing Robot-as-a-Service (RaaS) AUV operations.

We are continuing to expand our product portfolio, now moving into the surface maritime domain. Products like Dive-XL, Dive-LD, Copperhead, Seabed Sentry, and surface products in the pipeline will create a system-of-systems that enable a multitude of autonomous missions across all maritime domains. If you are passionate about solving problems that have real impact and working on systems that directly contribute to achieving national strategic priorities, we want you to join Anduril’s Maritime Division and help us build the future of defense capability.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are seeking a highly motivated and experienced Electrical Engineer to aid the technical development of a holistic support system for service, maintenance, deployment, launch, and recovery of the Copperhead family of vehicles. This role involves close collaboration with electrical and systems teams as well as customer representatives to ensure effective support and execution of Copperhead missions in a variety of rugged environments.

As a key member of our Quincy, MA based team, the Electrical Engineer will work closely with the program leadership and a wide spectrum of cross-departments focused on solving hard problems and changing the trajectory of the industry. This position will be responsible for designing and supporting the integration of various electrical subsystems, supporting testing efforts, and ensuring overall system performance meets the required specifications and standards.

Join our dynamic team and help us build the next generation of autonomous maritime systems!

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Design electrical interfaces and enclosures for integration of sensors, and peripheral equipment for autonomous systems
  • Troubleshoot issues that span the electrical and software boundaries, with solid skills using both test equipment (Oscilloscopes, DMM, etc.) and basic software debugging tools
  • Develop subsystems (sensors, interfaces, power management, and networking) for bespoke capabilities
  • Work closely with other electrical, mechanical, software, firmware, and test engineers to deliver fully functional products
  • Work in a fast-paced environment balancing schedule against cost and performance parameters
  • Conduct peer-level and cross-discipline design reviews, perform requirements analysis, and plan system verification to ensure compliance with project goals and industry standards

  • Knowledge of modern analog and digital electronics and electronic circuits
  • Experience developing schematics, interconnect diagrams, and wiring harnesses
  • Competence with test equipment such as multi-meter, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and automation of tests
  • Experience with electro-mechanical and electrical design concepts
  • Experience in fieldable system design
  • High-ownership and a bias toward action – if you see a problem, you want to solve and fix it
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance
  • Ability to travel 5%

  • Experience with high reliability and/or autonomous systems
  • Familiarity with designing for rugged environments

  • Design and source PCB Assemblies with varying complexity - from FPGA based data acquisition boards, to MCU platform data interfaces, breakout boards, wiring harnesses, or peripheral modules.
  • Architect and source circuit board test fixtures, integrating your designs with internally developed and off-the-shelf data acquisition equipment.
  • Build internal library for test circuit for data acquisition, leverage your expertise for DFM / DFT.
  • Bring up, Debug, and Characterize circuits, low speed interfaces (I2C, SPI, CAN, etc.) and high speed signals (RF, memory, USB).

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical/Electronics, Computer, Mechanical Engineering, or related fields OR 6+ years of advanced knowledge acquired through work experience and/or intellectual instruction in lieu of degree.
  • 4+ years of relevant industry experience with emphasis on product designs that have gone to manufacturing.
  • Experience with Professional Electronics Design packages (Altium, Cadence, PADs, etc.) for schematic capture and layout.
  • Expertise in PCBA Design. Ability to design and fabricate your own designs, or guide contract manufacturing resources.
  • Familiarity with electronics test equipment such as power supplies, electronic loads, oscilloscope, function generators, spectrum analyzers, data acquisition and measurement sensors.
  • Familiar with Product Life Cycle (PLM) systems and releasing designs for production.
  • Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

  • Experience with scripting tools Python for configuration and automation of setup tasks.
  • Familiarity with FPGA PCBA platforms - RTL, design synthesis, and bare-metal coding.

Anduril's Maritime Division is transforming American sea power to meet the defining national security challenges of our era and secure our future of maritime dominance.

Arsenal-2 is purpose-built to break long-standing industrial bottlenecks and scale production of critical components for the Navy's Virginia-class attack submarines to support fleet requirements. At the same time, it will build the industrial muscle to field our next-generation AUVs at scale.

We aren't waiting for the new shipyard to be completed. In Anduril's Maritime Division, we are actively building America's next decisive advantage at sea—and this is the moment to join us.

ABOUT THE JOB

  • Design external charging interfaces and solutions for rapid turnaround
  • Manage energy budget and power allocation across all consuming subsystems
  • Define electrical interfaces between energy subsystem and other vehicle systems
  • Manage subsystem schedule and cost performance across prototype, LRIP, and FRP phases
  • Provide technical mentorship to engineers across energy disciplines
  • Drive design-for-manufacturability in coordination with Production

About the Team

The Imaging team builds and fields state-of-the-art camera and sensor systems deployed to solve real security challenges for the United States and its allies. We work across the full stack, from bare-metal hardware and firmware to networked services and cloud integrations, and we own our systems all the way through to the field. When something breaks in a deployed environment, we fix it.

About the Role

We're looking for a Site Reliability Engineer to join the Imaging team. This is not a product development role, and it isn't a traditional cloud-SRE role either. You are the frontline for keeping fielded imaging systems alive: the person field personnel and customer-support escalations turn to when a deployed system isn't behaving. You'll be the second SRE on a small, high-trust team, working directly with our lead, with real room to shape how Imaging reliability and support operate as we scale.

The work is varied and often ambiguous. You might spend a morning triaging a networking failure on a system being stood up at a remote site, an afternoon walking a field operator through a sensor calibration over the phone, and the back half of a week hardening a runbook so the next person never has to solve that problem live again. When a fielded system misbehaves, the root cause could be anywhere in the stack--and you're the one who narrows it down.

If you get energy from diagnosing live systems under pressure, being the reason a deployment stays up, and turning recurring fire-drills into durable fixes, this role is built for you.

What You'll Do

Own fielded system reliability. You are responsible for the health and uptime of deployed imaging systems. When issues arise--whether the root cause is in the network, the calibration, an upgrade, or the sensor hardware itself--you triage, diagnose, and drive resolution.

Run point on escalations. You'll be first and second line of response for issues coming through our support channels and Anduril's customer-support pipeline (Tier 0 to Mission Success / Product Operations to SRE), acting as the deep-expertise backstop the rest of the funnel escalates to.

Turn fires into runbooks. Recurring issues shouldn't be solved live twice. You'll build and maintain runbooks, diagnostics, and self-service tooling that reduce repeat problems and shrink the support load over time.

Hold the boundary with engineering. You own everything short of a code fix. When an issue turns out to be a genuine software defect, you'll cleanly reproduce it, document it, and hand it off to the Mission Software Engineers--protecting their focus by keeping frontline support where it belongs.

Feed reliability back into the product. You'll turn what you learn in the field into signals that make our systems more supportable--better observability, safer upgrades, more graceful failure.

Travel expected approximately 20% of the time for field support and deployment windows.

What We're Looking For

Required

  • 3+ years in SRE, DevOps, field/systems engineering, or production support of deployed hardware/software systems--with real ownership after systems ship, not just standing them up
  • Strong Linux fundamentals, including comfort troubleshooting real networking issues (IP, routing, VPNs, connectivity in constrained or field environments)
  • Demonstrated ability to diagnose and resolve issues across system boundaries (networking, services, hardware interaction) without always having full visibility into every component
  • Comfortable owning a structured on-call rotation, including scheduled after-hours and weekend coverage
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to run a remote troubleshooting session with a non-technical operator and document what happened
  • Eligibility to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret clearance

Preferred

  • Experience supporting fielded or deployed systems, not just development environments
  • Experience with fielded hardware or sensor systems (EO/IR, optical, or similar), including familiarity with sensor calibration
  • Scripting for diagnostics and automation (Python, Bash, or similar)
  • Familiarity with Nix or NixOS--uncommon, but valuable on our stack
  • Familiarity with systemd service management and observability practices on Linux
  • Familiarity with incident tooling (PagerDuty or equivalent)

What Makes Someone Successful Here

The people who thrive in this role share a few traits that don't always show up on a resume:

They close loops. When they pick up a problem they own it until it's resolved, not until it's someone else's problem.

They stay calm under pressure. A system down in the field with an operator waiting is a high-stress moment. They work the problem methodically instead of reacting.

They communicate proactively. They don't wait to be asked for a status update. They document what they find, share what they learn, and keep the people who need to know informed.

They're comfortable with ambiguity at the stack boundary. When a device behaves unexpectedly in the field, the root cause could be anywhere. They have a methodology for narrowing it down systematically rather than guessing or waiting for someone else to have the answer.

They know where the line is. They own frontline support fully, and they know when an issue is a true code-level defect that belongs with engineering--handing it off cleanly rather than either sitting on it or tossing it over the wall half-formed.

ABOUT THE JOB

The Deployment Handling engineer owns ground handling procedures and equipment for autonomous maritime vehicle movement at deployment sites. You will design handling fixtures, select and specify ground support equipment, develop handling procedures, and ensure vehicles are moved safely between transport, storage, and water. You will own launch and recovery for maritime autonomous vehicles. Reporting to the Deployment Lead, you will design assist with designing L&R systems, define host vessel interfaces, and develop operational procedures that enable safe deployment and retrieval at sea across a range of conditions.

Your spectrum of support will be diverse in nature and require you to leverage your technical expertise as well as leadership skills to set objectives, build cross-functional teams, and rapidly drive to completion. The ability to leverage your intuition and prior experience will be key in making sure the right design, analysis, and test steps are completed to ensure success. The ideal candidate will leverage their experience executing and successfully completing prior highly optimized multi-disciplinary projects.

  • Willingness to travel up to 50%, including extended deployments.

ABOUT THE TEAM
Our IT Asset Management (ITAM) team is the backbone of our corporate technology operations. We manage the full lifecycle of every endpoint asset, from receiving in our facility to secure, eco-friendly disposal. We combine software automation, precise inventory auditing, and streamlined physical logistics so our workforce always has the tools it needs. We are a collaborative, detail-oriented group that connects high-level vendor compliance with hands-on, day-to-day technical support. On our team, you will play a critical role in keeping our global IT endpoint devices organized, cost-effective, and ready to scale.

ABOUT THE JOB
We are seeking an IT Asset Management Technician I to primarily support our offboarding and asset recovery program. You will own the day-to-day returns workflow for departing employees, contractors, and interns: making sure every device is recovered, verified, secured, and returned to service quickly. You will also support IT audit assessments that keep our asset records accurate. When the team needs extra hands, you will help with inventory and deployments. You will work closely with our Asset Administrator, People Business Partners, managers, and regional IT teams.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Offboarding & Returns

  • Departure Coordination: Manage offboarding cases from start to finish. Confirm each leaver's assigned devices, set the return method and location, and keep stakeholders updated until every device is back.
  • Return Logistics: Issue return shipping labels and QR codes, arrange return boxes, track shipments, and follow up on unreturned devices according to our escalation timelines.
  • Receiving & Verification: Receive returned devices, verify serial numbers against the asset record, and update the asset management system the same day.
  • Data & Device Security: Follow data-preservation and legal-hold procedures, including device imaging when required, before devices are wiped, released, and returned to inventory.
  • Return Tracking: Keep the return tracker current on a regular cadence, close out completed cases, and report outstanding devices and trends.
  • Volume Surges: Support high-volume events, such as intern cohort departures and refresh programs, with clear organization and steady follow-through.

Auditing

  • Record Accuracy: Run recurring audits to confirm the assigned user, owner, and location of each device are correct in our asset management system, and cross-check against other data sources.
  • Discrepancy Investigation: Investigate mismatches, such as unreturned devices, users with more than one computer that goes unused, and shared or service devices without a named owner. Resolve each one or escalate it.
  • User Verification: Support user device confirmations and document results so they are ready for compliance reviews.

Inventory & Deployment Support (as needed)

  • Physical Logistics: Move, stock, and deploy inventory (must be able to lift up to 50 lbs). This includes moving pallets, breaking down boxes, and stocking shelves.
  • Device Maintenance: Physically clean and wipe returned assets, and partner with cross-functional teams on repairs and RMA (Return Merchandise Authorization) processes so devices are ready to redeploy.
  • Workspace Setup: Set up desks, monitors, and peripherals for new hires and team moves when needed.
  • Support Ticket Resolution: Handle offboarding and returns tickets in Jira and walk-up requests, and provide deskside support as needed.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Soft Skills: Eager, motivated, collaborative, reliable, and highly customer-focused, with professional, tactful communication when working with departing team members and their managers.
  • Organization & Follow-Through: Able to manage many open cases at once, track deadlines, and follow up consistently until each case is closed.
  • Attention to Detail: This role focuses heavily on verifying serial numbers and matching records, so strong attention to detail is essential.
  • Inventory Control: Experience maintaining accurate inventory counts and asset records.
  • Discretion: Comfortable handling sensitive situations and data, including involuntary separations and legal holds, with confidentiality.
  • Physical Capability: Comfortable with physical labor, standing or walking for most of the day, and lifting heavy items (50 lbs+).
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain a US Secret Security Clearance.

As the Manager, Supply Chain, you will serve as a hands-on operational partner to the Head of Production in Quonset, driving planning, procurement oversight, and materials management for Anduril's Maritime Undersea Dominance product line. This is a lead-level role that blends individual contributor execution with team oversight. You will own the daily operational cadence, keeping production on track through master scheduling, demand planning, procurement triage, and warehouse coordination. The right person for this role is a strong planner first who can also step into procurement and materials work when needed, thrives in a fast-paced environment, and brings the kind of no-task-too-small mentality it takes to build and sustain a high-performing supply chain operation.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own production planning and material planning for the Quonset site, serving as the central point of accountability for master scheduling and demand/supply planning.
  • Drive the day-to-day tactical planning rhythm, ensuring production has clear visibility into what is coming, what is needed, and when.
  • Maintain accuracy across digital systems (Oracle on the supply side, Forge/Foundry on the production side), including rev rec verification and ensuring system data reflects reality on the floor.
  • Partner directly with the Head of Production on daily battle rhythm, report-outs, and operational cadence to keep the site running smoothly.
  • Identify planning gaps and build toward a scalable planning function over time, including informing future hiring needs such as a dedicated master scheduler.
  • Provide oversight and monitoring of PO status across the procurement team, catching items that fall through the cracks and directing the team to triage effectively.
  • Own visibility into supplier delivery performance, including on-time shipment tracking, inventory health, and escalation of shortages to Production Support Engineers (PSEs).
  • Handle boots-on-the-ground procurement needs as they arise, including facilities-related purchases, COTS items, and miscellaneous material requirements that pop up outside standard production procurement flows.
  • Provide light oversight and mentoring for materials and warehouse operations at the Quonset site.
  • Serve as the connective tissue between operations teams, ensuring alignment on inventory management, material flow, and warehouse priorities.
  • Understand and work within Anduril's 3Si (Shared Site Services) model as it relates to planning and warehousing functions.
  • Facilitate rather than direct, this pillar is about ensuring coordination and removing blockers rather than day-to-day IC execution.
  • Serve as a key stakeholder and operational partner to the Head of Production, providing daily visibility into supply chain health and contributing to site-level decision making.
  • Work closely with Anduril's Accounting, Finance, and Legal teams to ensure timely supplier payment, contracting, and financing.
  • Collaborate with Anduril's broader US-based Supply Chain organization to leverage existing processes, best practices, and strategies.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 5+ years of experience in supply chain with a strong emphasis on production planning, material planning, or master scheduling within a manufacturing environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage demand and supply planning processes and keep production teams informed and unblocked.
  • Hands-on experience with ERP/MRP systems; familiarity with Oracle is a plus.
  • Working knowledge of procurement processes, supplier management, and inventory management.
  • Comfort operating as both a lead-level individual contributor and a people leader, with the ability to mentor and oversee small teams.
  • Strong cross-functional communication skills with the ability to partner effectively with production, engineering, and finance stakeholders.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, unstructured environment where priorities shift quickly. Startup or high-growth experience preferred.
  • Positive attitude, bias for action, and a no-task-too-small mentality.
  • Bachelor's degree preferred, not required.
  • Must be able to obtain and maintain a US Security Clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Experience in a technically complex industry such as aerospace, defense, automotive, or consumer electronics.
  • Prior experience standing up or scaling supply chain operations in a growing organization.
  • Experience with AS9100D guidelines.
  • Familiarity with shared services or multi-site supply chain operating models.
  • Track record of building operational cadences, KPIs, and reporting rhythms from the ground up.
