We are looking for an Electrical Engineer to join our rapidly growing team in Irvine, CA. This role will own rapidly developed, ruggedized electronics design in addition to scaling legacy design concepts to support full-rate production. In this role, you will partner with our Architecture and Product Management team to help drive system requirements prior to owning full PCB and/or electrical system design. This will require identifying high risk areas, creating and validating electronics designs for embedded compute and/or power systems, and testing for long term-reliability while considering manufacturability and testability in the design.

If you are someone who enjoys designing mission-critical electrical circuit cards and integrated systems with the freedom to drive product development from often undefined requirements then this role is for you.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Take ownership as the main point of contact for electrical integration activities.
  • Provide hands on and in-field support of prototype and production level product.
  • Collaborate with mechanical engineers to optimize selection, design and integration of high power components, modules and distribution.
  • Trade-off component and module selections against size, weight, power and EMC requirements.
  • Collaborate with design team to achieve reliability goals at a system level in context of concepts of operation.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Minimum 3+ years of professional experience
  • Self starter with the ability to design digital & analog electronics from concept and functional prototype, to production ready product.
  • Ability to troubleshoot existing hardware to find root cause of issues and implement improvements to improve the design.
  • Develop clear documentation to capture design requirements, specifications, test coverage, and test reports.
  • Complete full cycle PCB design including collecting requirements, schematic design, component selection, completion of layout, bring-up, test, debug, validation, characterization, and integration with the system.
  • Work closely with other mechanical, software, firmware, and test engineers to deliver fully functional products.
  • Work in a fast-paced environment supporting new developments, active deployments, and customer operated hardware.
  • Concurrently manage involvement in multiple projects at various stages.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical Engineering or equivalent
  • 3+ years of experience designing, testing and troubleshooting complex board designs and products.
  • Competence with test equipment such as oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, thermal chambers, current-probes, and automation of tests.
  • Familiarity with switch mode power supply design and testing.
  • Familiarity with standard interfaces such as Ethernet, CAN, I2C, SPI, PCIe, USB, etc.
  • Familiarity with common MCU, CPU, FPGA devices and technologies.
  • Knowledge of modern analog and digital electronics and electronic circuits.
  • Exceptional organization and communication skills (both written and oral).
  • Proficient with Altium Designer or equivalent electronic design automation design tools.
  • Proficiency with scripting languages (Python, Matlab, etc.)
  • Ability to root cause Full stack HLOS application to hardware component level issues.

ABOUT THE JOB

This position involves working in a multi-disciplinary environment on the design, fabrication and flight testing of advanced payloads for Space. We are interested in candidates that are excited to work on new projects from conceptualization through production.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Work with EE Manager and Systems Engineer to develop requirements
  • Create a Block Diagram of the proposed design
  • Make a Schematic for the design in Altium
  • Simulation of the circuit design
  • Perform Layout or work with a Layout Engineer to design the PCB
  • Generate Drawings and Documentation for the design
  • Perform Design Validation Testing (DVT) on the finished PCBA
  • Support testing and test development
  • Debug support

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 5+ years of relevant experience
  • B.S. in Electrical or Computer Engineering or equivalent
  • Team player with strong organization and communication skills
  • Experience with schematic design
  • Experience performing board bring-up
  • Experience performing schematic reviews
  • Ability to work independently under tight deadlines with minimal supervision, delivering quality results in fast-paced environments.
  • Experience developing checklists and procedures for developed designs
  • Experience developing technical drawings and documentation
  • Experience with power circuit design and implementation
  • Familiarity with lab equipment (DMM, O-Scope, Power Supply, etc)

  • Schematic and layout design in Altium
  • Experience performing PDN analysis

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

About the Team

Anduril develops advanced robotic systems that operate at the edge across land, sea, and air. Our team builds the critical systems powering everything from Group 1–3 autonomous aerial systems (such as Ghost, Anvil, Bolt, and Altius) to autonomous Sentry Towers that safeguard borders and critical infrastructure with real-time sensor fusion.
Underpinning these diverse robotic fleets is our DeviceOS team, which engineers the unified, highly reliable operating system and hardware-enablement platform that powers all of Anduril's autonomous assets. We take systems from initial schematics and paper sketches to hardened, field-ready robotics deployed in the most challenging operational environments on Earth.

About the Job

Underneath our airframes and Sentry Towers are custom carrier boards, embedded ARM architectures, and NVIDIA Jetson modules integrated with an intense array of hardware: electro-optical/infrared cameras, radars, CAN-connected sensor nodes, GPS, flight controllers, radios, and high-power motor drivers.
Between the silicon vendor’s raw Board Support Package (BSP) and our autonomous mission software sits a layer that must be owned deliberately: the boot chain, device trees, kernel drivers, and the guarantee that every piece of hardware deterministically enumerates and operates when our image boots.
In this role, you will own the boundary where custom hardware meets software. You will customize vendor BSPs and evaluate upstream changes. You will debug boot end-to-end—from firmware (EDK2/U-Boot) through unified kernel images to an encrypted root filesystem running at the tactical edge. You are the engineer who can read a schematic to diagnose a bus fault, remediate a kernel CVE on deployed hardware, and write the platform drivers that keep our robots flying and monitoring.
In this role, you will maintain and support a large deployed fleet by writing fixes for existing hardware and boot chains. This work is critical to our operations: a firmware regression is not just a failing test, it is a physical unit someone has to service in the field.

What You’ll Do

  • Own the Boot Path: Own the boot sequence end-to-end on deployed compute: low-level firmware, U-Boot/UEFI, unified kernel images, initrd, encrypted storage unlock, and handoff to a running NixOS environment. Debug boot failures on hardware via remote support.
  • Customize & Sustain Vendor BSPs: Reconcile vendor BSPs (Tegra/Jetson Linux, NXP, etc.) with modern NixOS package sets. Produce kernel and device tree patches when hardware requires custom behavior, and forward-port these changes across OS baseline upgrades.
  • Guarantee Deterministic Hardware Availability: Ensure all peripherals—cameras, radars, motor controllers, CAN networks, and radios—are reliably enumerated, correctly named, and fully operational across boots and platform upgrades.
  • Sustain a Long-Lived Baseline: Keep the existing signed boot chain and disk encryption working as the firmware, kernels, and package sets change underneath them. Triage and remediate CVEs in vendor kernels and low-level system components on our systems already deployed in the field.
  • Automate & Validate: Build and maintain automated Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) test suites to catch regressions in power states, bus communication, and platform stability before code hits flight or field hardware.
  • Perform Deep Hardware/Software Root-Cause Analysis: Diagnose intermittent bus errors, thermal and power throttling issues, kernel panics, and boot hangs using serial consoles, logic analyzers, dmesg, and hardware schematics.
  • Be the Upstream: Triage upstream kernel and vendor BSP issues, produce the patch when no upstream fix is coming, and carry that patch set forward as the platform moves.

Required Qualifications

  • 4+ years of professional embedded Linux platform, sustainment of deployed embedded Linux platforms, or kernel-adjacent integration experience.
  • Deep understanding of the embedded Linux boot chain: firmware/bootloaders (U-Boot, EDK2), device trees, kernel command line, initrd/initramfs, and root filesystem assembly.
  • Strong programming skills in C (for kernel/driver development and BSP patching) along with proficiency in Rust or C++ for userspace platform integration and services.
  • Hands-on experience debugging hardware at the bench: using serial consoles, reading schematics and component datasheets, and tracing issues to the board level.
  • Experience maintaining software deployed on real-world hardware, where updates must be safe, resilient to bricking, and strictly validated against regressions.
  • U.S. Person status is required due to export control regulations (ITAR/EAR), with eligibility to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Nix / NixOS Experience: Direct experience with declarative systems (Nix/NixOS) for embedded builds; or deep expertise in Yocto/Buildroot paired with an appetite to transition to modern, reproducible paradigms.
  • NVIDIA Jetson / Tegra Depth: Hands-on experience with JetPack, Jetson Linux BSP, Tegra boot architecture, or CUDA compute runtime integration.
  • Low-Level Platform Security: Practical implementation of hardware root-of-trust, secure boot, HAB/AHAB, or measured boot (TPM).
  • Automated HIL Testing: Experience architecting automated test benches using Python or Bash to validate embedded Linux builds against physical test targets.
  • Familiarity with functional programming paradigms (e.g., Nix, Haskell).
  • Upstream open-source contributions to the Linux kernel, U-Boot, or system-level open-source projects.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for a Manufacturing Test Technician to join our growing team in Quonset, RI. In this role, you will work on cutting-edge technology aimed at advancing the state-of-the-possible in subsea robotics. You will play a key role in delivering our AUVs to our customers by working hands-on with our engineering team on a multi-disciplinary environment to scale our AUV production globally. This role will be testing complex electromechanical assemblies and integrating them into the final product!

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Work within a team of multidisciplinary engineers and operations team on pressure vessel assembly and test as part overall AUV production integration
  • Perform configuration tasks to flash/load correct SW/FW versions onto devices.
  • Build, test, and integrate complex electrical and mechanical assemblies into our world class AUVs
  • Execute on detailed sub-system End-of-Line (EOL) tests from prepared procedures
  • Perform incoming quality inspection testing on PCBA’s
  • Proficient at troubleshooting and repair of electrical, electronics and integrated circuits to the component level.
  • Help develop, document, and improve the pressure vessel production process
  • 5S work areas, perform part inspections, close out work order, and follow safety best practices
  • Support management of tools, equipment, and lab supplies (maintenance, calibrations, raw material stock)
  • Potential of traveling offshore to support our operations team

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Solid background in electronics working in relevant fields (Robotics, Defense, Avionics)
  • Experience in preparing and executing test procedures with high levels of attention to detail
  • Familiarity with electrical engineering principles and concepts

  • Commitment to a high-quality product and strong sense of personal accountability
  • Familiarity with basic electrical test equipment such as DMMs, oscilloscopes, function generators, etc.
  • Extremely organized and detail-oriented
  • Excellent verbal & written communication skills
  • Has a never-ending sense of urgency and enthusiasm
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience in sub-sea robotics (AUVs, UUVs, underwater equipment)

  • Experience with low volume / high mix manufacturing

ABOUT THE JOB

We are seeking a Field Test Engineer to join the Quincy based team at Anduril, where you’ll work in a cutting-edge start-up environment to advance the state-of-the-possible in subsea robotics. In this role, you will be at the water's edge and on the deck plate - planning, executing, and analyzing at-sea test events for autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) and subsea systems. You will serve as the critical link between engineering and the real-world ocean environment, turning design intent into validated hardware and software performance. This is a hands-on position for someone who thrives on solving hard problems in the field, often far from the lab and under demanding austere operational conditions.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Work within a dynamic team of multidisciplinary engineers and specialists throughout the life of AUV design, integration, and test efforts
  • Take on the principal responsibilities of the hands-on troubleshooting, repair, operation, and maintenance of AUVs and subsea systems in the field
  • Lead day-to-day local operations for multiple AUVs and subsea platforms, including conducting pre-mission testing, launch and recovery, vehicle tasking, and data analysis
  • Deploy globally in support of maritime operations from a variety of support vessel types
  • Write, review, and execute test plans during sea testing
  • Coordinate test execution with 3rd party vendors, partners, and logistics companies
  • Author detailed daily operational test reports to document the step-by-step execution of internal and customer facing efforts to test and evaluate Anduril maritime platforms and new capabilities
  • Support software UI design feedback for maritime systems

  • Contribute to routine design reviews of the platform under test with an eye towards improving operability and reducing learning curve for at-sea operations
  • Contribute to next-generation designs and features for maritime products, from identifying areas for improvement to leading test and evaluation efforts for new technology rollouts
  • Participate in day-to-day offshore test operations including supporting multiple nearshore sea test days per week
  • Travel and support customer facing operations approximately 50% of the time (domestic and international)

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 5+ years experience operating robotic systems at-sea in a commercial or research offshore environment
  • Ability to adapt quickly and learn in a fast-paced and dynamic work environment
  • Experience with leading on deck operations utilizing ship based crane, a-frame, or dedicated launch and recovery systems
  • Experience deploying and recovering subsea equipment at sea
  • Experience with Linux and command line interfaces as well as software debugging
  • Knowledge of electronics troubleshooting and basic use of test equipment
  • Experience with Microsoft Excel
  • Extremely organized and detail-oriented
  • Demonstrated experience with subsea operational procedures and equipment
  • Excellent communication and customer support skills
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs
  • Ability to deploy up to 50% of the time
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Top Secret Security Clearance

  • Experience with software development
  • Experience integrating subsea acoustic sensors, underwater navigation, and communication systems
  • Proficient in reading and understanding engineering drawings and specifications
  • Knowledge of offshore HSE policies and best practices

We are seeking a Field Test Engineer to join the Quincy based team at Anduril, where you’ll work in a cutting-edge start-up environment to advance the state-of-the-possible in subsea robotics.   • Travel and support customer facing operations approximately 50% of the time (domestic and international)

  • Experience with Microsoft Excel
  • Extremely organized and detail-oriented
  • Demonstrated experience with subsea operational procedures and equipment

Anduril's Maritime Dominance division builds advanced autonomous undersea vehicle systems designed to deter, compel, and defeat adversaries at scale. Our portfolio — including platforms like Dive-LD and Copperhead — spans high-performance multi-mission undersea vehicles purpose-built for contested environments and hyper-scale production. The Maritime Finance team provides the financial infrastructure to support programs as they scale from rapid development through production ramp, partnering with engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, and program leadership to maintain cost visibility and financial rigor across a fast-growing portfolio.

ABOUT THE JOB

As a Financial Analyst, you will provide dedicated finance support to the Undersea Reconnaissance & Strike Business Line within the Maritime Division. This portfolio spans cutting-edge AUV programs that are rapidly scaling from development into production. Your primary focus will be tracking and forecasting the cost build-up of hardware programs — understanding how material, labor, and overhead flow through each stage of the product lifecycle and translating that into reliable baselines, forecasts, and variance analysis.

You will work closely with Program Managers, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, and Accounting to ensure cost visibility keeps pace with program execution. This role requires someone who can operate autonomously, drive projects from inception to completion, and communicate financial performance clearly to cross-functional stakeholders.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own program-level cost forecasting and EAC/ETC development for hardware programs transitioning from development to production
  • Build and maintain bottoms-up cost models that capture material, labor, overhead, and subcontract elements across the hardware build cycle
  • Track actuals against baselines, identify variances, and drive root-cause analysis with program teams
  • Support the development and improvement of forecasting workflows in FP&A and ERP tools (Oracle, Hyperion EPM, Foundry)
  • Contribute to long-range planning and production rate ramp financial modeling
    Drive continuous improvement in reporting accuracy, data integrity, and process efficiency

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 1-3 years of experience in FP&A, program finance, or cost analysis — preferably in an environment that manufactures or integrates hardware
  • Bachelor's degree or higher in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or related field
    Ability to operate independently in a fast-paced, high-growth environment and carry projects forward with minimal direction
  • Excellent communication skills — comfortable presenting financial narratives and variance explanations to non-finance stakeholders
  • Must be authorized to work in the United States

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • DoD industry experience or familiarity with government contract cost accounting (FAR/CAS)
  • Security clearance (or ability to obtain one)
  • Exposure to supply chain or manufacturing finance
  • Experience building or managing cost models for physical products (BOM-based costing, production cost build-ups, or similar)
  • Strong understanding of how material, labor, and indirect costs flow through a manufacturing or defense program lifecycle
  • Proficiency with financial systems and data tools; experience with ERP platforms (Oracle preferred) is a plus

ABOUT THE JOB

As a Firmware Engineer on the Manufacturing Test team you will develop new platforms to interact with our products at the lowest levels (I2C, SPI, CAN, UART, USB, etc). You will work within an interdisciplinary product development team, delivering a streamlined solution for test execution and automation. Your code will ensure that we are consistently shipping the highest quality products to our customers. You will build features targeted at embedded Linux, NIX, and several RTOS platforms. You will debug and solve complex data acquisition challenges in analog and digital realms. In this role you’ll need to think creatively and come up with solutions to solve difficult testing problems and push to continuously improve our methods of automation, throughput, user interfaces, and data analytics. 

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Build things that test things. Utilize your expertise in firmware/software development to anticipate failure modes and build code for host/client verification of form, fit, function.
  • Develop low-level firmware/software for microcontroller platforms interfacing to robots, or control algorithms for OTS Data acquisition tools.
  • Build capability for device side validation of system-level features, utilizing SSH, gRPC, while creating or leveraging existing debug tools.
  • Quickly debug and troubleshoot issues that span the electrical, firmware, and software boundaries, and transfer that process to automated test and failure analysis SOPs for production line staff.
  • Engage in DFT/DFM reviews with electrical engineering and product firmware teams.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • BS or MS in CS/CE/EE or equivalent industry experience
  • 5 years of professional industry experience 
  • Strong C coding ability for embedded systems
  • Experience integrating microcontrollers with analog and digital sensors
  • Experience developing firmware in bare-metal, RTOS environments, and embedded Linux
  • Solid understanding and application of coding best practices, board bring up and debugging
  • Some familiarity with common bus protocols such as USB, SPI, I2C, CAN, RS232, RS485, Ethernet, etc.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance 
    •  

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 8 years of professional industry experience 
  • Bring up and Debug expertise for new designs, comfortable with low and high-speed interfaces
  • Strong fundamentals for data acquisition and analysis (FFT, Bode, control loops)
  • Experience with one or more microcontroller cores (ARM, AVR, MSP430, PIC, etc.)
  • Experience with embedded Linux development and deployment process
  • Debugging skills with JTAG, SWD, Oscilloscopes, and Logic analyzers
  • Have a bias for action. If you see a problem, you want to solve and fix it
  • Be naturally curious about the technologies and tools you use

ABOUT THE JOB

As a Firmware Engineer on the Manufacturing Test team you will develop new platforms to interact with our products at the lowest levels (I2C, SPI, CAN, UART, USB, etc). You will work within an interdisciplinary product development team, delivering a streamlined solution for test execution and automation. Your code will ensure that we are consistently shipping the highest quality products to our customers. You will build features targeted at embedded Linux, NIX, and several RTOS platforms. You will debug and solve complex data acquisition challenges in analog and digital realms. In this role you’ll need to think creatively and come up with solutions to solve difficult testing problems and push to continuously improve our methods of automation, throughput, user interfaces, and data analytics. 

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Build things that test things. Utilize your expertise in firmware/software development to anticipate failure modes and build code for host/client verification of form, fit, function.
  • Develop low-level firmware/software for microcontroller platforms interfacing to robots, or control algorithms for OTS Data acquisition tools.
  • Build capability for device side validation of system-level features, utilizing SSH, gRPC, while creating or leveraging existing debug tools.
  • Quickly debug and troubleshoot issues that span the electrical, firmware, and software boundaries, and transfer that process to automated test and failure analysis SOPs for production line staff.
  • Engage in DFT/DFM reviews with electrical engineering and product firmware teams.

  • BS or MS in CS/CE/EE or equivalent industry experience
  • 5 years of professional industry experience 
  • Strong C coding ability for embedded systems
  • Experience integrating microcontrollers with analog and digital sensors
  • Experience developing firmware in bare-metal, RTOS environments, and embedded Linux
  • Solid understanding and application of coding best practices, board bring up and debugging
  • Some familiarity with common bus protocols such as USB, SPI, I2C, CAN, RS232, RS485, Ethernet, etc.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance 

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 8 years of professional industry experience 
  • Bring up and Debug expertise for new designs, comfortable with low and high-speed interfaces
  • Strong fundamentals for data acquisition and analysis (FFT, Bode, control loops)
  • Experience with one or more microcontroller cores (ARM, AVR, MSP430, PIC, etc.)
  • Experience with embedded Linux development and deployment process
  • Debugging skills with JTAG, SWD, Oscilloscopes, and Logic analyzers
  • Have a bias for action. If you see a problem, you want to solve and fix it
  • Be naturally curious about the technologies and tools you use

As a Mission Autonomy Flight Test Engineer at Anduril Industries, you will play a critical role in shaping the future of defense technology. Your focus on autonomy will empower users to execute multifaceted missions with precision and efficiency. Join us in our mission to transform military capabilities with your expertise in testing and autonomy.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Drive the advancement of Anduril's testing methodologies, with a focus on mission autonomy systems, to ensure robust and reliable performance in complex operational scenarios.
  • Design and implement test plans that challenge and verify the capabilities of autonomous systems in a variety of simulated mission profiles.
  • Analyze data from tests to validate system performance and identify areas for improvement, iterating rapidly to refine autonomy algorithms and behaviors.
  • Work collaboratively with cross-functional teams, including software engineers, hardware engineers, and product managers, to define test requirements and ensure alignment with system capabilities and mission objectives.
  • Drive end-to-end test management by shaping program requirements, designing comprehensive test plans, leading execution efforts, analyzing complex data, and delivering clear, concise reports to cross-functional and program teams.
  • Execute and analyze simulations that replicate real-world scenarios for autonomous systems to accelerate testing cycles, optimize system performance, and inform stakeholders on development and deployment implications.
  • Coordinate with private and government test ranges to test and evaluate systems and software

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • A Bachelor's degree in engineering, computer science, robotics, or a related technical field from an accredited institution, or equivalent experience in autonomous systems testing.
  • Minimum of 3 years of experience in flight testing, with a strong emphasis on autonomous or remotely piloted systems.
  • Demonstrated ability in developing and executing test plans for complex systems within aggressive timelines.
  • Familiarity with the principles of mission autonomy, unmanned systems, and the integration of multiple assets into cohesive operational frameworks.
  • Strong analytical skills, with the ability to interpret test data, diagnose system behaviors, and recommend actionable improvements.
  • Proven track record of working collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams to achieve project milestones and deliverables.
  • Excellent communication skills, capable of effectively articulating technical challenges and solutions to a diverse audience.
  • Willingness to work flexible hours and travel to various testing locations as required.
  • Must be able to obtain and maintain a U.S. Top Secret-Level security clearance.
  • In this role, you will be subject to pre-employment and randomized substance screening, as required by the Company.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Direct experience in the development, testing, and deployment of mission autonomy systems in a defense or aerospace context.
  • Hands-on experience with simulation environments and tools used for testing autonomous systems.
  • Familiarity with software development practices and experience with programming languages used in autonomy and robotics (e.g., Python, C++, ROS).
  • Knowledge of current industry and military standards related to unmanned aerial systems and their operation within national airspace.

ABOUT THE JOB

We’re looking for a Head of Corporate Finance to build and lead the financial planning engine behind one of the fastest-scaling defense companies in history. This person will own Corporate FP&A and the operating rhythms that connect Anduril’s financial model to its strategic priorities. You’ll sit at the intersection of the corporate finance team, the division finance teams, and the C-suite — translating details from across the company into a clear narrative and ensuring leadership has the right financial data and analysis to make good decisions.

This is an operating and decision-making role, not just a slide-making one. You’ll own the company’s financial operating plan and forecasting, the analysis behind the decisions that shape it, and the executive-level reporting that goes to the leadership team, the Board, and investors. You’ll influence decisions around how the company deploys capital, including which programs and R&D initiatives to pursue and how much production capacity to build. You’ll inherit a fast-growing function with a lean, capable team and a mandate to evolve Anduril’s Corporate Finance function into a best-in-class organization without slowing the business down.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own Anduril’s financial model, including the annual operating plan and the forecast rhythm across every business unit and functional organization.
  • Partner closely with Anduril’s CFO and senior finance leadership on major strategic and tactical decisions.
  • Hire, lead, and develop a team of FP&A and business-partner finance professionals across corporate and the business units.
  • Turn the plan into headcount, capital, and cash targets that leaders can manage against, and hold the organization accountable to them.
  • Collaborate with Production Finance on capacity decisions, including facility build-outs, tooling, automation, long-lead inventory and capital requirements.
  • Build Board and investor materials, including quarterly reporting packages, KPI dashboards, and the narrative behind variance to plan.
  • Run a monthly C-suite business review that management uses to make decisions and drive meaningful changes in the business.
  • Partner with Accounting on the close, Treasury on liquidity, and Division Finance on business operating rhythms.
  • Raise the standard of financial rigor across the company, including preparing the organization for the reporting and forecasting discipline of a public company.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 15+ years of progressive finance experience, including FP&A leadership at a company scaling through significant revenue and headcount growth.
  • Ownership of a full planning cycle, including long-range planning, annual operating planning, and rolling forecasts for a business of meaningful complexity.
  • Strong command of hardware/product economics, including unit cost, gross margin, inventory and working capital, and the cash implications of building physical products.
  • Experience preparing materials for and presenting to senior management, including the C-suite, Board of Directors, and institutional investors.
  • Track record of hiring and developing finance teams and replacing manual processes with durable, scalable systems.
  • Proven ability to operate as a strategic business partner across engineering, manufacturing, and G&A organizations, earning trust and influencing decisions before they are made.
  • Fluency in the underlying financial detail, with the ability to build models when needed and defend key assumptions.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Manufacturing or industrial finance experience, including capital project evaluation and factory ramp planning.
  • Exposure to IPO readiness, public-company reporting, or debt and equity financing processes.
  • Investment banking, private equity, or corporate development experience combined with operating experience.

We are looking for an Industrial Engineer to join our rapidly growing team in Quonset, RI. This role sits within our technical shared services organization (3SI) and carries a dual mandate. First, you operate as a flexible resource for the site: production lines "lease" your time to design and optimize their manufacturing operations as their needs peak and shift — moving across programs and bringing data-driven IE rigor to production line and workstation design, capital equipment, and the metrics that keep a line healthy. Second, you hold a standing factory-macro remit on behalf of 3SI: owning site-level factory layouts, leading cross-functional technical projects, and optimizing material flow across the whole facility rather than any single line. You'll zoom from one line's workstation up to how the entire site moves material and uses its floor space, working shoulder-to-shoulder with Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, Business Operations, and the Factory Services team to get complex undersea hardware built and shipped to spec.

If you are someone who thrives on bringing order to a fast-scaling production floor — and can hold both the single-line detail and the whole-factory picture at once — this role is for you.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Deliver core Industrial Engineering standards and capabilities to Quonset's production lines — capacity planning, labor standards, time studies, workstation and line layouts, and discrete event simulation (DES)
  • Deploy across production lines as a shared resource — partnering with each line's Manufacturing leads to scope the work, deliver it, and hand off cleanly
  • Own site-level factory layout and material flow — plan and maintain the master floor layout and optimize how material moves between receiving, storage, lineside, and shared services as programs scale and new capabilities come online
  • Specify, justify, and deploy capital equipment and tooling — define requirements, own the business case and capex justification, and support vendor selection, build, install, and qualification through to production readiness.
  • Lead cross-functional technical projects on behalf of 3SI — scope, schedule, and drive site infrastructure, equipment, and process-improvement initiatives from definition through execution.
  • Own operations health metrics and KPIs and build the tools and reports that communicate line and site health across the org.
  • Identify bottlenecks and constraints across layout, part shortages, staffing, and tooling, then drive resolution with Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Engineering, and Quality.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 5+ years past experience in a rate manufacturing environment and production-type role where complex mechanical and/or electrical assemblies were built.
  • Experience using real operational data to make informed suggestions and decisions.
  • Experience and demonstrated skills with AutoCAD.
  • Proven line/facility design: value stream mapping, continuous/one-piece flow, and workstation design
  • Experience with Lean Manufacturing principles/implementation.
  • Able to read technical documentation (drawings, vendor schematics, CAD) and understand hardware processes across electronics and mechanical structures
  • Understanding of the means and methods of how material flows around a facility including but not limited to pull systems + triggers, Kanban and MIN MAX calculations.
  • Experience modeling operations using discrete event simulation.
  • Working knowledge of an MES and an ERP (Oracle or equivalent).
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's or higher in Industrial, Mechanical, Aerospace, Manufacturing, Electrical, or Computer Engineering.
  • Hands-on design of tooling, fixtures, or GSE (ground support equipment) for heavy or large-format hardware.
  • Data analytics knowledge and experience including the use of SQL to create complex custom queries, mining and joining tables from production and supply chain databases (experience with Palantir Foundry a plus).
  • Experience creating and owning program, project or production schedules.
  • Experience with Simio and/or Siemen’s Plant Simulation.
  • Experience in a marine, subsea, or other regulated/harsh-environment hardware program

As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

About Anduril Production Strategy & Operations (PS&O)

  • PS&O is the strategic operations arm of Anduril's Production organization. We exist at the intersection of corporate strategy and manufacturing execution — the team that takes senior leadership's strategic priorities and turns them into operational reality. Industrial Development is one of three PS&O pillars:
    • Industrial Development: Production M&A thesis, upstream funnel management, review of vertical integration, production centric diligence
    • Industrial Integration: Post-acquisition production integration deployment to suppliers
    • Special Projects: High-priority, cross-cutting production initiatives ("up and out" strategic projects and "down and in" site deployments)
  • We are a small, high-leverage team building the playbook for scaling defense production. If you want to work on problems that matter — at the intersection of M&A, manufacturing, and national security — this is the team.

What You'll Do

    • You will be the production voice in Anduril's M&A process — the person who can look at an acquisition target and articulate whether it makes Anduril's production base stronger, weaker, or redundant. This is not a traditional CorpDev role. You won't be building DCFs or negotiating purchase agreements. You'll be developing the production thesis for why Anduril should (or shouldn't) acquire a company, running the production centric diligence that CorpDev doesn't have the domain expertise to execute, and ensuring that what we buy actually integrates into how we build things.
    • Production M&A Thesis Development: Scan the defense industrial base and work with Division leaders to evaluate acquisition targets that fill production capability gaps — vertical integration opportunities, critical supplier consolidation, or capacity expansion. Build business cases grounded in manufacturing economics (not just revenue multiples).
    • Diligence Leadership: Scope and lead production-focused diligence workstreams for active deals. Assess target manufacturing capabilities, production capacity, workforce quality, equipment condition, quality systems maturity, and supply chain health. Deliver clear go/no-go recommendations to CorpDev and Production leadership.
    • Integration Handoff: Translate diligence findings into actionable integration plans. Coordinate with Anduril’s M&A integration team on Day 0/Day 1 activities while owning the production-specific integration risks (systems cutover, supplier transition, quality system harmonization).
    • CorpDev Partnership: Serve as the primary PS&O interface to CorpDev throughout the deal process. You complement their financial and legal diligence with operational and production assessment — you are the person who can tell CorpDev "yes, this factory can actually scale to 10x volume" or "no, their quality system is a $5M fix."
    • Team Leadership: Lead a 2-person sub-team (Analyst + Production Diligence Specialist). Set diligence priorities, review work products, and develop junior team members.

What We're Looking For

    • 4–6 years of experience in corporate development, M&A, or strategic transactions — ideally at a defense prime or industrials company (L3Harris, RTX, Northrop, GD, Textron, etc.) where you've seen acquisitions from the operating company side, not just the financial side.
    • Strong understanding of manufacturing operations and what makes a production facility valuable (or a liability). You don't need to be an engineer, but you need to know the right questions to ask on a plant tour.
    • Experience structuring and running diligence processes. You've built diligence plans, coordinated expert workstreams, and synthesized findings into decision-ready packages.
    • Ability to build a thesis from ambiguous inputs. Anduril's data environment is messy and the production landscape is evolving fast — you need to be comfortable with incomplete information and iterating as you learn.
    • Comfortable navigating cross-functional relationships — you'll work across CorpDev, supply chain, engineering, quality, and division production leadership.
    • Strong written and verbal communication skills. You will present to VP/SVP-level production leadership regularly.

Ideal Backgrounds (in order of preference)

    • CorpDev at a defense prime or diversified industrial: You've run acquisitions from inside an operating company. You understand how deals fit into a broader production strategy, not just a financial portfolio. You've done plant visits, managed integration PMOs, or assessed manufacturing synergies. This is the sweet spot.
    • Defense-focused PE (mid-level): Associate or VP at a fund like Veritas Capital, Carlyle's A&D group, or similar. You've done operational diligence on defense/industrial targets and understand production risk assessment. Note: this background is strong but comp expectations may be challenging.
    • Management consulting with M&A/operations focus: Post-MBA or equivalent from a firm with strong industrial practice (McKinsey, Bain, A&M). You've done commercial or operational diligence on manufacturing companies and want to move to the operating side.

What This Role Is Not

    • This is not a financial modeling role. You won't be building LBO models or running accretion/dilution analysis — CorpDev handles that.
    • This is not a pure strategy role. You will be on-site at target facilities, in data rooms, and on the phone with target company operations leaders.
    • This is not a CorpDev role that happens to sit in Production. The skillset is deliberately different — production and manufacturing expertise is what differentiates us.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for an Inventory Control Supervisor to join our rapidly growing team in Quonset, Rhode Island. In this role, you will be responsible for standing up and leading the inventory control function at our multi-product manufacturing site, ensuring material accuracy and availability across multiple production lines. You will oversee a team of Inventory Control Associates, establish cycle count programs, drive root cause analysis on inventory discrepancies, and partner closely with production and warehouse teams to maintain uninterrupted material flow. This will require experience with inventory management systems (ERP/WMS), cycle counting methodologies, and a strong foundation in warehouse operations within a manufacturing or production environment. If you are someone who thrives in a fast-paced, build-from-scratch environment, can bring structure where processes are still being defined, and is energized by the challenge of scaling operations across new product lines, then this role is for you.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Inventory Accuracy & Control: Own cycle count programs, physical inventory counts, and reconciliation processes across all product lines. Drive inventory record accuracy above target thresholds and investigate root causes when discrepancies arise.
  • Team Leadership: Supervise and develop a team of Inventory Control Technicians. Set priorities, assign work, and build a culture of precision and accountability. Coordinate with Materials Associates to ensure alignment across warehouse operations.
  • Multi-Business Line Operations: Maintain segregated inventory tracking across multiple Maritime programs. Ensure material movements, transactions, and adjustments are attributed to the correct business line to support the site's cost allocation model.
  • ERP/WMS System Ownership: Serve as a warehouse power user for ERP and WMS platforms. Support system configuration for multi-BL tracking, ensure transaction discipline, and troubleshoot system issues. Participate in ongoing systems buildout as the site scales.
  • Financial Stewardship: Monitor and reconcile inventory-related variances. Support financial auditing activities, lead physical inventory counts, and partner with the Production Finance Lead on inventory valuation and excess and obsolete (E&O) material management.
  • Compliance & Government Property: Ensure all material management practices comply with federal requirements, including the Defense Federal Acquisitions Regulation Supplement (DFARS) for government property accountability. Maintain audit-ready records at all times.
  • Cross-Functional Coordination: Act as the primary inventory liaison between the warehouse, production lines, procurement, and Finance. Participate in the site's battle rhythm meetings and provide visibility into material status, risks, and constraints.
  • Continuous Improvement: Identify and lead process improvements to increase accuracy, reduce waste, and improve material flow. Implement standardized procedures that scale as additional business lines come to the site.
  • Metric Reporting: Develop and maintain inventory dashboards covering accuracy percentages, inventory turns, transaction discipline, shrinkage, and cycle count results. Report regularly to site leadership on performance and trends.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 3+ years of experience in inventory control, warehouse management, or materials management in a manufacturing environment
  • 1+ year of experience supervising or leading a team
  • Proficiency with ERP and/or WMS platforms (e.g., NetSuite, SAP, Oracle, or similar)
  • Advanced Excel skills (PivotTables, VLOOKUP/INDEX-MATCH) and comfort working with large data sets
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail
  • Effective communicator who can work across functions and present to leadership
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities

PREFFERED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience in a defense, aerospace, or government-contract manufacturing environment
  • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Industrial Engineering, Business, or a related field
  • Experience standing up inventory processes at a new or scaling facility
  • Familiarity with quality management systems (e.g., AS9100, ISO 9001)
  • Lean, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement certification or experience
  • Programming or scripting skills (Python, SQL) for data analysis and reporting automation
  • Experience managing inventory across multiple product lines or programs within a single facility

As the Inventory Control Supervisor, you will lead the physical and system-based integrity of our warehouse operations. You will design, implement, and manage a robust inventory control program that supports Anduril's rapid manufacturing and deployment timelines. This is a warehousing-heavy role: you will not just look at spreadsheets—you will be "boots-on-the-ground," optimizing physical material slotting, strict ABC cycle count adherence, leading a team of material handlers and inventory specialists, and ensuring physical inventory matches our digital systems (ERP/WMS) with near-perfect accuracy.
The ideal candidate has a strong background in aerospace/defense warehousing, thrives in a fast-paced environment, has hands-on experience managing government property, and is passionate about building, mentoring, and scaling a high-performing warehouse team.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

  • Lead & Develop Talent/Processes: Supervise, mentor, and build a high-performing warehouse and inventory control team. Establish standard operating procedures (SOPs) and train team members on physical material handling, safety, and system transactions.
    • Develop processes that increase the efficiency (speed & elimination of waste) and effectiveness of Anduril materials management.
    • Implement necessary systems that match Anduril Federal policies on management of government property & inventory management.
  • Drive Inventory Accuracy: Own the development and execution of a robust Cycle Count and Physical Inventory program (including ABC classification analysis) to achieve and maintain >99% inventory accuracy.
  • Warehouse Slotting Optimization: Optimize picking by velocity, ensure all high-velocity parts are in ideal primary pick locations (preferably golden zone) and a replenishment program is keeping these locations stocked.
  • Investigate & Resolve Discrepancies: Perform deep-dive root cause analyses on inventory variances, shipping/receiving discrepancies, and WIP bin aging. Implement corrective actions to prevent recurrence.
  • Systems & Data Management: Serve as the warehouse super-user for ERP and WMS systems. Ensure all physical material movements (receipts, stock transfers, issues to production) are mirrored accurately and in real-time.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner closely with production planning and manufacturing teams to align material availability with production schedules, minimize disruptions, and meet customer demand on time.
  • Safety & 5S Ownership: Maintain a clean, organized, and safe warehouse environment utilizing 5S methodologies. Ensure proper maintenance and safe operation of material handling equipment (forklifts, pallet jacks, etc.).

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Business Administration, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 3+ years of experience in inventory control, warehouse management, or materials management within an aerospace, defense, or high-volume hardware manufacturing environment.
  • 1+ years of direct supervisory experience leading warehouse associates, inventory specialists, or material handlers.
  • Deep understanding of cycle counting methodologies, warehouse management systems (WMS), and enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems.
  • Ability to be 100% onsite at Anduril’s facilities in Costa Mesa, CA.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Associate’s or Bachelor’s degree in supply chain, manufacturing or related operations field
  • Strong analytical skills (Excel, SQL, or BI tools) to present inventory metrics, cycle count coverage/trends, and capacity constraints.
  • Strong knowledge of AS9100 standards and OSHA laws
  • Experience being hands-on and boots on the ground in the warehouse with proven skills in both process and equipment troubleshooting, and ability to adapt to constantly changing warehouse environments
  • Passion for employee development and enjoy the process of training and developing both new hires and veteran warehouse staff
  • Strong understanding of production rate, critical path analysis, and key warehouse fundamentals
  • Experience supporting process development and implementing new processes
  • Knowledge of 5S, lean manufacturing or 6-Sigma principles
  • Reliable, organized and detail-oriented with excellent verbal & written communication skills
  • Experience in ramping from low-volume/R&D prototyping to high-rate production.

We are seeking a Lead Financial Analyst to join our Corporate Finance team. This individual will join the Consolidations team, serving as the connective tissue across Corporate and Division finance teams to produce financial analysis and insights across Anduril’s business. The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, proactive, and highly collaborative, with an FP&A, consulting or investment banking background, a high standard for accuracy, and the instinct to ask why a number moved rather than simply reporting that it did. This individual will aggregate and validate financial data across divisions, and produce the analysis that the team builds its executive narrative on for the CFO and the C-Suite. This role works across every business unit at Anduril, providing an executive level view of the entire company’s financial performance.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Run the Cadence: Execute the financial operating calendar (monthly, quarterly, annually), owning the templates, data pulls, and deliverables that make each cycle land on time, and chasing inputs from cross-functional partners ahead of key deadlines.
  • Consolidate the Numbers: Own the mechanics of consolidated budgeting, forecasting, and annual planning — collecting and validating division submissions, and building the consolidated view of actuals against plan and forecast.
  • Explain the Variances: Produce clear, accurate variance and driver analysis at the company, division, and business-line level, and draft the first version of the story behind it — what moved, why, and what it implies — for review by the team and delivery to C-Suite.
  • Prepare Executive Materials: Build the exhibits, models, and presentation materials used in monthly business reviews, quarterly reviews, and planning sessions, to a standard that holds up to scrutiny without rework.
  • Build for Scale: Treat recurring manual work as a problem to be solved, not a cost of doing business. Use AI tooling and modern data tools to compress the distance between raw data and finished analysis, so a small team can carry a company-wide scope.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 3-5 years of relevant experience in Corporate Finance/FP&A, Consulting or Strategy, or Investment Banking. Exposure to corporate consolidations, month-end close, or multi-entity reporting is a plus.
  • Strong financial acumen and advanced proficiency in Excel and financial modeling; able to build a model another person can audit.
  • Comfortable working in and across financial systems (e.g., ERP, consolidation, planning tools), with an understanding of how data flows between them and an eye for improving the processes and tooling that make analysis faster and more reliable.
  • Fluent with current AI tools and actively applying them to real work — you have used them to automate or accelerate something meaningful in a prior role, and can walk through what you built, where it worked, and where you deliberately chose not to trust the output.
  • Strong written and oral communication skills and the ability to work seamlessly cross-functionally; collaborative by default, and comfortable building trust with partners across Finance, Accounting, and the business.
  • Intellectually curious — you seek to understand the why behind the numbers and dive into the operations as needed.
  • Action oriented, with a track record of owning a deliverable end to end and producing high-quality work under tight deadlines.
  • High attention to detail and a low tolerance for numbers that do not tie.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Statistics, Economics, Engineering, Business, or related field.
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities.

The Legal Operations team is responsible for optimizing the efficiency and effectiveness of the Legal Department at Anduril and works cross-functionally to streamline workflows, automate routine tasks, implement best practices and support regulatory compliance efforts. With the overarching aim of supporting the Company’s overall strategic goals, the Legal Operations team acts as a bridge between legal, the Company’s business units, and outside counsel.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Legal Operations Engineer to join our rapidly growing team on-site in Costa Mesa, California. This is a hands-on technical execution role where you’ll serve as the operational backbone for the Legal Department’s technology ecosystem for our fast-paced, multi-disciplinary team. You will spend real time in Jira, Airtable, Foundry, our CLM, and the seams between them. Expect to move between a same-day fix for a business partner who can't get a document routed, a data cleanup across a few thousand contract records, and a configuration change that shaves a step out of an approval chain.

You will become a member of the team who knows how every one of these systems actually behaves, not just how it is supposed to work, which is the foundation for designing the next generation of them. As you build that fluency and demonstrate technical judgment, the work shifts from maintaining to building: scoping requirements, designing automated workflows, and eventually taking point on new system implementations as this function grows.

If you are scrappy, technically curious, allergic to manual work a machine could do, and comfortable being the person who gets pinged when a workflow breaks, this role is for you.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Systems Administration & Operational Excellence

  • Integrate into the Legal Department's intake and support queue in Jira - triaging tickets, setting expectations, resolving requests, and escalating what needs a lawyer's judgment to gain first-hand knowledge of our fundamental workflows
  • Serve as frontline administrator and first responder for our legal systems, including CLM, e-signature, matter management, document management, e-billing, and AI tooling - access, permissions, templates, configuration, and break/fix
  • Monitor existing automations and integrations for failures, diagnose root causes, and fix them
  • Execute recurring operational work: user provisioning and offboarding, template updates, approval routing changes, access reviews, and system hygiene checks
  • Maintain data integrity and quality across contract and matter management systems - establishing metadata standards, field hygiene, bulk updates, deduplication, and cleanup ahead of reporting cycles
  • Produce and refresh recurring reporting and dashboards on cycle times, request volume, contract throughput, and outside counsel spend

Process Improvements

  • Make incremental improvements to existing workflows: reduce manual steps, tighten validation, add conditional logic, eliminate the failure modes you keep seeing in the queue
  • Build automations and integrations to close gaps between systems using no-code/low-code platforms, APIs, and scripting
  • Track recurring pain points from the ticket queue and surface them to Legal Ops with a proposed fix and a rough sense of effort
  • Assist with data migrations and configuration changes during larger Legal Ops initiatives
  • Support AI tooling in the department - prompt and template maintenance, output quality spot-checks, and honest reporting on where the tool isn't working

Growing into

We are looking for an exceptional Accounting Manager to build and lead the long-lived assets function — property, plant, and equipment, leases, and intangibles. The Accounting team owns the close, technical accounting, and reporting infrastructure behind one of the fastest-scaling companies in defense. This is a build seat more than a maintain seat: we are preparing for a future potential IPO, expanding rapidly, and integrating acquired businesses, so you will set the processes, systems, and controls this function runs on for years. 

ABOUT THE JOB

The ideal candidate will be able to support the hyper growth of our business and will therefore need to be comfortable and experienced moving at an incredibly fast pace. Come join us as we disrupt an entire industry and help take your career to the next level with a team that is charging towards changing the world of defense.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Long-Lived Asset Ownership: Own the accounting for Anduril’s long-lived assets end to end — property, plant, and equipment, leases, and intangibles — including the fixed asset and lease subledgers, depreciation and amortization, additions, transfers, disposals, and monthly roll-forwards.
  • Capitalization Policy: Serve as the primary liaison between the business and Anduril’s capitalization policy — advising program, engineering, and operations teams on capitalize-versus-expense treatment, reviewing capital spend requests for policy compliance, and keeping the policy current as the business scales.
  • Team Leadership: Lead, mentor, and develop a team of accountants, setting priorities, reviewing work, and building bench strength as the asset base scales.
  • Government Grants: Monitor and track government grants funding Anduril’s capital projects to ensure compliance, accurate reporting, and timely disbursement.
  • Software Capitalization: Oversee and execute capitalization of software assets in alignment with applicable accounting standards (ASC 350).
  • Financial Close: Own the monthly, quarterly, and annual close for long-lived asset accounts, delivering journal entries, accruals, and flux analysis on the close calendar.
  • Reporting & Disclosures: Own the fixed asset, lease, and intangible asset footnotes, disclosures, and supporting schedules for financial reporting.
  • Reconciliations: Review balance sheet reconciliations for long-lived asset accounts on a timely basis, and research and resolve variances as needed.
  • Systems & Process Improvement: Help implement new systems or improve efficiencies with current systems to support continued company and team growth.
  • SOX Readiness: Help build and maintain SOX-ready process documentation and key controls over fixed assets, leases, and intangibles in support of public company readiness.
  • Audit Support: Serve as the primary owner of external audit requests covering long-lived assets, including PBC schedules, walkthroughs, and technical accounting memos.
  • Cross-Functional Partnership: Partner with FP&A, Procurement, Facilities and Real Estate, and Tax on capital planning, lease commitments, asset tracking, and book-to-tax depreciation differences.
  • Mindset: No job too small mentality, be curious and helpful to others.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Fixed Assets & CIP: Experience managing or overseeing fixed assets and Capital Improvement Projects (CIP) is required.
  • Education: Bachelor's degree in accounting or related field.
  • Experience: 6+ years of progressive accounting experience, including direct people management experience.
  • Technical Accounting: Working knowledge of the long-lived asset standards — ASC 360 (property, plant and equipment; impairment), ASC 842 (leases), and ASC 350 (intangibles and internal-use software).
  • Systems & Rigor: Highly detail-oriented with strong experience in Excel, ERP systems, and US GAAP.
  • Prioritization: Proven ability to manage competing priorities in a high-growth organization.
  • Execution & Strategic Vision: Able to get your hands dirty to drive organizational change while also maintaining an ability to manage against strategic priorities and reporting.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Launched Effects team at Anduril is responsible for scaling the manufacturing and delivery of the Altius family of systems (including the ALTIUS-600 and ALTIUS-700). As the premier Air-Launched Effects (ALE) platform for the U.S. military and its allies, ALTIUS is redefining modern warfare. These tube-launched, autonomous aerial systems must be built to survive extreme deployment environments, requiring precision manufacturing of advanced composites, complex avionics, and modular payload integrations for ISR, Electronic Warfare, and kinetic strike capabilities.

As part of the Launched Effects manufacturing team, you will bridge the gap between cutting-edge R&D and high-rate production. We are a fast-moving, mission-driven group of manufacturing engineers, quality specialists, and production operations experts who refuse to accept traditional, slow defense manufacturing timelines. We continuously optimize our assembly lines, implement automated testing, design for manufacturing (DFM), and build resilient supply chains to deploy reliable systems to the front lines at unprecedented speed. If you want to work on a team where your production and manufacturing decisions directly impact global security, this is it.

ABOUT THE JOB

This role is about much more than just processes; it's about orchestrating the industrialization of a vital product. You will own the entire manufacturing value-chain for Altius, from current rate to high-volume deployment. Your responsibilities will span the spectrum: driving Design for Manufacturability (DFM) feedback into design, innovating tool design and selection, creating and optimizing high-rate production lines, fostering strategic vendor partnerships, embedding robust quality assurance throughout, and meticulously documenting build processes.

*This position is permanently based in Ashville, OH, and requires candidates to temporarily relocate for a comprehensive 3-month training program: 1 month in Santa Ana, CA, followed by 2 months (approximately) in Atlanta, GA. To support your transition, Anduril will fully provide and cover all corporate housing, transportation, and travel accommodations during this training period. Your recruiter will discuss the logistics of this program with you in detail during the hiring process

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Execute the manufacturing of a certain product or set of products, from initial prototyping through large full-scale production.
  • Work with design engineers during the development process to drive design for manufacturing best practices into the design effort, and help facilitate the transition from design to prototype to rate production.
  • Act as a manufacturing laison for mechanical fabrication and avionics with subject matter expertise in these areas and key experience in design for manufacturability.
  • Own documentation required for successfully manufacturing product group hardware at scale, such as MBOM’s, work instructions & requirements, etc.
  • Advise on quality management and business application programs as they pertain to manufacturing within your area.
  • Collaborate with internal customers and manufacturing planning teams to define capacity planning actions to meet customer needs and expectations.
  • Analyze metrics for continuous improvement initiatives (cost reduction, QI reduction & capacity increase).
  • Instill a culture of innovation, teamwork, and accountability within the manufacturing engineering product team.
  • Develop production and test methodologies and implement best practices to enable scaling production capabilities for larger, more complex products.
  • Travel to suppliers and partner sites to do initial sourcing work, solve ongoing production issues, and implement process procedures as required.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams, which requires regular interaction with production and manufacturing stakeholders and frequently working directly on the production floor.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Degree in a technical field preferred such as engineering, math, or a hard science.
  • 2+ years of experience in a relevant field, preferably manufacturing or design of electromechanical hardware.
  • Demonstrated ability to creatively deliver electromechanical hardware in a resource-constrained environment.
  • An attitude of world-class mission assurance, quality, attention to detail, and dedication.
  • A genuine interest in manufacturing and thirst for learning.
  • Candidates must demonstrate flexibility and dedication, being prepared to work extended hours and weekends when dictated by critical business priorities.
  • Regular travel between our various locations is an essential component of this role.
  • U.S. citizenship is required pursuant to contractual obligations.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Exposure to aircraft programs or other relevant aerospace & defense technologies.
  • Software scripting experience in any language.
  • Lean Six Sigma certification (Green Belt or higher) or equivalent experience.
  • Familiarity with J-STD-001, IPC-A-610, and IPC/WHMA-A-620 or equivalent standards.

ABOUT THE JOB 

We are seeking a Manufacturing Test Engineer to join Anduril, working in a cutting-edge start-up environment to advance the state-of-the-possible in subsea robotics. The Manufacturing Test Engineer will be charged with developing and implementing high-fidelity, automated test procedures on both the component and system level. Working closely with engineering staff and a team of skilled electro-mechanical technicians, this role is key to advancing our testing capabilities to ensure the highest levels quality are achieved as we continue drive scalability into our production operations.

WHAT YOU’LL DO 

  • Build a broad range of test capabilities across the manufacturing value stream - from system level checkouts and acceptance testing to key component level in process validation
  • Develop, execute, and manage test eco-system to de-risk hardware and ensure product meets target reliability levels and ultimate design intent
  • Perform hands-on and data-driven root cause analysis of electromechanical subsystems utilizing structured problem solving methodologies
  • Design and implement semi-automated testing equipment/protocols for subsystem characterization and reliability/environmental testing
  • Collaborate with the design/systems team throughout product development cycles to perform risk assessments, maintain ownership of test deployment activities in production, oversee technician training, burn down bug fixes/improvements as needed
  • Produce and maintain testing logs/data, develop library of error codes with troubleshooting logic/diagrams for fast issue resolution
  • Generate controlled test instructions that can be easily followed by technician team in MES or other test execution systems
  • Optimize test design and execution of full system “end of line” factory acceptance test (FAT) of AUVs
  • Design and execution of PCBA and electrical system components with hands on testing and rework as necessary

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Electro-Mechanical, EE/Computer Engineering, or related field, or equivalent work experience
  • Experience in hardware testing and automated test systems (LabVIEW, Test Stand, etc.)
  • Proficiency in programming languages such as Python, Matlab, SHELL, or others
  • Experience with computer hardware communication protocols: USB, Ethernet, RS232, RS485, PCIe, HDMI, CAN, etc
  • 3+ years of experience in a relevant field, preferably test design of electro-mechanical hardware in a manufacturing environment
  • Are well versed with complex electromechanical systems and are passionate about understanding what it takes to make them work reliably
  • Have experience developing full system test plans and know how to execute them on fast-paced product development timelines
  • Have experience with programming/testing a wide range of sensors, actuators, and electrical components
  • Can prototype and run your own tests, from experimental setup to hardware and software implementation
  • Must be eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience in sub-sea robotics or AUV/UUV industries
  • Familiar with Product Life Cycle (PLM) systems, Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), and Test Execution Systems (TES)
  • Demonstrated ability to learn new skills or adapt to new situations. Un-phased by challenges that go beyond the traditional comfort zone or work experience. Multidisciplinary approach to problem solving
  • Comfortable with high project ownership under technical and schedule pressure, particularly where the scope and definition are limited
  • Experience testing and operating with or around hazardous systems (high voltage up to 400V)
  • Experience working on projects that involve the integration of electrical, mechanical, and software/firmware systems

This team owns the shared technical services that support all production business lines on site, including machining, hydrostatic testing, tooling, and 3D printing. The hydrostatic test chamber is a critical shared resource used to validate the integrity of pressurized vessels and components before they are integrated into undersea systems. As the site scales to support multiple product lines, demand on this capability will grow and this role will be essential to keeping production on schedule.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Pressure Vessel Test Technician to operate and maintain our hydrostatic test chamber, performing pressure testing on sealed vessels, housings, and other pressurized components used in autonomous underwater vehicles. Our undersea platforms are flooded vehicles, meaning the electronics and other water-sensitive subsystems are housed inside individually sealed, pressurized enclosures. This role is responsible for verifying the structural integrity and watertight seal of those enclosures before they are integrated into production vehicles. You will set up and execute test procedures, monitor pressure data, document results, and work closely with production and engineering teams to ensure components meet specifications. This is a hands-on role that requires mechanical aptitude, comfort working with high-pressure systems, strong attention to detail, and the discipline to follow test procedures precisely. If you are someone who takes pride in getting the details right and understands that your work directly impacts the reliability of fielded systems, this role is for you.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Hydrostatic Test Execution: Set up, operate, and monitor the hydrostatic test chamber to perform pressure testing on sealed vessels, housings, and pressurized components. Follow established test procedures to pressurize components to specified levels, hold for required durations, and monitor for pressure loss or leaks.
  • Test Preparation and Fixturing: Prepare components for testing by installing fittings, plugs, seals, and connections. Verify test setup is correct before pressurization. Maintain and organize test fixtures, tooling, and support equipment.
  • Inspection and Defect Identification: Visually inspect components before, during, and after testing for leaks, pinholes, seal failures, weld deficiencies, or other nonconforming conditions. Identify and clearly document any anomalies found during testing.
  • Data Recording and Documentation: Accurately record all test parameters, results, and observations. Complete test reports and quality records in accordance with standard operating procedures. Interpret pressure gauge readings and calibration data to ensure testing accuracy.
  • Equipment Maintenance and Calibration: Perform routine maintenance on the test chamber, pumps, gauges, fittings, and related equipment. Support calibration activities and flag equipment that is out of tolerance or in need of repair.
  • Safety Compliance: Adhere strictly to all safety protocols for high-pressure testing operations. Maintain a clean and organized work area. Report any safety concerns, near-misses, or equipment malfunctions immediately.
  • Cross-Functional Coordination: Work with production teams, quality, and engineering to schedule tests, communicate results, and support troubleshooting when components do not pass. Provide feedback to engineering on recurring test failures or design concerns.
  • Process Improvement: Contribute to the development and refinement of test procedures, fixturing, and workflows. Identify opportunities to improve test efficiency, throughput, or reliability as the site scales.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 4+ years of experience in a hands-on testing, inspection, or manufacturing technician role
  • Familiarity with pressure testing (hydrostatic or pneumatic), leak detection, or similar quality verification processes
  • Ability to read and work from technical documentation, engineering drawings, and test procedures
  • Strong attention to detail with a disciplined approach to following procedures and recording data accurately
  • Mechanical aptitude and comfort working with high-pressure systems, pumps, fittings, and gauges
  • Effective communicator who can clearly document and convey test results to engineering and production teams
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience in defense, aerospace, or maritime manufacturing
  • Experience with pressure vessel testing, proof testing, or burst testing of sealed enclosures or housings
  • Familiarity with subsea, AUV, UUV, or underwater robotics systems
  • VT (Visual Testing) or PT (Penetrant Testing) certification, or willingness to obtain
  • Experience with ERP or MES systems for test record management and work order closeout
  • Confined space, crane, or rigging certification
  • High school diploma or technical certificate in a relevant trade; associate degree in a technical field is a plus
