ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril Imaging builds electro-optical and infrared sensor systems that go on Anduril platforms as well as our own stand-alone products. The hardware is precision optics, cooled infrared detectors, custom electronics, and tight-tolerance electromechanical assemblies. Several products are moving from development into rate production at the same time.

ABOUT THE JOB

Senior Commodity Manager owns the supply chain outcomes behind those products. The team is small and growing. You will own supplier relationships end to end, from identifying a source and negotiating the agreement to standing up capacity and holding it through a ramp.

This role requires deep understanding of areas in infrared optics and the materials behind them. Germanium crystal, boules, and blanks. Chalcogenide infrared glass. Lens and window fabrication, grinding, polishing, diamond turning, and centering as well as optical coatings. Lens cell assemblies and related optical assemblies. Detector and dewar assemblies, cold filters, and cryocoolers.

This commodity carries additional exposure. Germanium pricing and availability are driven by export policy and a thin upstream supply base, and the alternative material paths carry their own critical mineral dependencies. The work includes reaching past tier one into the feedstock layer, modeling material price scenarios, and structuring forward positions and consignment arrangements that secure supply rather than just placing orders.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own suppliers end to end. Identify and select sources, run requests for quote, drive input to make-buy decisions, and serve as the commercial and technical owner of the relationship. Supplier signals currently reach Anduril through several uncoordinated paths. You will be the conduit that keeps them consistent across programs.
  • Negotiate the commercial structure. Draft and negotiate pricing, capacity commitments, lead times, payment, warranty, and service terms. Build toward long-term agreements where they secure capacity. Sequence leverage deliberately so commitments buy terms rather than just parts.
  • Build the cost model, then use it. Develop should-cost and clean-sheet models, run cost-breakdown analysis on quotes, and drive total cost of ownership across the lifecycle. Reconcile bill of material cost against finance so product cost reflects what the parts actually cost.
  • Secure capacity ahead of ramp. Map supply network lead time and flexibility, place coverage against demand well before it is needed, and resolve capacity gaps before they become schedule problems. Suppliers in this space book out far in advance. The job is to be early.
  • Engage engineering before the design locks. Give design for manufacturability feedback, influence specifications using supply intelligence on availability, lead time, and lifecycle health, so design decisions account for supply reality instead of discovering it.
  • De-risk the bill of material. Complete risk assessments, qualify alternates and second sources, drive commonality and supplier rationalization, and manage obsolescence before it gates a build.
  • Escalate and clear blockers. Participate in program reviews and operational escalation forums. Triage supply disruptions, resolve shortages, and drive supplier issues to conclusion, including executive escalation when it is warranted.
  • Carry compliance into the sourcing decision. Work country of origin, domestic content, defense acquisition regulation, export control, and rated order requirements into supplier selection and purchase order structure. The point is to engineer compliance into the design and supply decision rather than remediate it later.
  • Complete supplier qualification. Own the capability and authorization portions of supplier evaluation and coordinate with the Supplier Quality Organization.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, supply chain, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience
  • 8 or more years across sourcing engineering, commodity management, supplier development, supplier quality, manufacturing engineering, or cost engineering
  • Experience owning supplier relationships that included both technical assessment and commercial negotiation
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings and CAD model and assemblies.
  • Ability to travel a 10-25% of the time for vendor on-site visits
  • Eligible to access export-controlled technical data under United States export control law
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. secret clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Advanced technical degree
  • Experience in infrared or electro-optical systems, precision optics, photonics, sensors, or other high-precision hardware
  • Should-cost or clean-sheet cost modeling, design-to-cost, or value engineering work
  • Experience taking a product from development into rate production, particularly in high-mix low-volume environments
  • Experience negotiating long-term agreements, supply agreements, or capacity commitments
  • Familiarity with defense acquisition regulation flowdowns, export control, rated orders, country of origin, or domestic content requirements
  • Experience in a fast-moving company where the process was still being built

We are seeking an exceptional Senior, Cost Accounting to execute full stack cost accounting for Anduril’s high-rate manufacturing site, Arsenal-1. This role is critical to driving accuracy, insight, and control across our development, manufacturing, and production operations.

ABOUT THE JOB

Reporting to the Senior Manager, Cost Accounting, the Senior will ensure consistent and compliant application of Anduril’s standard costing methodology and be responsible for detailed transactional and balance sheet reconciliation review. The ideal candidate will bring deep technical competency, strong leadership skills, and a risk-based approach in support of the company’s preparation for a potential future IPO.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Perform and continuously improve standard costing practices to ensure accurate product costing, variance analysis, and margin reporting for designated product lines and production sites.

  • Support the Senior Manager with preparing insightful cost analyses and recommendations to support strategic and operational decision-making.
  • Support the Manager with a continuous improvement mindset, prioritizing automation to enhance efficiency and accuracy in all financial processes.

Anduril's Marketing team helps people understand what we build, why it matters and why it's urgent. We work with Communications and Design to shape how Anduril shows up and how our products are understood by customers, policymakers, partners, recruits and the public.

Product Marketing sits at the center of that work. Differentiation, credibility and earned trust are core values of the team's approach.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Senior Director of Global Product Marketing to lead Anduril's product marketing strategy across Anduril's expanding portfolio of products and capabilities. This leader will build the systems that determine how we position products, translate technical differentiation into mission impact, bring capabilities to market across the US & allied nations and reinforce the maturity & manufacturability of our products.

The role covers the full product lifecycle. Products at different stages require different marketing approaches. The Senior Director needs to know when to drive awareness, when to build demand, when to deepen adoption and when to let the product speak for itself. Every claim has to be precise, credible and grounded in what the product actually does.

This leader will work directly with division leaders and senior executives, including the Chief Business Officer and Chief Strategy Officer. They will work collaboratively across Business Divisions, Communications, Design and Strategic Growth teams, so Anduril presents one coherent portfolio while preserving the distinct mission, customer and competitive context of each product.

The Senior Director will also lead Anduril's marketing approach in international markets working closely with Anduril's Global Defense team and local country leaders.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own Anduril's global product narrative, positioning and messaging architecture in close collaboration with the Communications team. Connect individual products to the company mission. Make sure Anduril communicates as one company across divisions, products, markets and channels.
  • Build differentiated marketing approaches across the full product lifecycle. Know what each stage demands and execute accordingly.
  • Own the product marketing component of go-to-market planning for priority products, programs and markets. Define clear success criteria tied to business outcomes and credible forms of measurement.
  • Partner with Strategic Growth, Business Development, and division leadership to define target audiences, competitive positioning, proof points and market entry strategies.
  • Equip customer-facing teams with the narratives, presentations, product materials, demonstrations and competitive intelligence they need.
  • Serve as the primary product marketing partner to the CBO, CSO and other senior leaders.
  • Develop a global framework for marketing Anduril's products to allied nations. Adapt narratives to the strategic, operational, cultural and lifecycle context of each market.
  • Provide oversight of the product marketing strategy for major U.S. and international defense trade shows. Inform key win themes, messaging hierarchy, and which product capabilities deserve priority focus at each event.
  • Elevate & grow the talented product marketing team. Rooted in ambitious standards, low ego, consistent candor, disciplined systems, and extreme autonomy.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 15+ years in product marketing, portfolio marketing, go-to-market strategy, product strategy or a closely related field
  • 7+ years leading and developing high-performing teams, including senior leaders and multidisciplinary organizations
  • Demonstrated experience defining positioning and go-to-market strategy for technically complex products
  • Track record of marketing products across the full lifecycle, from launch through scaled adoption
  • Exceptional ability to turn complex technical capabilities into clear, credible narratives
  • Experience partnering directly with senior executives, business unit leaders, product leaders and technical teams
  • Strong strategic judgment. Can distinguish consequential priorities from noise.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence across functions and drive decisions without relying on formal authority
  • Excellent written, verbal and presentation skills
  • Strong operational and financial discipline, including experience managing meaningful budgets and proving measurable impact in credible ways
  • Comfort operating in a fast-moving environment with ambiguity, incomplete information and high expectations
  • Willingness to travel regularly within the United States and internationally
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities

Experience:

  • Defense technology, aerospace, national security, enterprise technology, AI, robotics, autonomy or another deeply technical industry
  • Developing product marketing strategies across multiple countries and regional markets
  • Marketing an integrated portfolio that combines hardware, software and services
  • Supporting government customers, regulated markets or products with sensitive communications considerations
  • Leading strategy for major industry events, product demonstrations or executive-level customer engagements
  • Existing relationships across the defense, technology or national security ecosystem.
  • Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Top Secret security clearance

This role will interface with senior leadership across finance, production, engineering, growth, program management, and supply chain to shape and execute on the division’s long-term business objectives.

Leadership & Business Partnering

  • Build, lead, and develop a team of finance managers and analysts, elevating the quality and consistency of financial support across business lines
  • Serve as strategic advisor to business line and division leaders, translating financial analysis into resourcing, tradeoff, and operational decisions
  • Guide production and engineering partners in defining KPIs and evaluating performance against productivity and profitability targets

Strategic Finance

  • Build and pressure-test the long-term business cases behind the division’s biggest bets, including new IP, facility investments, and major program pursuits
  • Inform the division’s long-range plan by translating production ramps, R&D investment, and contract timing into scenario-based outcomes that give executive leadership a coherent view of where and when to deploy capital
  • Benchmark against peers across defense, autonomy, and industrial tech to sharpen the division’s point of view on unit economics, efficiency, and capital allocation
  • Partner with Growth to shape pricing structures and new commercial models for the division’s future products and programs

Operational Finance

  • Own working capital forecasts and capital expenditure tracking across a portfolio of product lines and contracts
  • Ensure supply chain financial commitments are tracked and governed appropriately as the business scales

We are looking for a Senior Electrical Engineer to join our rapidly growing team in Irvine, CA. This role will own rapidly developed, ruggedized electronics design in addition to scaling legacy design concepts to support full-rate production. In this role, you will partner with our Architecture and Product Management team to help drive system requirements prior to owning full PCB and/or electrical system design. This will require identifying high risk areas, creating and validating electronics designs for embedded compute and/or power systems, and testing for long term-reliability while considering manufacturability and testability in the design.

If you are someone who enjoys designing mission-critical electrical circuit cards and integrated systems with the freedom to drive product development from often undefined requirements then this role is for you.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Take ownership as the main point of contact for electrical integration activities.
  • Provide hands on and in-field support of prototype and production level product.
  • Collaborate with mechanical engineers to optimize selection, design and integration of high power components, modules and distribution.
  • Trade-off component and module selections against size, weight, power and EMC requirements.
  • Collaborate with design team to achieve reliability goals at a system level in context of concepts of operation.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Minimum 8+ years of professional experience
  • Self starter with the ability to design digital & analog electronics from concept and functional prototype, to production ready product.
  • Ability to troubleshoot existing hardware to find root cause of issues and implement improvements to improve the design.
  • Develop clear documentation to capture design requirements, specifications, test coverage, and test reports.
  • Complete full cycle PCB design including collecting requirements, schematic design, component selection, completion of layout, bring-up, test, debug, validation, characterization, and integration with the system.
  • Work closely with other mechanical, software, firmware, and test engineers to deliver fully functional products.
  • Work in a fast-paced environment supporting new developments, active deployments, and customer operated hardware.
  • Concurrently manage involvement in multiple projects at various stages.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical Engineering or equivalent
  • 8+ years of experience designing, testing and troubleshooting complex board designs and products.
  • Competence with test equipment such as oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, thermal chambers, current-probes, and automation of tests.
  • Familiarity with switch mode power supply design and testing.
  • Familiarity with standard interfaces such as Ethernet, CAN, I2C, SPI, PCIe, USB, etc.
  • Familiarity with common MCU, CPU, FPGA devices and technologies.
  • Knowledge of modern analog and digital electronics and electronic circuits.
  • Exceptional organization and communication skills (both written and oral).
  • Proficient with Altium Designer or equivalent electronic design automation design tools.
  • Proficiency with scripting languages (Python, Matlab, etc.)
  • Ability to root cause Full stack HLOS application to hardware component level issues.

By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

About the Team

Anduril develops advanced robotic systems that operate at the edge across land, sea, and air. Our team builds the critical systems powering everything from Group 1–3 autonomous aerial systems (such as Ghost, Anvil, Bolt, and Altius) to autonomous Sentry Towers that safeguard borders and critical infrastructure with real-time sensor fusion.
Underpinning these diverse robotic fleets is our DeviceOS team, which engineers the unified, highly reliable operating system and hardware-enablement platform that powers all of Anduril's autonomous assets. We take systems from initial schematics and paper sketches to hardened, field-ready robotics deployed in the most challenging operational environments on Earth.

About the Job

Underneath our airframes and Sentry Towers are custom carrier boards, embedded ARM architectures, and NVIDIA Jetson modules integrated with an intense array of hardware: electro-optical/infrared cameras, radars, CAN-connected sensor nodes, GPS, flight controllers, radios, and high-power motor drivers.
Between the silicon vendor’s raw Board Support Package (BSP) and our autonomous mission software sits a layer that must be owned deliberately: the boot chain, device trees, kernel drivers, and the guarantee that every piece of hardware deterministically enumerates and operates when our image boots.
In this role, you will own the boundary where custom hardware meets software. You will customize vendor BSPs and evaluate upstream changes. You will debug boot end-to-end—from firmware (EDK2/U-Boot) through unified kernel images to an encrypted root filesystem running at the tactical edge. You are the engineer who can read a schematic to diagnose a bus fault, remediate a kernel CVE on deployed hardware, and write the platform drivers that keep our robots flying and monitoring.
In this role, you will maintain and support a large deployed fleet by writing fixes for existing hardware and boot chains. This work is critical to our operations: a firmware regression is not just a failing test, it is a physical unit someone has to service in the field.

What You’ll Do

  • Own the Boot Path: Own the boot sequence end-to-end on deployed compute: low-level firmware, U-Boot/UEFI, unified kernel images, initrd, encrypted storage unlock, and handoff to a running NixOS environment. Debug boot failures on hardware via remote support.
  • Customize & Sustain Vendor BSPs: Reconcile vendor BSPs (Tegra/Jetson Linux, NXP, etc.) with modern NixOS package sets. Produce kernel and device tree patches when hardware requires custom behavior, and forward-port these changes across OS baseline upgrades.
  • Guarantee Deterministic Hardware Availability: Ensure all peripherals—cameras, radars, motor controllers, CAN networks, and radios—are reliably enumerated, correctly named, and fully operational across boots and platform upgrades.
  • Sustain a Long-Lived Baseline: Keep the existing signed boot chain and disk encryption working as the firmware, kernels, and package sets change underneath them. Triage and remediate CVEs in vendor kernels and low-level system components on our systems already deployed in the field.
  • Automate & Validate: Build and maintain automated Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) test suites to catch regressions in power states, bus communication, and platform stability before code hits flight or field hardware.
  • Perform Deep Hardware/Software Root-Cause Analysis: Diagnose intermittent bus errors, thermal and power throttling issues, kernel panics, and boot hangs using serial consoles, logic analyzers, dmesg, and hardware schematics.
  • Be the Upstream: Triage upstream kernel and vendor BSP issues, produce the patch when no upstream fix is coming, and carry that patch set forward as the platform moves.

Required Qualifications

  • 4+ years of professional embedded Linux platform, sustainment of deployed embedded Linux platforms, or kernel-adjacent integration experience.
  • Deep understanding of the embedded Linux boot chain: firmware/bootloaders (U-Boot, EDK2), device trees, kernel command line, initrd/initramfs, and root filesystem assembly.
  • Strong programming skills in C (for kernel/driver development and BSP patching) along with proficiency in Rust or C++ for userspace platform integration and services.
  • Hands-on experience debugging hardware at the bench: using serial consoles, reading schematics and component datasheets, and tracing issues to the board level.
  • Experience maintaining software deployed on real-world hardware, where updates must be safe, resilient to bricking, and strictly validated against regressions.
  • U.S. Person status is required due to export control regulations (ITAR/EAR), with eligibility to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Nix / NixOS Experience: Direct experience with declarative systems (Nix/NixOS) for embedded builds; or deep expertise in Yocto/Buildroot paired with an appetite to transition to modern, reproducible paradigms.
  • NVIDIA Jetson / Tegra Depth: Hands-on experience with JetPack, Jetson Linux BSP, Tegra boot architecture, or CUDA compute runtime integration.
  • Low-Level Platform Security: Practical implementation of hardware root-of-trust, secure boot, HAB/AHAB, or measured boot (TPM).
  • Automated HIL Testing: Experience architecting automated test benches using Python or Bash to validate embedded Linux builds against physical test targets.
  • Familiarity with functional programming paradigms (e.g., Nix, Haskell).
  • Upstream open-source contributions to the Linux kernel, U-Boot, or system-level open-source projects.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril Imaging builds electro-optical and infrared sensor systems that go on Anduril platforms as well as our own stand-alone products. The hardware is precision optics, cooled infrared detectors, custom electronics, and tight-tolerance electromechanical assemblies. Several products are moving from development into rate production at the same time.

ABOUT THE JOB

Senior Global Supply Manager owns the supply chain outcomes behind those products. The team is small and growing. You will own supplier relationships end to end, from identifying a source and negotiating the agreement to standing up capacity and holding it through a ramp.

This role requires deep understanding of areas in infrared optics and the materials behind them. Germanium crystal, boules, and blanks. Chalcogenide infrared glass. Lens and window fabrication, grinding, polishing, diamond turning, and centering as well as optical coatings. Lens cell assemblies and related optical assemblies. Detector and dewar assemblies, cold filters, and cryocoolers.

This commodity carries additional exposure. Germanium pricing and availability are driven by export policy and a thin upstream supply base, and the alternative material paths carry their own critical mineral dependencies. The work includes reaching past tier one into the feedstock layer, modeling material price scenarios, and structuring forward positions and consignment arrangements that secure supply rather than just placing orders.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own suppliers end to end. Identify and select sources, run requests for quote, drive input to make-buy decisions, and serve as the commercial and technical owner of the relationship. Supplier signals currently reach Anduril through several uncoordinated paths. You will be the conduit that keeps them consistent across programs.
  • Negotiate the commercial structure. Draft and negotiate pricing, capacity commitments, lead times, payment, warranty, and service terms. Build toward long-term agreements where they secure capacity. Sequence leverage deliberately so commitments buy terms rather than just parts.
  • Build the cost model, then use it. Develop should-cost and clean-sheet models, run cost-breakdown analysis on quotes, and drive total cost of ownership across the lifecycle. Reconcile bill of material cost against finance so product cost reflects what the parts actually cost.
  • Secure capacity ahead of ramp. Map supply network lead time and flexibility, place coverage against demand well before it is needed, and resolve capacity gaps before they become schedule problems. Suppliers in this space book out far in advance. The job is to be early.
  • Engage engineering before the design locks. Give design for manufacturability feedback, influence specifications using supply intelligence on availability, lead time, and lifecycle health, so design decisions account for supply reality instead of discovering it.
  • De-risk the bill of material. Complete risk assessments, qualify alternates and second sources, drive commonality and supplier rationalization, and manage obsolescence before it gates a build.
  • Escalate and clear blockers. Participate in program reviews and operational escalation forums. Triage supply disruptions, resolve shortages, and drive supplier issues to conclusion, including executive escalation when it is warranted.
  • Carry compliance into the sourcing decision. Work country of origin, domestic content, defense acquisition regulation, export control, and rated order requirements into supplier selection and purchase order structure. The point is to engineer compliance into the design and supply decision rather than remediate it later.
  • Complete supplier qualification. Own the capability and authorization portions of supplier evaluation and coordinate with the Supplier Quality Organization.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, supply chain, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience
  • 8 or more years across sourcing engineering, commodity management, supplier development, supplier quality, manufacturing engineering, or cost engineering
  • Experience owning supplier relationships that included both technical assessment and commercial negotiation
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings and CAD model and assemblies.
  • Ability to travel a 10-25% of the time for vendor on-site visits
  • Eligible to access export-controlled technical data under United States export control law
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. secret clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Advanced technical degree
  • Experience in infrared or electro-optical systems, precision optics, photonics, sensors, or other high-precision hardware
  • Should-cost or clean-sheet cost modeling, design-to-cost, or value engineering work
  • Experience taking a product from development into rate production, particularly in high-mix low-volume environments
  • Experience negotiating long-term agreements, supply agreements, or capacity commitments
  • Familiarity with defense acquisition regulation flowdowns, export control, rated orders, country of origin, or domestic content requirements
  • Experience in a fast-moving company where the process was still being built

ABOUT THE JOB

We are seeking a Senior Maintenance Supervisor to help stand up and lead the maintenance and reliability function at Arsenal-1. This is a ground-floor leadership role: you will build the maintenance organization from the ground up — hiring and developing the technician team, establishing preventive and predictive maintenance programs, standing up the CMMS and asset data, and partnering with facilities, controls, and production to keep a hyper-scale manufacturing operation running at high availability. You will own the reliability of the equipment and systems that our production depends on, set the standard for how maintenance is done at the site, and grow a team that keeps the line up as we ramp.

This is a highly dynamic, hands-on role that requires both frontline technical depth and people-leadership skills. You will be on the floor, solving problems with your team, while building the programs, discipline, and culture that make maintenance a competitive advantage for the site.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Build, lead, coach, and mentor the Arsenal-1 maintenance technician team — from the first hires through a scaled, multi-shift organization — developing skills, cross-training, and a strong safety-first culture.
  • Stand up and own the preventive, predictive, and reactive maintenance programs for production equipment, tooling, and facility-critical systems, driving toward high equipment availability and uptime.
  • Establish and administer the computerized maintenance management system (CMMS), including asset hierarchy, PM schedules, work-order workflows, and spare-parts/MRO inventory, and keep the data accurate as the single source of truth.
  • Direct daily maintenance operations — prioritize and assign work orders, clear blockers, and balance planned PM against emergent breakdowns to protect the production schedule.
  • Lead rapid troubleshooting and repair of mechanical, electrical, pneumatic, hydraulic, and controls issues on the floor, minimizing downtime and getting equipment back into production quickly.
  • Drive root-cause analysis and corrective action on recurring failures, tracking issues to closure and feeding improvements back into PM plans and standard work.
  • Ensure all maintenance work follows safety procedures, lockout/tagout, and standard work; proactively identify and drive safety improvement opportunities.
  • Partner with facilities, controls/automation, manufacturing engineering, production, supply chain, and EHS to support new equipment installation, commissioning, and readiness, and to design for maintainability up front.
  • Develop and manage spare-parts strategy, critical-spares inventory, and vendor/service relationships to support total cost of ownership.
  • Build and manage maintenance KPIs (uptime, MTBF, MTTR, PM compliance, backlog) and provide a regular report-out of reliability performance, blockers, risks, and needs.
  • Be an active participant in and champion of 5S and continuous improvement activities across the maintenance organization.
  • Support capital and equipment planning by providing reliability input, maintainability requirements, and lifecycle cost perspective.
  • Show up every day with extreme urgency and enthusiasm to keep the line running and get the job done.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 3+ years leading or supervising maintenance, reliability, or skilled-trades teams in a manufacturing or industrial environment.
  • Demonstrated hands-on technical depth across mechanical, electrical, pneumatic, hydraulic, and/or controls systems, with proven equipment troubleshooting skills.
  • Experience building and executing preventive and predictive maintenance programs and driving measurable improvements in equipment availability and uptime.
  • Working knowledge of a CMMS / EAM system for work orders, PM scheduling, and asset/spares management.
  • Strong understanding of root-cause analysis and corrective-action methodologies (e.g., 5-Why, FMEA).
  • Experience managing MRO / spare-parts inventory and vendor or service-provider relationships.
  • Solid grasp of workplace safety practices, lockout/tagout, and electrical safety.
  • Can interpret technical documentation — mechanical drawings, electrical schematics, P&IDs, equipment specs, and OEM manuals.
  • Willing and able to work on hardware hands-on and prefer to be on the production floor, adapting easily to a constantly changing environment.
  • Passion for employee development and the process of training and developing both new hires and veteran technicians.
  • Knowledge of 5S, Lean manufacturing, or Six Sigma principles.
  • Proficient with MS Office programs (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Project).
  • Extremely reliable, organized, and detail-oriented with excellent written and verbal communication skills.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Associate’s or Bachelor’s degree in a technical field (engineering, industrial maintenance, or applied science), or equivalent trade/journeyman certification.
  • Experience standing up a maintenance organization or program from the ground up in a new or ramping facility.
  • Lean Six Sigma Green Belt certified.
  • Reliability certifications such as CMRP (Certified Maintenance & Reliability Professional) or CRL.
  • Working knowledge of AS9100 standards and OSHA regulations.
  • Experience with industrial automation, robotics, PLCs, and controls maintenance.
  • Experience maintaining electrical and mechanical assembly and integration equipment.
  • Forklift and hoisting/rigging certification a plus.
  • Experience ramping low-volume manufacturing to high rate.
  • Extensive hiring and organizational design experience.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Senior Manufacturing Engineer to own the recertification and repair operation for our Dive-LD Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) in Quonset, RI. In this role, you will be the process owner for vehicles and major assemblies returning from the field for diagnosis, repair, and recertification, as well as for scheduled refurbishment and overhaul of fielded assets. You will own the repair process from intake through recert test, partner with Design and Sustaining Engineering to close the loop on field failures, and stand up the routings, work instructions, tooling, and test flows needed to scale a depot-level operation alongside a still-maturing production line.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own the end-to-end manufacturing process for recertification, repair, and refurbishment/overhaul of returned AUVs and major subassemblies
  • Lead intake and disposition of field returns: triage incoming units, drive failure analysis with Quality and Design Engineering, and partner with the Material Review Board (MRB) to disposition non-conforming hardware quickly and traceably
  • Develop and maintain repair routings, work instructions, tooling, and inspection criteria specific to the recert/repair line — distinct from new-build flows
  • Define and own the recertification test flow that gates a repaired or overhauled vehicle's return to service, in partnership with Test Engineering and Quality
  • Close the feedback loop to Design and Sustaining Engineering: turn field failure data into prioritized design changes, ECRs, and process improvements
  • Stand up planning, scheduling, and material flows for refurb/overhaul cycles, coordinating with Supply Chain on long-lead spares and obsolescence
  • Apply Lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, or other methodologies to reduce turnaround time, scrap, and rework on the recert/repair line
  • Coordinate with cross-functional teams, including Design, Quality, Supply Chain, Test, and Field Service, to ensure repaired hardware meets the same standards as new production
  • Mentor and support junior engineers and manufacturing technicians working the recert/repair line
  • Stay abreast of technological advancements and industry trends in depot operations, sustainment, and reliability engineering to drive innovation in how we keep the fleet ready

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Degree in a technical field such as engineering, math, or a hard science
  • 5+ years of experience in a relevant field, preferably manufacturing or design of electromechanical hardware

  • Demonstrated technical leadership skills with an expertise in manufacturing
  • Personal experience physically manufacturing hardware via any means (machining, fabrication, soldering, assembly, etc.) Work on personal or extracurricular projects is a plus
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Direct experience standing up or running a recertification, repair, refurbishment, or depot-level operation for complex electromechanical systems
  • Experience leading field return / RMA processes — intake, triage, failure analysis, and disposition of returned hardware
  • Experience developing repair-specific routings, work instructions, and recertification test flows distinct from new-build production
  • Familiarity with sustainment engineering practices: reliability data analysis, root cause / corrective action (RCCA), and closing the loop from field failures back to design
  • Experience coordinating with Field Service or customer support teams on returned assets and warranty repair programs
  • Experience in maritime robotics (AUVs, UUVs, USVs, subsea sensors)
  • Experience working with electrical systems up to 400VDc
  • Prior experience working with JIRA, Siemens NX, Teamcenter (PLM), or Oracle (ERP) or equivalents
  • A strong passion manufacturing and thirst for continuous improvement
  • Experience with large scale high mix manufacturing at different stages of product maturity

The Mission Operations (MOPs) team is responsible for managing the execution, growth, and success of our customer accounts. They work side-by-side with customers to understand their specific problem sets and then shape Anduril’s offerings alongside our engineering teams to fit the mission needs. Because the problems we solve are uniquely challenging, our Mission Operations Engineers naturally gravitate toward finding solutions and are adept at navigating organizational hurdles. Through collaboration with our engineering, logistics, and technical operations teams, Mission Operators are in charge of deploying our products to customer environments, training end-users, and ensuring the high performance of our systems. We are obsessed with engagement and keeping our finger on the pulse of how customers interact with our systems.

Grow your business through programmatic success. You will be responsible for defining, proposing, and executing programmatic and business strategies that drive technology adoption and scale Anduril's footprint within the Army Intelligence community. This requires establishing committed and trust-based partnerships with PMs and acquisition leaders to not only help them solve their immediate problems, but also to foresee future opportunities where Anduril’s technology can make them more effective.

We are looking for a Senior Product Quality Engineer (Low Observable Systems) to support our Fury autonomous aircraft program at our Arsenal 1 facility in Ashville, OH. This role will be on the Quality Engineering Team and partner directly with the Air Dominance and Strike Team, as well as the broader product development, manufacturing, and field operations organizations. ABOUT THE JOB

As a Staff Product Quality Engineer specializing in Low Observable Systems for the Fury program, you will be deeply integrated within the product realization lifecycle. You will define, develop, and execute quality processes that ensure high-performance, reliable, and LO autonomous aircraft components and systems, such as LO structures, LO coatings, integrated antennas, and RF subsystems, meet stringent survivability and mission requirements. This role focuses on collaborating and driving early quality engagement with our LO and RF design teams, as well as manufacturing and test organizations, to achieve our demanding aerospace standards the first time. You will ensure that the design, manufacturing, and testing of Fury's LO/RF features are robust, verifiable, and consistently achieve desired LO characteristics and RF performance. Everything comes down to clarity and action within our specialized LO/RF engineering, production, and test teams, ensuring Fury aircraft are inherently robust, LO, and perform reliably in contested environments. The right person for this role has knowledge of LO principles, RF system engineering, specialized manufacturing processes, advanced metrology for LO characteristics, and continuous improvement methodologies applied to complex aerospace systems. If you are someone who loves to build world-class quality processes for advanced aerospace technology, work hands-on with specialized engineering, and be accountable for critical results, then this role is for you.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Act as the primary quality interface for Low Observable and RF systems within the Fury program, deeply embedding yourself within design, manufacturing, and test teams to proactively influence and integrate quality principles from concept to high-rate production.
  • Partner with LO and RF design teams to review designs and analyses of antennas and LO features, providing critical Design for Manufacturability (DFM), Design for Testability (DFT), Design for Reliability (DFR), and Design for Inspectability (DFI) feedback. Ensure product specifications, drawings, material call-outs, and test requirements are robust and unambiguous for LO and RF performance.
  • Review and approve the decomposition of system requirements for LO/RF, such as link-budget analysis and RCS requirements, ensuring they are measurable, verifiable, and traceable through quality plans.
  • Develop and implement comprehensive Quality Control Plans for the manufacturing, integration, and sustainment of Fury's Low Observable structures, LO coatings, and integrated RF systems, ensuring adherence to specialized materials and processes.
  • Lead the development and implementation of Production Part Approval Process (PPAP) and First Article Inspection (FAI) for specialized LO/RF components and assemblies, ensuring compliance with unique material and geometric requirements.
  • Drive the implementation and continuous improvement of in-process and final product quality controls for LO and RF manufacturing. This includes defining critical process parameters for LO material application, developing Statistical Process Control (SPC) for critical features, and establishing robust inspection and test plans for Fury’s LO/RF elements.
  • Ensure specialized LO/RF manufacturing processes and test capabilities are aligned to the system's performance and reliability requirements for LO and communication.
  • Collaborate closely with the Air Dominance and Strike Low Observable Team, broader Engineering, Manufacturing, and Program Management to ensure predictable product quality for LO/RF features throughout prototyping, production ramp, and sustained production for the Fury autonomous aircraft.
  • Drive manufacturing and product quality readiness by analyzing key and critical characteristics (KCCs/CTQs) from LO/RF designs, developing robust measurement systems (e.g., for RCS, IR, RF performance), and leading internal process and product qualification activities (e.g., capability studies, Gauge R&R, reliability testing, production validation testing) for Fury’s LO/RF systems.
  • Develop, witness, and approve comprehensive test plans and procedures for LO/RF performance, including anechoic chamber testing, near-field/far-field RF measurements, and RCS measurements. Ensure test methodologies are robust, statistically sound, and meet stringent aerospace and LO validation standards.
  • Own the identification and mitigation of manufacturing process and product quality risks specific to LO/RF systems to improve overall quality & reliability across the product lifecycle. Utilize process audits, production readiness reviews, and training & documentation to ensure compliance with LO/RF best practices.
  • Lead Root Cause and Corrective Action (RCCA) and Material Review Board (MRB) activities for in-house manufacturing defects, non-conformances, and field failures related to Fury’s LO/RF product quality. Drive effective containment and corrective actions.
  • Analyze effectiveness of corrective actions and share lessons learned across engineering and production teams for the Fury program, focusing on LO/RF specific issues. Drive internal corrective action and preventive action (CAPA) processes.
  • Audit the Quality Management System within specialized LO/RF manufacturing, test, and assembly operations for Fury, ensuring robust process controls and compliance with internal, customer, and regulatory requirements (e.g., AS9100, MIL-STD-882, relevant LO/RF standards).

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Able to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Top Secret security clearance
  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or other STEM Field
  • 5+ years of Quality Engineering, Manufacturing Quality, or Product Test Engineering experience with a strong focus on RF systems, Low Observable technologies, or other highly specialized aerospace materials/processes.
  • Proficient understanding of RF concepts including aperture antennas, impedance matching, link-budget analysis, and co-site interference, from a quality assurance and test validation perspective.
  • Experience with quality validation of antenna modeling and prediction tools, such such as Computational Electromagnetic (CEM) tools (HFSS, CST Microwave Studio, SENTRi, ADS, FEKO).
  • Proficient in quality assurance of specialized antenna measurement techniques including anechoic chamber, near field/far field RF measurements, and RCS measurements.
  • Experience in developing quality control plans for the manufacturing and integration of LO/RF components, including specialized material handling and application.
  • Working knowledge of AS9100/ISO 9001-based Quality Management System requirements, particularly pertaining to design, manufacturing, inspection, and test in aerospace. Lead / Internal Auditor Certification is a plus.
  • Working knowledge of product development and manufacturing methodologies such as Design Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (DFMEA), Process Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (PFMEA), Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP), Production Part Approval Process (PPAP), Measurement Systems Analysis (MSA), statistical process control (SPC), and Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T).
  • A strong ownership mindset with demonstrated capability to drive projects from start to completion in a fast-paced, high-stakes environment.
  • Analytical skills and experiences for data mining, data quality, metrics generation, issue management systems, and statistical analysis tools (MatLab, JMP, MiniTab, etc) applied to LO/RF performance data.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Top Secret security clearance
  • Master’s degree in a technical field related to RF, LO, or Quality Engineering.
  • Experience with quality assurance of LO apertures, phased array designs, RF front-ends, and their associated testing.
  • Understanding of LO aircraft sustainment and maintainability challenges from a quality perspective.
  • Experience with government contracts and auditing standard requirements related to advanced aerospace production and quality assurance.
  • Knowledge of aerospace certification processes (e.g., FAA Part 21/23/25, AS9145).
  • Competence with test equipment such as oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, network analyzers, signal generators, thermal chambers, and automation of tests for LO/RF products.
  • Experience with Teamcenter, SolidWorks, Oracle/Netsuite, Jira, Tableau, Foundry, Altium are preferred, Eagle and others acceptable.
  • Ability to work in a fast paced, autonomously driven, and demanding environment.

We are looking for a Senior Recruiter to join our rapidly growing team in Costa Mesa, CA, Seattle, WA, Boston, MA or Washington, DC. In this role, you will be responsible for owning the Recruiting for Recruiting function.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The LatticeOS Team builds the foundational software-defined operating system that powers our family of autonomous systems, sensors, and third-party integrations. Our work spans edge devices, robotic platforms, and cloud infrastructure, creating a unified operating environment for system orchestration, secure data distribution, and real-time execution. As a core engineering capability, LatticeOS directly enables mission-critical operations across all domains, powering both internal products and external developer partners integrating through the Lattice SDK. Our solutions are designed for real-world deployment in the most demanding operational environments, where reliable middleware, high availability, and seamless hardware-software integration make the difference between mission success and failure.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join the LatticeOS team, where you will design and develop the core platform services, middleware, and operating system components running onboard autonomous vehicles and edge devices. You will collaborate closely with hardware, autonomy, and application teams to create a highly reliable, performant, and secure platform that abstracts complex hardware and networking into clean software interfaces. If you are someone who is self-motivated, holds yourself to high standards, and thrives in a low-structure, high-autonomy environment, then this role is for you.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Design and implement core components and middleware for LatticeOS running onboard autonomous vehicles and edge devices.
  • Develop robust, fault-tolerant distributed systems that can operate reliably over denied, degraded, or intermittent communications links.
  • Create interfaces, APIs, and tooling that enable internal teams and third-party partners to integrate seamlessly with LatticeOS through the Lattice SDK.
  • Collaborate with autonomy and hardware teams to ensure diverse physical platforms can reliably run and interact with the core operating system.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a relevant field, or equivalent experience.
  • 5+ years of professional software development experience, with a focus on systems programming, distributed systems, or robotics.
  • Deep experience with C++, Rust, or similar systems programming languages.
  • Proficiency with protocol design, serialization, and implementation (e.g., gRPC, Protobuf, Zenoh, DDS).
  • Experience building software solutions involving high-throughput data processing, transport, or system orchestration.
  • Excellent collaboration skills and the ability to work across multiple cross-functional engineering teams.
  • A desire to work on critical infrastructure software that has a real-world impact.
  • US Persons: Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience developing operating systems, middleware, SDKs, or developer platforms.
  • Background in developing systems for defense, aerospace, robotics, or other mission-critical applications.
  • Familiarity with software development for embedded systems, Linux internals, or resource-constrained environments.
  • Strong understanding of distributed communication networks, routing, and modern messaging standards.

Ensuring we deliver high quality, trustable products is table stakes. ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril Imaging builds electro-optical and infrared sensor systems that go on Anduril platforms as well as our own stand-alone products. The hardware is precision optics, cooled infrared detectors, custom electronics, and tight-tolerance electromechanical assemblies. Several products are moving from development into rate production at the same time.

ABOUT THE JOB

Senior Sourcing Engineer owns the supply chain outcomes behind those products. The team is small and growing. You will own supplier relationships end to end, from identifying a source and negotiating the agreement to standing up capacity and holding it through a ramp.

This role requires deep understanding of areas in infrared optics and the materials behind them. Germanium crystal, boules, and blanks. Chalcogenide infrared glass. Lens and window fabrication, grinding, polishing, diamond turning, and centering as well as optical coatings. Lens cell assemblies and related optical assemblies. Detector and dewar assemblies, cold filters, and cryocoolers.

This commodity carries additional exposure. Germanium pricing and availability are driven by export policy and a thin upstream supply base, and the alternative material paths carry their own critical mineral dependencies. The work includes reaching past tier one into the feedstock layer, modeling material price scenarios, and structuring forward positions and consignment arrangements that secure supply rather than just placing orders.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own suppliers end to end. Identify and select sources, run requests for quote, drive input to make-buy decisions, and serve as the commercial and technical owner of the relationship. Supplier signals currently reach Anduril through several uncoordinated paths. You will be the conduit that keeps them consistent across programs.
  • Negotiate the commercial structure. Draft and negotiate pricing, capacity commitments, lead times, payment, warranty, and service terms. Build toward long-term agreements where they secure capacity. Sequence leverage deliberately so commitments buy terms rather than just parts.
  • Build the cost model, then use it. Develop should-cost and clean-sheet models, run cost-breakdown analysis on quotes, and drive total cost of ownership across the lifecycle. Reconcile bill of material cost against finance so product cost reflects what the parts actually cost.
  • Secure capacity ahead of ramp. Map supply network lead time and flexibility, place coverage against demand well before it is needed, and resolve capacity gaps before they become schedule problems. Suppliers in this space book out far in advance. The job is to be early.
  • Engage engineering before the design locks. Give design for manufacturability feedback, influence specifications using supply intelligence on availability, lead time, and lifecycle health, so design decisions account for supply reality instead of discovering it.
  • De-risk the bill of material. Complete risk assessments, qualify alternates and second sources, drive commonality and supplier rationalization, and manage obsolescence before it gates a build.
  • Escalate and clear blockers. Participate in program reviews and operational escalation forums. Triage supply disruptions, resolve shortages, and drive supplier issues to conclusion, including executive escalation when it is warranted.
  • Carry compliance into the sourcing decision. Work country of origin, domestic content, defense acquisition regulation, export control, and rated order requirements into supplier selection and purchase order structure. The point is to engineer compliance into the design and supply decision rather than remediate it later.
  • Complete supplier qualification. Own the capability and authorization portions of supplier evaluation and coordinate with the Supplier Quality Organization.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, supply chain, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience
  • 8 or more years across sourcing engineering, commodity management, supplier development, supplier quality, manufacturing engineering, or cost engineering
  • Experience owning supplier relationships that included both technical assessment and commercial negotiation
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings and CAD model and assemblies.
  • Ability to travel a 10-25% of the time for vendor on-site visits
  • Eligible to access export-controlled technical data under United States export control law
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. secret clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Advanced technical degree
  • Experience in infrared or electro-optical systems, precision optics, photonics, sensors, or other high-precision hardware
  • Should-cost or clean-sheet cost modeling, design-to-cost, or value engineering work
  • Experience taking a product from development into rate production, particularly in high-mix low-volume environments
  • Experience negotiating long-term agreements, supply agreements, or capacity commitments
  • Familiarity with defense acquisition regulation flowdowns, export control, rated orders, country of origin, or domestic content requirements
  • Experience in a fast-moving company where the process was still being built

About the Team

The Technology Security and Foreign Disclosure (TSFD) team determines whether Anduril's capabilities can be exported, to whom, and on what authority. We secure the approvals that turn a product into a releasable product: Low Observable and Counter-Low Observable Tri-Service Committee decision memoranda, Critical Program Information assessments, service export baselines, and the disclosure policy that governs what may be said to a partner nation and when.

We work across every business line and every service. Our counterparts are SAF/IA, NIPO, DTSA, DASA DE&C, the program executive offices, and the security assistance enterprise. We partner daily with International Trade Compliance on licensing, and with Global Defense capture teams whose pursuits depend on the approvals we obtain. When exportability is the constraint on a campaign, we are the path off it.

About the Job

This role owns the systems engineering product description and performance review supporting OUSW technology release. You will run the assessment and approval pipeline end to end: scoping product reviews, assembling the artifacts and stakeholders, driving classified assessments to a signed decision, and tracking every open action to closure across dozens of concurrent capabilities and partner nations.

You will navigate complex Technology Security and Foreign Disclosure (TSFD) pipelines, the Low Observable/Counter-Low Observable Tri-Services Committee (LO/CLO TSC), and Anti-Tamper (AT) frameworks to enable Foreign Military Sales (FMS) and Direct Commercial Sales (DCS).

What You'll Do

  • Collaborate and interface with the Anduril Global Defense TSFD and International Trade Compliance teams to serve as an engineering focal point navigating Technology Security and Foreign Disclosure (TSFD) pipes and approval processes across the military departments and joint agencies.

  • Build the repeatable process, templates, and artifact standards that shorten time from assessment request to approval as the number of capabilities under review grows.

ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril is seeking a Senior Technical Program Manager to lead development and delivery of Sentry Fixed Site Systems. In this role, you will own technical planning and cross-functional execution for integrated fixed-site products, driving alignment across subsystem teams, platform teams, manufacturing, field operations, product management, and business line stakeholders. You will be responsible for ensuring complex hardware and software subsystems mature into complete, deployable systems that meet customer needs, technical requirements, schedule commitments, and manufacturing readiness expectations.

Success in this role hinges on three key facets:

ABOUT THE TEAM

Our Technical Revenue Accounting team is at the forefront of Anduril’s rapid growth, ensuring the accuracy and integrity of our financial reporting as we scale globally. We are searching for an analytical and forward-thinking Senior Technical Revenue Accountant to join us and support our evolving deal review processes.

ABOUT THE JOB

Reporting to the Manager of Technical Revenue Accounting, you will ensure the consistent and compliant application of ASC 606, lead detailed contract reviews, and author high-quality technical documentation. The ideal candidate will bring deep technical competency, strong cross-functional communication skills, and a passion for challenging the status quo to design innovative accounting solutions.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Lead Contract Reviews: Analyze complex, multi-element arrangements and prepare ASC 606 checklists to document Anduril’s technical accounting conclusions for point-in-time and over-time revenue recognition.
  • Establish Fair Value: Support, calculate, and maintain Standalone Selling Price (SSP) and fair value determinations for our cutting-edge product and service offerings.
  • Partner Cross-Functionally: Collaborate with key partners across Finance, Program Management, Contract Management, Legal, Order Management, and Proposals to streamline and support contract accounting operations.
  • Technical Research & Guidance: Research ASC 606 codification for highly complex revenue scenarios to deliver expert guidance on deal structuring and author comprehensive technical accounting memos.
  • Manage Audits: Liaise directly with external auditors, proactively managing requests and providing clear and well-supported documentation for complex transactions.
  • Drive Process Innovation: Identify and implement process improvements and automation within the revenue accounting cycle to drive efficiency and support Anduril’s rapid growth.
  • Month-End Close: Prepare and review complex journal entries and balance sheet reconciliations to support a timely and accurate month-end close.
  • Controls & Compliance: Assist in the formulation, implementation, and testing of internal controls, policies, and procedures in compliance with SOX, GAAP, and IPO readiness.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.
  • 3+ years of progressive experience in technical accounting with a strong, working application of ASC 606.
  • Demonstrated experience with government contracting, including Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF), Time & Materials (T&M), and Cost Reimbursable (CR) contracts, is highly desirable.
  • Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to translate complex technical accounting concepts into clear, actionable advice for non-finance stakeholders.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Slack is a plus.
  • Hands-on experience with a large-scale ERP system (e.g., Oracle, SAP) and its Project Accounting functionalities. Experience with Oracle Fusion Cloud and Salesforce is strongly preferred.
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities.

ABOUT THE JOB

Frontier AI is looking for a backend software engineer to own and evolve our internal LLM agent framework. This role sits at the intersection of backend infrastructure, applied AI, agent architecture, model post-training, and evaluation tooling. You will build the platform that enables teams across Anduril to develop, evaluate, and deploy reliable LLM agents in mission-critical environments.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own Anduril’s internal LLM agent framework, including core abstractions, runtime architecture, developer experience, integrations, and reliability.
  • Support multiple business lines building LLM agents by providing new framework capabilities, implementation guidance, architectural reviews, and best-practice patterns.
  • Partner with machine learning teams to make model post-training workflows easy to integrate, ranging from supervised fine-tuning to offline RL, online RL, and environment-driven agent improvement.
  • Design tooling that supports modern agent patterns, including structured tool calling, filesystem-using agents, memory and retrieval, planning loops, subagents, agent graphs, and human-in-the-loop workflows.
  • Work with partner teams to define comprehensive evaluation suites that measure task success, tool-call correctness, trajectory quality, robustness, regressions, and deployment readiness.
  • Stay current on emerging agent architecture and evaluation trends, and make pragmatic decisions about which techniques should or should not be adopted internally.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Strong backend engineering experience building production-quality platforms, frameworks, APIs, or infrastructure used by other engineers.
  • Deep expertise in LLM agent framework design, including the tradeoffs between different orchestration patterns such as linear agents, graph-based agents, multi-agent systems, planner/executor loops, and tool-heavy agents.
  • Experience designing agent evaluation paradigms, including trajectory evaluations, LLM-as-judge workflows, task-success metrics, tool-call correctness checks, rubric-based qualitative grading, adversarial scenario testing, regression eval suites, and human-in-the-loop review.
  • Familiarity with model post-training workflows such as SFT, preference tuning, reinforcement learning, and environment-based agent training.
  • Strong judgment around reliability, observability, debugging, and safety for LLM applications deployed in high-stakes settings.
  • Ability to work directly with partner teams, understand ambiguous product needs, and turn them into reusable platform capabilities.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with agent frameworks like Langchain Deepagents, Claude SDK, etc.
  • Experience building evaluation platforms, simulation environments, benchmark suites, or agent test harnesses.
  • Experience with Kubernetes, Docker, distributed systems, workflow orchestration, or ML infrastructure.
  • Familiarity with defense, robotics, command-and-control systems, autonomy, or operational planning domains.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Staff Technical Program Engineer on the Cross Domain Solutions (CDS) Integration team, you will own the delivery and accreditation of capabilities that allow Lattice to operate securely across classification boundaries. Sitting at the nexus of engineering, vendors, and government authorizing officials, you will navigate complex technical and compliance hurdles to deliver secure, real-time data flows to warfighters in the field.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Drive end-to-end delivery. Own the execution roadmap for integrating Lattice across security domains, ensuring solutions are delivered on time, within scope, and aligned with operational requirements.

  • Drive disciplined engineering standards. Institute and maintain rigorous engineering, validation, and fielding processes so that deployed solutions are resilient, repeatable, and maintainable in real-world operational environments.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Possess and maintain an active U.S. Top Secret clearance with SCI eligibility (TS/SCI).
  • Demonstrated track record as a Senior or Staff Technical Program Manager, Systems Engineer, or Security Engineer delivering complex IT, networking, or cybersecurity solutions.
  • Foundational understanding of computer and network security principles, cybersecurity architectures, threat modeling, and/or defense-in-depth strategies.
  • Experience navigating U.S. Government security compliance frameworks (e.g., Risk Management Framework [RMF], NIST SP 800-53, DoDI 8510.01, ICD 503) and driving systems through the ATO process.
  • Demonstrated experience managing cross-functional execution across distributed software engineering, infrastructure, and test teams.
  • Proven ability to manage technical vendor partnerships, evaluate third-party technologies, and hold external partners accountable to technical milestones.
  • Excellent technical communication skills, with the ability to bridge conversations between low-level software engineers, operational military personnel, and senior government authorization authorities.

  • Experience building, integrating, testing, or authorizing Cross Domain Solutions (CDS) or Multi-Level Security (MLS) architectures within DoD or Intelligence Community (IC) environments.
  • Familiarity with National Cross Domain Strategy and Management Office (NCDSMO) requirements and CDS lifecycle processes (Raise-the-Bar standards).
  • Experience navigating international export controls, ITAR, and EAR compliance in the context of defense software and security platforms.
  • Background in distributed systems, secure cloud environments, and tactical network integration.

The Sentry Platform Technologies team develops the common hardware and software capabilities that power the Sentry product family. These foundational technologies include pan-tilt units, compute, power systems, communications, platform software, and other shared capabilities that enable rapid development of autonomous systems across Counter-Intrusion, Air Defense, Maritime, and future mission areas. By investing in common platform technologies, the team accelerates product development, improves reliability and manufacturability, reduces lifecycle cost, and enables scalable solutions that can be leveraged across multiple products and business lines.

ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril is seeking a Staff Technical Program Manager to lead development of Sentry Platform Technologies. Rather than owning a single customer-facing product, you’ll drive development of the shared hardware and software capabilities that serve as the technical foundation of the Sentry product family. You’ll partner closely with Product Management, the Lead Platform Architect, Chief Engineers, and engineering teams across Counter-Intrusion, Air Defense, Maritime, and other business lines to evolve common platform capabilities that support a diverse set of mission requirements. In this role, you’ll own technical planning and cross-functional execution from concept through prototype development, system integration, qualification, manufacturing readiness, production, and adoption across multiple products. Success requires balancing the needs of multiple engineering teams and business lines while developing scalable, reusable technologies that accelerate product development across the Sentry portfolio.

Success in this role hinges on three key facets:

  • Platform mindset — understanding how common technologies can be developed once and leveraged across multiple products, reducing duplication while improving scalability and long-term maintainability.
  • Technical execution — driving complex hardware and software development efforts from concept through production while managing technical risk, dependencies, and cross-functional execution.
  • Cross-functional leadership — partnering across Product Management, Platform Architecture, Engineering, Manufacturing, and business line leadership to align shared technology investments with evolving mission needs.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Lead technical execution for shared Sentry platform technologies, including pan-tilt units, compute, power systems, communications, platform software, and other foundational hardware and software capabilities.
  • Drive development from concept through prototype builds, integration, validation, qualification, manufacturing readiness, production, and adoption across multiple Sentry products.
  • Partner closely with Product Managers, the Lead Platform Architect, Chief Engineers, and business line stakeholders to align shared platform capabilities with product roadmaps and mission requirements.
  • Collaborate with Fixed Site Systems and Maneuver Systems TPMs to synchronize platform roadmaps with integrated product milestones.
  • Coordinate execution across Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Software Engineering, Systems Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Quality, Reliability, Test, Product Management, and Platform Architecture teams.
  • Drive standardization, modularity, and reuse of common technologies across the Sentry product family.
  • Identify technical and programmatic risks early, develop mitigation strategies, and drive alignment across engineering organizations.

  • Communicate roadmap status, technical decisions, program health, risks, and dependencies to engineering and executive leadership.

As a Federal Materials Supervisor, you will create a strategic plan to optimize warehouse operations in strict compliance with federal regulations, create a standard set of metrics to monitor team performance, set goals for improving performance, and identify areas to reduce cost while maintaining quality and audit readiness. The right person for this role has extensive defense supply chain knowledge, has developed SOPs and implemented them under FAR/DFARS guidelines, has implemented or improved ERP/WMS with government property tracking integrations, and has a proven track record of managing expensive, federally owned inventory. If you are someone who can operate autonomously to keep a warehouse team motivated, excel under rigorous audit standards, and enjoys process improvement, this may be the role for you.

 

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

  • Develop and implement material management strategies, policies, and procedures to comply with federal regulations, including FAR 52.245-1 (Government Property) and DFARS clauses 
    • Hiring & training talent who can manage material flow per Anduril guidelines.
    • Develop processes that increase the efficiency (speed & elimination of waste) and effectiveness of Anduril materials management. 
    • Implement necessary systems that match Anduril Federal policies on management of government property & inventory management. 
  • Implement End-to-End material management measures, including FIFO adherence, material variances, cycle time optimization, scrap/obsolescence/disposal management (via PCARSS/eTools), cycle/physical counting, and DCMA/internal audits, to ensure 100% inventory accuracy and mitigate stockouts or overstocking. This includes the development & improvement of critical compliance metrics.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including procurement, Government Property Administrators, production, manufacturing engineering, logistics, and quality, to aid in accurate demand forecasting, procurement planning, and timely delivery of materials.
  • Collaborate with production planning and manufacturing teams to align material availability with production schedules, minimize disruptions, and meet federal contract and customer demand on time.
  • Analyze material usage trends, identify opportunities for process improvements, and implement lean practices to optimize material handling, storage, and secure distribution.
  • Utilize ERP, WMS, and federal registry software systems (such as PIEE/WAWF) to track inventory, generate reports, and provide data-driven insights to support decision-making and optimize material-related processes.
  • Ensure strict compliance with regulatory requirements (including ITAR/EAR), safety standards (OSHA), and quality control protocols (AS9100) in all material management and shipping/receiving activities.
  • Lead and develop a high-performing warehouse team, providing guidance, training, and performance feedback to foster a culture of compliant operational excellence and continuous improvement.

 

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor's degree in supply chain management, logistics, business administration, or equivalent work experience

  • 3+ years of experience in material management, inventory control, or supply chain management roles in an aerospace and/or defense manufacturing environment operating under federal regulations (FAR/DFARS)

  • 1+ years of experience managing a lead of supervisors, associates, or technicians

  • Familiarity with Government-Furnished Property (GFP) administration and FAR Part 45/52.245-1 requirements

  • Ability to obtain and maintain a US Government Security Clearance

  • Ability to be onsite, local to Santa Ana, CA or Costa Mesa, CA

 

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Associate’s or Bachelor’s degree in supply chain, manufacturing, or related operations field
  • National Property Management Association (NPMA) certification (CPPS, CPPA, or CPPM)
  • Direct experience preparing for and passing DCMA Government Property Management System Audits (PMSAs)
  • Strong understanding of production rate, critical path analysis, and key warehouse fundamentals
  • Strong understanding of receiving and deployment documentation for domestic and international shipments, including ITAR/EAR export compliance and DD250 processing
  • Ability to identify safety issues with warehouse vehicles to ensure safe operations
  • Strong knowledge of AS9100 standards, FIAR compliance, and OSHA laws
  • Experience being hands-on and boots on the ground in the warehouse with proven skills in both process and equipment troubleshooting, and the ability to adapt to constantly changing defense manufacturing environments
  • Passion for employee development and enjoy the process of training and developing both new hires and veteran warehouse staff in a highly regulated environment
  • Experience supporting process development and implementing new processes (specifically transitioning from manual tracking to automated systems of record)
  • Experience supporting warehouse equipment maintenance and safety compliance
  • Knowledge of 5S, lean manufacturing, or 6-Sigma principles
  • Proficient with computer use (standard browser, ERPs like Deltek Costpoint or SAP, and PIEE/WAWF portals) and the ability to present data
  • Experience in ramping low-volume operations to high-rate military production
  • Reliable, organized, and detail-oriented with excellent verbal & written communication skills
  • Forklift certification
