The team brings together Roadrunner, Sentry, Anvil, Pulsar, and Wisp with existing and third-party sensors and effectors through Lattice, creating a software-enabled family of systems for the modern battlespace. As control of the air becomes more contested, these networked capabilities give warfighters the awareness and response options needed to protect forces against rapidly evolving UAS threats.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are hiring a Systems Engineer for Anduril's air defense work with the U.S. Army. The portfolio fields counter-UAS systems that bring together Pulsar, Wisp, and other Anduril and third-party sensors, effectors, and communications, and they have to work wherever the Army needs them. Some are deployable systems, held ready and set up on short notice at a site the customer chooses. You will start on one of those, taking it from requirements and design reviews through integration, validation with the government, and sustainment, and your scope will follow where the portfolio needs engineering over time.

You own a defined part of the system's technical scope and the evidence that it works, inside a technical baseline set by the portfolio's technical lead. In practice that means requirements and verification, integration and calibration, the procedures and training material field teams depend on, and engineering support once the system is fielded.
The role is hands-on. You will spend real time with the hardware: configuring and integrating it, running calibration and test at the range, diagnosing problems from logs and data, and traveling to the site when a problem needs someone at the equipment. Fielded systems often have to work with no engineer on site, so much of the job is making sure the procedures and configurations you write hold up in someone else's hands.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Own requirements and verification for your scope. Write and maintain the requirements and verification records, tie each requirement to a test, and produce and defend your portion of formal design reviews. Present your results in customer and program reviews.

Integrate, calibrate, and test the hardware. Configure and integrate systems before they ship, and run them through burn-in, calibration, and test at the range. Keep interface documentation matched to what the hardware actually does.

Equip the people who run it. Write the site requirements, setup and calibration procedures, checklists, and training content that field teams and operators use. Keep fielded systems ready through maintenance, software updates, and configuration tracking, so what deploys matches what was validated.

Support the system in the field. Root-cause issues from logs and data, lead technical recovery for your scope, and travel to the site when the problem needs hands on the equipment. Bring what you learn back to the product teams that can fix it.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Engineering, science, or other technical degree, or equivalent practical experience
  • 4+ years of systems engineering or related engineering experience on hardware and software systems
  • Ownership of a subsystem, interface, or other defined technical scope through verification and fielding, with accountability for whether it actually worked, not only for its design artifacts
  • Ability to explain the architecture and interfaces of a subsystem you owned, and a record of keeping interface documentation consistent with observed behavior
  • Ability to turn a defined scope into clear requirements and verification steps, then plan and run the test that shows it works
  • Experience debugging on real hardware and real data, including root-causing field issues with limited supervision
  • Experience presenting your own results to a technical working group or customer, and producing your portion of a formal design review
  • Willingness to travel up to 25% of the time on average, with periods of up to 50% during test events and deployments
  • Eligibility to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Active U.S. Secret security clearance
  • Experience with deployable or expeditionary systems that are set up, calibrated, and torn down in the field
  • Experience writing procedures, checklists, or training material that operators or technicians executed successfully without you present
  • Depth in at least one of: radar, passive RF detection, electro-optical and infrared sensors, tactical radios and networking, or command and control software
  • Experience sustaining equipment held in reserve or storage, including preventive maintenance, software currency, and battery health
  • Experience developing and executing the Risk Management Framework (RMF) process to achieve and maintain an Authority to Operate (ATO) for a fielded system
  • Experience delivering counter-UAS, air defense, or force protection capability to a U.S. Army customer
  • Comfort on the Linux command line, and with Python for parsing and visualizing test data
  • Prior military service, particularly in Army air defense or an expeditionary unit

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Seabed Sentry team is responsible for Maritime Domain Awareness providing subsea autonomous sensing and communication across critical commercial and defense mission sets. You'll operate in a fast-paced environment where small empowered teams move with urgency to deliver cutting-edge maritime capabilities from concept to deployment in months, not years. ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril Industries is seeking our next Technical Program Manager to lead international deployment execution for a maritime undersea domain awareness program. This role sits at the intersection of engineering, program management, and customer delivery — you will own the end-to-end execution of international demonstrations and system deployments, from planning through on-site execution. You will be the connective tissue between product teams, engineering, operations, business development, and international customers. This is not a role where you manage from a distance — you will be in the details, in the room with the customer, and accountable for delivery. Our next Technical Program Manager is the person who is energized by complexity, who builds trust with customers through competence and follow-through, and seeks to put order to chaos.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own planning, scheduling, and execution of international system deployments and demonstrations for undersea domain awareness capabilities
  • Build and maintain program schedules in Jira, ensuring milestones, dependencies, and critical path items are current and visible to all stakeholders
  • Develop and maintain milestone trackers, risk registers, and action item burndowns across multiple concurrent workstreams
  • Drive technical alignment across hardware, software, and systems engineering teams to ensure deployment-ready configurations meet customer requirements
  • Prepare and deliver technical briefings and program status reviews to international customers, senior leadership, and cross-functional stakeholders
  • Coordinate logistics for international hardware shipments including export compliance, temporary import/permanent export documentation, and customs coordination
  • Identify and manage risks and dependencies across engineering, supply chain, compliance, and operations — escalate early and with proposed mitigations
  • Translate customer requirements into actionable engineering tasking and ensure product teams understand the operational context behind what they're building
  • Keep Jira updated as the single source of truth for schedule status — ensure sprint planning, epic tracking, and program milestones reflect reality, not aspirations
  • Drive alignment across stakeholders who don't always agree — get decisions made, documented, and executed
  • Support contract amendment processes, milestone payment tracking, and deliverable acceptance with the customer
  • Document product baselines, configuration states, and deployment readiness criteria in Confluence
  • Operate as the single point of accountability for deployment readiness — if something isn't tracking, you own the recovery plan

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 5+ years of technical program management experience, preferably in defense, maritime, or aerospace
  • Demonstrated ability to manage international customer engagements and deployments in high-stakes environments
  • Strong technical foundation — able to go deep on systems architecture, integration challenges, and hardware/software trade-offs without relying on engineering to translate for you
  • Experience building and presenting technical briefings to senior military and government stakeholders
  • Track record of managing complex, multi-team schedules with interdependent milestones and hard deadlines
  • Proficiency in Jira for program scheduling, sprint management, and milestone tracking — you treat the tool as a real-time reflection of program health, not an administrative chore
  • Exceptional organizational skills — you are the person who tracks every action item, every dependency, every open risk, and doesn't let things fall through
  • Comfort operating in ambiguity and high-pressure situations where the plan is changing and decisions have real consequences
  • Experience with export control processes (ITAR/EAR) and international logistics
  • Familiarity with DoD acquisition processes, contract structures (FFP, T&M, CPFF), and milestone-based deliverables
  • Ability to travel internationally up to 25%-40%, including extended deployments for demonstrations
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience in undersea warfare, autonomous systems, or maritime ISR programs
  • Background in systems engineering or test & evaluation
  • Experience working with Indo-Pacific partner nations
  • Experience with Confluence for documentation and product baseline management
  • Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Maritime Services Team is responsible for collecting seabed survey and exploration data for commercial and government customers worldwide. Today, we are simultaneously delivering services and capability, while helping invent advanced large-scale autonomous solutions for tomorrow.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Technical Program Manager to join our rapidly growing team in Quincy, MA. Make no mistake — this is a diverse role that requires an agile manager comfortable with operating in a chaotic environment, not just a schedule-and-Gantt PM. In this role, you will be responsible for planning and execution of survey projects, informing the design of survey plans, driving development and test plans for new capabilities, and supporting business development activities as both external advocate and internal "voice of the customer". This requires someone with a robust set of of offshore experiences, precise project management and contracting knowhow, outstanding communication skills, and the ability to work in a high velocity environment. If you want to merge the most advanced hardware and software imaginable to rewrite the book on seabed exploration, then this role is for you. We don't do bureaucracy here - if you'd rather write a status report than solve the problem in front of you, this isn't your team.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Project Planning: Plan and coordinate multiple concurrent commercial and government AUV survey projects, including resource demand planning, scheduling, and logistics. Develop project scope and manage changes through the life of the project. Identify, track, and manage risks. Generate and maintain project schedules, including identifying required resourcing and assets. Work with customers to define project objectives, deliverables, and timelines. Partner with Field Operations to identify resourcing, assets, vessels, and required support equipment and services.
  • Data Processing: Review customer data requirements and expectations, mapping them to current and future system capabilities. Support generation of post mission analysis data products, quality controls, and standardized workflows to meet project requirements.
  • Contract Management: Provide contract management support including drafting and reviewing statements of work, change orders, financial management, terms and conditions, data rights assertions, etc. Manage deliverables, including routine status updates and final data delivery to the customer.
  • Test Event Execution: Support the Engineering team in integration, testing, and debug in a high-paced environment. Participate in formal testing efforts by identifying resources needed, tracking cost and schedule during workup testing and execution, and supporting mobilization logistics. Serve as customer PoC and interface during testing and funded work, providing clear and concise status, reporting on risks, and progress against required data deliverables
  • Growth Support: Interface across the spectrum of survey stakeholders and customers, and be able to represent the technical aspects of the Anduril Maritime portfolio. Serve as the “voice of the customer” for follow-on business capture efforts and activities, ensuring customer needs and requirements are clearly articulated to product and engineering teams while supporting proposal generation, identification of new work, and prioritization of new capabilities. Act as a champion for customers across geophysical survey applications, including exploration and surveys for deep sea minerals, oil and gas, telecom, etc.
  • Autonomous Execution: Default to action: autonomously execute on broad and/or ambiguous requirements from external customers. Show a proven ability to work across the ambiguity to refine and capture key outcomes and deliverables for each individual project. Demonstrate high ownership on all pieces of work. Become a trusted partner across multiple teams in Anduril Maritime, including Engineering, Products, Operations, and Field Test Engineering.
  • Travel to support customer meetings and operations approximately 25-40% of the time.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor of Science degree in systems engineering, renewable energy, ocean engineering, or a related field, as well as a demonstrated passion for hydrographic survey
  • 5+ years of project management, technical management, or offshore party chief experience, specifically in robotics or hydrographic survey
  • Technical background in geophysical data acquisition, processing, and deliverable generation
  • High ownership and proven ability to lead a multi-disciplinary team to a common outcome
  • Extremely organized and detail oriented
  • Excellent communication skills
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience operating robotic systems offshore
  • Experience with development and integration of subsea sensors.
  • Experience in deep ocean exploration
  • Experience with international and commercial customers

ABOUT THE JOB
We are seeking a Technical Recruiter or Sourcer to drive the hiring strategy for our hardware teams within the Air Dominance and Strike division.  This person will operate independently as a subject matter expert, ensuring we recruit top-tier hardware talent and shape our long-term talent strategy.
 
Per Anduril's expansion plans, we anticipate this job will be based out of Long Beach, CA beginning late 2027. Until then, this role will be based out of Costa Mesa, CA.

WHAT YOU’LL DO
  • Operate Autonomously: Serve as a trusted talent advisor for complex hiring projects across the division.
  • Develop and optimize recruiting strategies using prospecting techniques, tools, and automation to continuously improve candidate management and data extraction processes.
  • Collaborate closely with the talent acquisition team, hiring managers, and senior leadership to shape recruitment strategy, guide process improvements, and drive high-impact, complex hiring projects.
  • Advise on workforce planning through regular strategic updates and business reviews.
  • Act as a subject matter expert using tools like Greenhouse, LinkedIn Recruiter, Gem, and email to engage passive candidates and conduct initial interviews, ensuring high interview-to-offer ratios by anticipating hiring manager preferences.
  • Build talent maps and leverage market intelligence to adapt hiring strategies in response to competitor movements and emerging trends.

  • Influence and elevate recruitment best practices, ensuring a consistent and exceptional candidate experience while continually driving process efficiency and quality across high-stakes projects.

  • 5+ years of experience in talent acquisition, preferably in executive search and divisional hiring.
  • Proven ability to convey complex information in simple terms and drive a data-driven narrative.
  • Demonstrated leadership in ambiguous, fast-paced environments with a focus on strategic stakeholder alignment.
  • Strong cross-functional collaboration skills and a track record of influencing organizational best practices.
  • Deep knowledge of recruitment technology and a passion for innovating processes to achieve creative and effective TA goals.
  • Must be eligible to obtain and maintain a DoD Security Clearance.
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
  • Experience in startups, tech, and relevant hardware domains (Autonomous Vehicles, Aerospace, Robotics, etc.).

We’re looking for an engineer to lead the optimization of OpenAI’s state-of-the-art frontier models on TPUs. You will own performance across the full forward pass, from model code through kernels to execution on the hardware.

About the team

Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) builds compliance programs and provides assurance for OpenAI’s technology, people, and products. We combine technical understanding with practical operations to reduce risk, support product and research teams, and produce reliable evidence of how our controls work.

About the role

As a Regulatory Compliance Program Manager, you will build and operate programs that turn regulatory requirements into clear responsibilities, effective processes, and evidence that can withstand external scrutiny.

Your work will focus on AI safety/security and content moderation, with privacy operations as an adjacent area. You will partner with Legal and the teams that build and operate our products to scope the work, maintain accurate control narratives, prepare regulatory responses, and lead external assessments for your assigned portfolio.

You should be comfortable owning delivery, explaining tradeoffs, and changing your recommendation when the evidence changes. Success means controls have accountable owners, evidence stays current, and teams can respond accurately without repeatedly rebuilding the same work. The initial portfolio and expectations will be agreed with the hiring manager.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead an agreed portfolio of AI safety/security and content-compliance work, including programs associated with the EU AI Act, DSA, OSA, and SB 53, with Legal and relevant experts confirming applicable requirements.

  • Translate requirements into scoped programs, operating processes, control and evidence responsibilities, milestones, and clear escalation paths.

  • Build and maintain accurate control narratives and traceable evidence for regulatory requests, reporting, audits, and assessments.

  • Lead preparation and delivery for external compliance assessments, coordinate the responsible teams, and track gaps through verified resolution or an explicitly owned decision.

  • Prioritize the work that materially improves compliance outcomes and reduces risk; explain what should proceed, change, or wait and why.

  • Develop evidence-backed recommendations with Legal, Product, Security, Safety, Integrity, Privacy, and other functional teams. Obtain decisions from the authorized owners for legal interpretation, external representations, and risk acceptance.

  • Improve operational workflows for content and privacy compliance while keeping implementation and operation of controls with the appropriate functional owners.

  • Simplify and automate repeated administrative work, test the results, and verify that the improvement is adopted and produces accurate, reliable outputs.

  • Learn the GRC security-control environment and participate in the team’s on-call rotation, with scope and expectations explained during the hiring process.

  • Communicate clearly, surface uncertainty early, incorporate feedback, and develop the domain knowledge needed for the next priority.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have practical experience building and operating AI safety/security and content-moderation programs, and can explain your own decisions, contribution, and results.

  • Have used agentic tooling to automate and improve to scaled processes

  • Understand relevant technical concepts across model evaluation, training and release, safety controls, content moderation, and post-launch operations, and can explain where specialist input is needed.

  • Have a strong understanding of relevant AI safety, content, and privacy requirements, including the EU AI Act, DSA, OSA, and SB 53, and experience translating them into operating processes and controls with domain experts and Legal.

  • Have led regulatory responses and external compliance audits, and can distinguish supported claims from evidence gaps.

  • Have delivered complex cross-functional programs, scoped practical first increments, and adapted priorities when constraints changed.

  • Have improved or automated an operational workflow and verified its accuracy, usefulness, and ongoing ownership.

  • Can maintain precise records, navigate technical/compliance documentation and contract language, follow through on commitments, and judge what to resolve directly or escalate.

  • Communicate clearly in writing and conversation with technical teams, Legal, leadership, and external stakeholders; explain evidence, uncertainty, recommendations, and tradeoffs.

  • Work constructively through disagreement, learn from feedback, and take responsibility for outcomes. Privacy program-management experience is a plus.

About the role

We’re looking for a product data scientist to help OpenAI create more value and drive sustainable growth for young people, families, and learners. You’ll drive product data science across under-18 audiences, emerging opportunities for children under 13, family experiences, and learning and education more broadly.

You’ll help decide where we should invest, what we should build, and how we’ll know it is working. This means understanding distinct audience needs, identifying promising use cases, and turning evidence into a clear product strategy. Your work will connect discovery and early product development with adoption, retention, and sustained user value.

You’ll partner across Chat Product, Growth, Foundations, SafeSys, and other teams, working closely with product managers, engineers, designers, and researchers. The role focuses and owns product value and growth while dedicated teams own policy and safety.

In this role, you will:

  • Shape strategy and prioritize opportunities. Size unmet needs and growth opportunities across audiences, use cases, and product experiences. Help teams choose where to invest and sequence work based on expected user value, reach, evidence, and effort.

  • Define what value and success mean. Develop an audience-specific measurement framework spanning activation, task success, learning progress, satisfaction, and durable retention. Connect these measures to product goals and assess whether repeat use reflects meaningful benefit.

  • Understand users and growth drivers. Analyze journeys, funnels, and cohorts to uncover where people find value, where they struggle, and what helps them return. Combine behavioral data with surveys and user research to explain differences across ages, family roles, and learning contexts.

  • Measure what changes actually cause. Design experiments and holdouts to evaluate product and model changes. Apply causal methods when randomization is impractical, make assumptions explicit, and account for seasonality, audience composition, and effects that differ across segments.

  • Turn findings into product decisions. Work with partners from initial hypotheses through launch and iteration. Recommend what to build, change, expand, or stop, explaining expected impact, uncertainty, and tradeoffs. Follow through to determine whether decisions delivered the intended results.

  • Build reliable measurement. Partner with engineering on instrumentation, dataset quality, and consistent audience definitions. Create reusable analyses and dashboards that make progress visible and let teams answer recurring questions independently.

  • Create alignment across teams. Bring a coherent view of audience value to work spanning multiple roadmaps. Help partners agree on priorities, success criteria, and the next questions to resolve, even when ownership is distributed and evidence is incomplete.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • A record of influencing product strategy and improving user outcomes through hands-on data science, including work from an ambiguous question to a decision and measurable impact.

  • Strong SQL and Python skills, sound statistical judgment, and practical experience with experiments, causal inference, cohort analysis, and measurement design.

  • The ability to develop useful definitions of product value, validate imperfect proxies, and distinguish short-term metric movement from lasting improvement.

  • Clear communication and strong product judgment. You can make a recommendation, explain its limits, and influence collaborators across functions without relying on formal authority.

  • Comfort setting priorities independently across a broad scope, staying close to users, and moving between strategic questions and detailed analytical work.

Helpful experience

Experience with consumer product growth, youth or family products, learning and education, or generative AI would be valuable. We also welcome experience measuring learning outcomes, combining quantitative and qualitative research, or evaluating products whose value emerges over time.

Role Summary

Scale builds AI applications for organizations where reliability, security, and measurable results matter. Our core platform, SGP, gives teams the capabilities to build, deploy, evaluate, and operate those applications in customer environments.

We're looking for a product leader to own the strategy and roadmap for SGP's core platform and lead the PM team responsible for it. You will work with customers, platform engineering, and forward deployed teams to build capabilities customers need, productize work developed in the field when it has broader value, and improve how teams build, deploy, and operate AI applications.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You will connect work across teams into a coherent product, make difficult scope and investment decisions, and stay close enough to the details to know whether what we ship works for the people using it.

What you'll do

  • Own the platform strategy and roadmap. Prioritize across developer experience, capabilities customers need, and productizing work built in the field where it has broader value. Sequence investments against customer value, commitments, and dependencies.
  • Define how the product should work. Work with users and engineers to write clear requirements and vibe code prototypes, user journeys, and measure success through customer outcomes, capability adoption, delivery time, and production performance, and follow through on gaps after launch.
  • Align teams across the business. Work with platform engineering, forward deployed PMs, and business leaders to agree on shared capabilities, rollout priorities, and necessary differences across environments. Make clear what is available, where it works, and what remains to be delivered.
  • Build and lead a strong PM team. Establish clear ownership across related product areas, hire and coach PMs, and raise the quality of product thinking and written requirements. Stay directly involved in the most consequential decisions.

What we're looking for

  • A track record of owning platform, infrastructure, or developer products from problem definition through launch and sustained production use.
  • Experience managing and developing product managers, setting direction across multiple related product areas, and remaining hands-on with important product decisions.
  • Strong product judgment. You can explain which problems you chose to solve, what you decided against, how you sequenced the work, and what changed for users as a result.
  • Technical depth to work credibly with engineers on APIs, runtime behavior, identity and authorization, deployment, observability, and data isolation. You can reason through architectural tradeoffs and their consequences for users, security, and operations.
  • Experience driving adoption across teams with different needs and constraints. You can reach decisions, establish ownership, and follow through when progress depends on people outside your reporting line.
  • Clear, precise writing and communication. You can turn an ambiguous problem into requirements engineers can act on and explain priorities and tradeoffs to customers and executives.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience with AI platforms, including agent runtimes, workflow orchestration, evaluation, datasets, human review, or production AI observability.
  • Experience building products for regulated industries or deploying into on-premises, air-gapped, or classified environments.
  • Experience turning capabilities developed for individual customers into reusable platform products.

Job Description:

The Director, DoN Growth Campaign Leader leads the internal operating rhythm that enables Shield AI’s UAS pursuits with the Department of the Navy, including the U.S. Navy and U.S. Marine Corps. Opportunity-focused Go-To-Market (GTM) leaders retain ownership of their customers, capture strategies, account plans, and individual pursuits. This role serves as the connective tissue across those leaders, integrating information across the DoN portfolio and providing the VP, Mission Solutions with a clear, decision-ready view of campaign health, priorities, dependencies, risks, mitigations, and resource requirements. 

The Director connects DoN pursuits with relevant activity across other Services, allied and partner nations, product and engineering, U.S. Government approvals, aircraft availability, ship and at-sea test windows, airworthiness and shipboard-suitability sequencing, internal investment, and industrial strategy. The role identifies shared dependencies and resource conflicts early, helps sequence competing demands, and coordinates the cross-functional support required for GTM leads to execute their captures effectively. 

The role maintains the authoritative DoN campaign picture and runs the operating cadence that turns portfolio insight into action. This includes campaign reviews, risk and dependency management, executive dashboards, action tracking, investment recommendations, and escalation of decisions requiring VP or executive attention. The Director ensures that information flows efficiently from the GTM organization to the VP, Mission Solutions and that leadership receives clear recommendations, tradeoffs, and required decisions. 

GTM leads remain accountable for customer engagement, account planning, capture strategy, win strategy, price-to-win, proposal content, and pursuit outcomes. The Director enables their success by improving coordination, reducing friction around shared resources, and ensuring that the broader organization is aligned behind the highest-priority Department of the Navy opportunities. 

Scope & authority:

    This is a senior, high-visibility seat with authority, not a reporting function: 
  • Portfolio: Multiple concurrent Navy and Marine Corps pursuits across the X-BAT FoS, representing a multi-billion-dollar addressable opportunity. 
  • Team: Leadership by influence role, leveraging dedicated capture-operations and analyst support, with the expectation to build the team as the portfolio scales. 
  • Investment: Develops and co-stewards annual campaign and indirect investment against prioritized campaign returns. 
  • Governance: holds a standing seat in DoN bid/no-bid and investment-prioritization reviews, and sets the agenda for the executive campaign review. 
  • Growth path: a pipeline role toward senior Department of the Navy growth or general-management leadership at Shield AI. 

What you'll do:

  • Own the DoN view. Build and maintain the integrated DoN campaign picture across all X-BAT FoS DoN pursuits: strategy status, critical path, milestones, dependencies, decision points, and campaign health in one authoritative view. 
  • Enable GTM leads. Give each GTM lead the templates, playbooks, data, competitive inputs, cost and schedule inputs, and cross-functional access they need to build and execute their own capture plan. Success is measured by their outcomes, not by your visibility. 
  • Synchronize functions. Coordinate engineering, product, export, legal, contracts, finance, government relations, and business operations against a single prioritized campaign plan so GTM leads are not individually negotiating for the same scarce resources. 
  • Surface conflicts between campaigns. Identify where two or more campaigns compete for the same aircraft, test window, ship or range availability, engineering effort, approval bandwidth, or indirect dollar, and bring executive leadership a clear tradeoff and a recommendation. 
  • Drive executive decision quality. Run the operating cadence — campaign reviews, gate reviews, risk registers, action tracking, and executive dashboards — so leadership receives timely, accurate, decision-ready information on bid/no-bid, investment, and prioritization. 
  • Steward indirect investment. Work with Finance and Business Operations to track campaign investment, indirect spend, and resource planning against campaign priorities and expected return. 
  • Scale discipline. Capture what worked and what did not across captures, and convert it into repeatable tools, templates, metrics, and playbooks so each new campaign starts further ahead than the last. 
  • Support a culture of accountability, urgency, collaboration, and continuous improvement. 
  • Roll up your sleeves. Personally drive the execution of critical customer responses (RFI, RFP, CSO, and other solicitation vehicles) — assembling cross-functional inputs, holding the response schedule, and driving on-time submission, while the GTM lead retains ownership of win strategy, price-to-win, and proposal content. 

Decision rights & interfaces:

  • This role is accountable for: the integrated campaign plan and DoN view; the operating cadence and campaign-health reporting; identification and escalation of cross-campaign dependencies, conflicts, and risks; path-to-win roadmap; and recommendations on investment prioritization and sequencing. 
  • Opportunity GTM leads are accountable for: customer relationships and engagement, capture strategy, win strategy and price-to-win for their pursuit, proposal content, and the bid/no-bid recommendation for their opportunity. 
  • Government Relations, Export, Legal, and Contracts are accountable for: data-rights, political and legislative engagements and outcomes, disclosure determinations, legal positions, and contracting terms. 
  • Engineering and Product are accountable for: technical solution definition, configuration decisions, performance commitments, and coordination with relevant DoN technical authorities on airworthiness and shipboard-suitability requirements. 
  • Program Management is accountable for: execution of customer-funded programs after award. 
  • External customer engagement by this role is in support of, and at the invitation of, the responsible GTM lead. 

Required qualifications:

  • U.S. person as defined by ITAR (22 CFR 120.62), with the ability to obtain and maintain a DoD Top Secret/SCI clearance and Special Access Program (SAP) eligibility. 
  • 12–20+ years in capture management, program management, strategic operations, business operations, technical program management, or a comparable cross-functional leadership role. 
  • Demonstrated success leading highly complex initiatives with multiple interdependent workstreams across engineering, business development, operations, finance, and executive leadership. 
  • Working knowledge of how Department of the Navy programs actually get funded and fielded — ASN(RD&A) and NAVAIR program-office dynamics (particularly PAE(A)) and the unmanned aviation portfolio), Navy and Marine Corps resource sponsorship and requirements staffing (N9/N98) and the Marine Corps aviation requirements process, the PPBE/POM cycle and Navy budget submission rhythm, and rapid-acquisition pathways such as OTAs, CSOs, Middle Tier of Acquisition, SBIR/STRATFI, DIU, ONR, and NavalX, including the transition from prototype to program of record. 
  • Proven ability to influence without direct authority and to drive accountability across functions and geographies. 
  • Strong executive communication: leadership briefings, dashboards, metrics, and decision-support materials that lead to decisions rather than discussion. 
  • Deep operational rigor in integrated schedules, critical path, milestones, action tracking, dependency management, and risk mitigation. 
  • Comfort operating in ambiguous, fast-changing environments with competing priorities across multiple time zones. 
  • Working understanding of the dependencies unique to naval aviation — NAVAIR airworthiness and flight-clearance processes, shipboard integration and suitability, environmental and marinization requirements, ship and at-sea test window availability, and DT/OT execution at Patuxent River and associated ranges. 
  • A service orientation toward the GTM leads this role supports, and the judgment to know when to escalate versus resolve quietly. 

Preferred qualifications:

  • Active DoD Top Secret/SCI clearance and current Special Access Program accesses. 
  • Experience supporting Department of Defense, aerospace, autonomy, robotics, aviation, or defense-technology organizations. 
  • Naval aviation background — U.S. Navy or Marine Corps operational, test, staff, or acquisition experience, or equivalent industry experience delivering aircraft to the Department of the Navy. 
  • Experience within business development, capture, proposal operations, strategic planning, or growth organizations running multiple concurrent U.S. Government pursuits. 
  • Familiarity with the export and international mechanisms that shape Department of the Navy pursuits — foreign disclosure determinations, FMS/DCS pathways, and security cooperation planning — where allied demand affects the Navy business case. 
  • Experience building executive dashboards, KPIs, operational scorecards, or portfolio health metrics. 
  • Experience supporting executive staff, chief-of-staff organizations, Strategy and Operations teams, or enterprise PMOs. 
  • Fluency with integrated schedule and work-management tooling (e.g., Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, Jira), and an advanced degree or relevant certification (MBA, PMP, Lean Six Sigma) is a plus but not required. 

Success in this role:

  • GTM leads report that the role makes their campaign easier to run, not heavier to report on. 
  • DoN path-to-win is in place and running on a predictable, repeatable cadence that the whole organization can plan against. 
  • Cross-campaign resource and timing conflicts reach leadership as a decision with a recommendation, not as a surprise. 
  • Executive leadership can see, at any time, an accurate health picture of the DoN X-BAT FoS portfolio and make investment calls with confidence. 
  • Campaign mechanisms are reused across opportunities, and each new pursuit stands up measurably faster than the previous one. 

How we work:

    Shield AI’s core values — Do What Honor Dictates, Live as a Servant Leader, and Pursue Excellence — are how we hire, promote, and make hard calls. This role in particular demands servant leadership: success is measured by the outcomes of the GTM leads it supports. 

    Veterans and transitioning service members: we actively seek candidates with U.S. Navy or U.S. Marine Corps operational, staff, or acquisition experience, and we support military-to-civilian transitions. 

    Compensation and benefits: competitive base salary, meaningful equity in a growing defense-technology company, annual bonus, comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k), and relocation support where applicable. Final compensation depends on experience, clearance, and location.

Australia is home to Shield AI Australia and its Melbourne-based engineering capability. You will help translate the substance of that local presence—including Australian engineering expertise, sensing and situational-awareness technologies, autonomy software, and collaboration with Australian defence and industry stakeholders—into credible, sustained external communications.

Working closely with the Regional Communications Lead for Asia and the Middle East, Global Communications, Australia business development, government relations, engineering, and cross-functional teams, you will support strategic business priorities and shape narratives around consequential technologies changing the defence landscape.   • Own and grow Shield AI's earned-media footprint in Australia, building trusted relationships with defence, aerospace, national-security, technology, business and policy journalists.

  • Identify and create high-quality opportunities for Shield AI executives, technical leaders and subject-matter experts to participate in interviews, briefings, contributed articles and other earned speaking engagements.

  • Shape and protect Shield AI's reputation as a credible, consistent and long-term contributor to Australia's defence and national-security ecosystem.
  • Build a sustained drumbeat of earned visibility that demonstrates Shield AI's commitment to Australia through local talent, engineering, technology development and collaboration with Australian industry and defence stakeholders.
  • Help differentiate Shield AI's local capability and technology leadership in a competitive discussion around sovereign autonomy, AI, sensing and future warfare.
  • Anticipate and help manage narrative risk, including questions related to foreign ownership, sovereign capability, defence procurement, AI assurance and geopolitical sensitivities.
  • Partner closely with Australia business development and government relations teams to ensure communications activity supports stakeholder engagement while maintaining appropriate independence and credibility with media.
    • Events and regional coordination
  • Lead communications planning and execution for priority Australian events, including Land Forces, Avalon Airshow and other relevant defence, aerospace, technology and policy engagements.
  • Develop integrated event communications plans covering narrative development, media targets, executive programmes, press materials, interview scheduling, on-site management and post-event follow-up.
  • Coordinate with the Asia and Middle East regional team on overlapping executive visits, partner announcements and major communications moments.
  • Manage external agencies, freelancers and suppliers where appropriate, setting clear scopes, standards, reporting and performance expectations.
  • Travel within Australia and periodically across the Asia-Pacific region as business needs require.

Required qualifications:

  • 8+ years of communications experience, including meaningful experience in defence, aerospace, national security, government, technology or other complex B2G sectors. A mix of in-house and agency experience is welcome.
  • Bachelor's degree in communications, journalism, public relations, political science, international relations, marketing or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Strong track record of securing high-quality earned media coverage in Australia, with established relationships across relevant defence, aerospace, business, technology and/or policy media.
  • Demonstrated experience developing communications strategies and executing programmes around major announcements, partnerships, events and executive visibility.·       Exceptional written and verbal storytelling skills, sound editorial judgement and close attention to detail.
  • Experience drafting and editing press releases, media materials, executive briefing documents, speeches, talking points and thought-leadership content.
  • Familiarity with Australian defence-industry dynamics, government and stakeholder sensitivities, and public discussions around sovereign capability, advanced technology and national security.
  • Ability to simplify complex technical concepts accurately for non-technical and technical audiences alike.
  • Strong critical thinking and analytical skills, with the ability to identify opportunities for brand enhancement while assessing potential reputational and issues risks.
  • Experience working across cross-functional and cross-cultural teams, including technical leaders, business development, government relations, external partners and senior executives.
  • Ability to operate with a high degree of autonomy and manage multiple projects, deadlines and stakeholders in a fast-paced environment.
  • Interest in AI, autonomy, uncrewed systems, sensing and defence technology.

  • Position Australia-based and visiting Shield AI leaders as credible, informed voices in earned media, industry and policy conversations.
  • Build a sustained, proactive earned-media programme that demonstrates Shield AI's long-term commitment and local contribution, rather than relying solely on news-driven announcements.
  • Develop a repeatable Australia storytelling engine that turns local engineering, technology, workforce, customer-safe programme and partnership proof points into high-quality external content.

Job Description

Great recommendations are how members find something worth their time. We are looking for an experienced Human Evaluations Program Manager to help us measure and improve the quality of recommendations across the Netflix homepage and discovery experience. You will work alongside Product Management and ML teams to build the human evaluation programs that tell us whether recommendations are working for members, and where they are not.

About the Role

Netflix is building toward more relevant, more varied, and more trustworthy recommendations, and thoughtful, high-quality evaluation is essential to making sure we are moving in the right direction. Join a team creating the frameworks, tools, and workflows that ensure human judgment is applied with consistency, clarity, and care, whether we are evaluating relevance, repetition, diversity, or whether a recommendation simply makes sense to the member.

You will not only shape how human evaluations of our recommendations are designed, but also own the day-to-day execution. From scoping and planning to vendor management, rater onboarding, and calibration, you will be accountable for driving delivery from start to finish. Just as critically, you will act as a thought partner to Product Management, helping translate recommendation strategy into evaluation designs and building a shared language around recommendation quality across teams.

The Opportunity

You will keep evaluation projects on track, ensuring consistent execution, timely delivery, efficient use of vendor capacity, and high rater alignment. You are skilled at translating product strategy into evaluation workflows, defining milestones, managing vendors, and delivering consistent results in a dynamic environment. You can steer teams across functions, keep timelines on track, and ensure rater quality without micromanaging. You are curious about how personalization works and can build credibility with PMs, data scientists, and ML engineers. You thrive in spaces where there is no roadmap, and you take pride in making things real, not just possible.

作成された日々の計画に沿って、作業工程が計画通りに円滑に進むようサポートを行います。

*勤務はシフト制、4勤3休の10時間勤務+休憩1時間となります。

Overview

 

Effective marketing starts with understanding customers: how they engage, what they need, and which experiences create value. Microsoft's Marketing Data Engineering Team turns signals across web, campaigns, content, seller and partner interactions, and sales outcomes into trusted data products. We help marketers improve multi-channel customer engagement and learn faster through evidence, with AI-native self-service that makes trusted data easier to find and use. 

As a Principal Data Engineering Architect, you will lead the architecture and hands-on development of petabyte-scale systems processing billions of events per day that power the business. You will help shape team strategy across data architecture, modeling, solution design and data products, and provide technical direction for major capabilities. This individual contributor role combines autonomy with influence across partner engineering teams, enabling domain teams through shared standards. 

Business acumen is central to the role. You will work closely with marketers, marketing technologists, analysts and data scientists to understand their challenges and the why behind requests. Connect customer and business needs to reusable capabilities that solve more than a single requirement, while choosing the simplest approach that delivers value without overbuilding.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. We bring a growth mindset to our work, collaborate across boundaries, and build on the values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create an inclusive culture where everyone can thrive.

Join us to unleash your potential and play a pivotal role as a data innovator with world-changing impact - your journey starts here!



Responsibilities

 

 

Business Understanding & Impact 

This role enables Microsoft's Marketing organization to transform raw data into trusted, scalable, AI-ready data products that fuel campaign performance measurement, customer intelligence, audience engagement, revenue growth, and executive decision-making through the Microsoft Fabric ecosystem.

 

The Principal Data Engineering Architect is responsible for the following:

  • Partner with PMs and business users to define problems, connect requests to customer journeys and business outcomes, and prioritize reusable capabilities. Use feedback, adoption, reuse and quality measures to guide product decisions and team data strategy. 
  • Lead solution design and production implementation of major data capabilities. Build hands-on prototypes, contribute production code, review code, models and designs, and remain accountable for operational reliability and measurable product outcomes. 
  • Develop logical, physical and semantic models for foundational marketing domains. Productize engagement signals with clear business definitions, metric logic, contracts and ownership so analysts, applications and AI consumers can use data without guessing its meaning. 
  • Design distributed processing and storage using streaming, batch or combined patterns. Apply immutable event data and flexible schema evolution to protect downstream products. Make explicit tradeoffs among latency, accuracy, reliability, cost and maintainability. 
  • Influence engineering and user-facing tools for governed self-service ingestion, publishing and extension of platform data. Improve discovery, access and user experience through interoperable templates, interfaces and semantic abstractions that preserve domain ownership. 
  • Embed security, privacy and quality by design, including metadata, lineage, classification, policy-aware access and retention. Establish monitoring and engineering practices that make federated products trustworthy, supportable and cost-conscious throughout their lifecycle. 
  • Advance AI automation and governed code generation for transformations, tests, documentation and self-service data extension. Use bounded assistance for operational detection and recommendations, with rigorous validation, approved remediation and human judgment for consequential changes. Measure delivery and operational improvements. 
  • Bring a startup mindset to a large, complex data environment: listen, simplify, iterate quickly and make sound decisions. Mentor and coach engineers, strengthen reviews and standards, and align partner teams through technical credibility and collaboration. 

Other

  • Embody our culture and values. 

 



Qualifications

 

 

 

Minimum Qualifications: 

 

  • Master's Degree in Computer Science, Math, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related field AND 4+ years experience in business analytics, data science, software development, data modeling, or data engineering
    • OR Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Math, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related field AND 6+ years experience in business analytics, data science, software development, data modeling, or data engineering
    • OR equivalent experience. 

 

 

Preferred Qualifications:

 

 

  • Master's Degree in Computer Science, Math, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related field AND 8+ years experience in business analytics, data science, software development, data modeling, or data engineering
    • OR Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Math, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related field AND 12+ years experience in business analytics, data science, software development, data modeling, or data engineering
    • OR equivalent experience.
  • 3+ years experience with data governance, data compliance and/or data security.
  • 8+ years of experience across the software development lifecycle, including 2+ years in a technical lead role designing and delivering large-scale data platforms. 
  • Demonstrated expertise in distributed and big-data processing, streaming and batch systems, logical and physical data modeling, semantic abstraction and schema evolution; proficiency in SQL and a programming language. 
  • Proficient business acumen and product judgment, with demonstrated ability to understand business users, translate ambiguous needs into reusable data capabilities, and connect engineering decisions to customer and business outcomes. 
  • Demonstrated cross-functional technical leadership, mentoring and influence through partnership. Clear written, verbal and presentation communication for technical and business audiences, and sound judgment informed by quantitative and qualitative evidence in fast-moving, ambiguous environments. 
  • Experience with marketing, digital media or web analytics, customer journey measurement, and data products supporting analytics, data science and activation.
  • Experience building federated self-service platforms or governed AI-assisted engineering and discovery tools, with evidence of improved adoption, delivery efficiency or operational quality.

Role: Product Manager II

Help millions of people discover why Copilot is worth paying for.

Copilot is becoming the AI companion people reach for at work, and more and more of those moments happen on a phone. Every day, people discover something new Copilot can do for them. Your job is to make sure that, when they are ready for more, the path to a paid plan is clear, helpful and genuinely valuable. You will own real experiments on a product used around the world, learn fast and see your work land with customers in weeks, not years.

Why this role, why now

Copilot recently came together as one app across web, desktop and mobile, with chat, agents and creation in a single experience. Monetization is moving inside the product, where value is felt. Early signals on mobile are strong, and in-app purchase is now live on iOS and Android. It is an exciting moment to join: the patterns for monetizing AI are being invented now.

How we work

  • Small, empowered mission teams with clear ownership.
  • Every bet starts with a written hypothesis, is measured rigorously, and decisions are made on evidence.
  • AI-native by default: we use AI agents and tools throughout our own workflow to research, prototype, analyze and ship faster.
  • Ship fast, learn faster, scale what works.
  • India shapes global strategy here, not just execution.

You'll thrive here if…

  • You would rather own the outcome, good or bad, than be shielded from it.
  • You love turning data and customer insight into a sharp idea worth testing.
  • You form a view, test it quickly and update it when the data disagrees.
  • You thrive with high ownership and ask for help early.
  • You already use AI to work faster and keep exploring what else it can do.
  • Shipping often sounds energizing, not exhausting.

This role may not be for you if…

  • You want a fully specified plan handed to you every quarter.
  • You prefer long studies to running a test and learning from it.
  • You measure success by features launched rather than customers who find value.

Why join us

This is a chance to shape how AI is experienced and valued by people around the world, early in your career and at real scale. You will learn alongside a fast-moving, AI-native team, own outcomes from day one and grow quickly. If that sounds like your kind of challenge, we would love to meet you.

The CUDA programming language defines a unified programming model across a range of system configurations and hardware capabilities. The compiler translates parallel programs written in higher-level languages, like CUDA C++, into microcode optimized for fast execution on NVIDIA’s family of industry-leading GPU architectures. More and more of that code is now written with the help of AI agents, and the compiler front end is where developers and agents first meet the language. In this role, you will focus on the CUDA compiler front end, building language features, diagnostics, and capabilities that help both developers and agents write correct, high-performance GPU code. You’ll also have the opportunity to grow into other parts of the compiler stack, including the LLVM-based optimizer, code generation, and MLIR.


What you'll be doing:

  • Build compiler capabilities that help AI agents generate high-performing, high-quality GPU code.
  • Improve front-end diagnostics and compiler feedback so that developers and AI agents can understand and act on what the compiler tells them.
  • Design and implement CUDA C++ language features and extensions in the compiler front end, including parsing, semantic analysis, and code generation to IR.
  • Track and implement evolving C++ standards features, and make sure they work well with the CUDA programming model.
  • Explore and contribute to all parts of the compiler stack, including optimization, back end, and MLIR, wherever the right solution lives.
  • Partner and collaborate with other compiler, library, and developer tools teams in a dynamic environment to deliver high-quality, robust solutions.

What we need to see:

  • Bachelor’s, Master’s, or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • 5+ years of relevant work or research experience in compiler development.
  • Hands-on experience with a production C or C++ compiler front end, such as Clang or GCC.
  • Strong understanding of the C++ language, including templates, overload resolution, and modern C++ standards.
  • Strong C/C++ programming and software design skills.
  • Ability to work independently, define project goals and scope, and drive complex engineering efforts to production.
  • Solid interpersonal skills and the ability to collaborate across teams.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Clang development experience, including upstream contributions.
  • Experience participating in programming language standards committees.
  • Experience with LLVM optimization passes, code generation, or MLIR dialects.
  • CUDA C++ application development experience and a deep understanding of parallel programming concepts.
  • Experience with compiler diagnostics, static analysis, or language tooling such as clangd.

Create and analyze block/subsystem-level coverage models, and add test cases to increase coverage.

Help build the system that proves a photo is real.

Imagine a photo that carries cryptographic proof it came from an Apple device sensor and hasn’t been altered. We’re building that. This is one of Apple’s most ambitious security, cryptography, and imaging initiatives. The system reaches from the image sensor, through on-device capture and RAW pipelines, into Private Cloud Compute (PCC) for processing and signing. It ends in the viewing and sharing experiences on iOS and macOS. Newsrooms, wire services, and everyday users will rely on it.

We’re looking for a Systems Engineer to own key parts of the architecture and the integration across the stack. You’ll work across hardware security, cloud infrastructure, and application behavior. You’ll partner with the project DRI and own specific systems-level work streams. You’ll also help several teams stay aligned on a system that is secure, coherent, and shippable.

Description

In this role you’ll be expected to:
* Contribute to and help maintain the systems architecture for Reference Image, spanning sensor-level signing, on-device RAW capture pipelines, and cloud-based development in PCC.
* Contribute to the design and implementation of cryptographic key rotation, certificate lifecycle management, and revocation frameworks.
* Work closely with Security and Privacy teams to help threat-model end-to-end media authenticity workflows, evaluating cryptographic integrity, data privacy, and downstream non-destructive edit handling.
* Help evaluate and advance standard and extended image container formats to support secure provenance and authenticity metadata.
* Coordinate with PCC/Cloud infrastructure teams on specific integration points to ensure the signing and certificate infrastructure scales and meets the security bar.
* Represent your work stream's technical tradeoffs in cross-functional forums (Photos, Camera Capture, ISP/hardware, QA, Privacy, Legal, Marketing), proactively identifying and resolving cross-team technical dependencies and blockers.
* Contribute to scoping and planning for future hardware generations under the direction of the DRI.

Minimum Qualifications

BS in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, and 5+ years of industry experience
Working knowledge of cryptographic signing and verification: certificates, secure boot, key management, and revocation
Comfort working closely with Security and Privacy teams
Ability to work with many stakeholder teams (hardware, platform software, cloud, privacy, legal, QA) on ambiguous, changing requirements, and to keep the DRI informed of key tradeoffs and risks
Strong communication skills. You can explain deep technical tradeoffs clearly to engineers and to non-engineers such as Legal, Marketing, and Support.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with image and media pipelines, including RAW processing, ISP behavior, and DNG, JPEG, and HEIF formats
Experience with distributed cloud infrastructure and confidential compute environments (PCC or similar)
Familiarity with trusted time stamping and its role in chain of custody for signed data
Hands-on experience with certificate issuance, validation, and revocation workflows
Experience shipping flagship security or trust features across multiple operating systems
Familiarity with international privacy and regulatory requirements that affect feature availability by region

The hard problems today include validating negotiated pricing from contract to invoice, handling the many forms of credits, app store billing, and keeping controls current while the systems under them are replaced.

This is a foundational role and the first hire of its kind on the team.   • Accounting domain knowledge (order to cash, month-end close, and materiality) sufficient to tell which billing changes have financial impact

Reinforcement learning is how Claude learns to reason, write code, and act autonomously over long horizons. At frontier scale, an RL run is a large distributed system: training, sampling, and environment execution run concurrently across a large fleet of accelerators and hosts. Anduril’s Mission Success team is a cross-functional group that partners with every business line and supports all products that Anduril builds. Our responsibilities include product operations, training and adoption, and user documentation. We are seeking an experienced technical writer to create and maintain user documentation across our diverse business lines. We believe that the quality of our documentation should reflect the quality of products, which are world-class.

ABOUT THE JOB

As an IPD Technical Writer, your mission is to partner with our numerous product and operations teams to deliver accurate, updated, and easy-to-understand documentation on how to use Anduril products. You will do whatever it takes to organize our engineering and program delivery functions in this mission. In this role, you will work closely with engineers, operations, and various subject matter experts to understand our products, identify user workflows, and use documentation to close the gap. As such, the technical writer will play a foundational role in setting the bar for tone, voice, and quality across our written artifacts.

With Anduril’s focus on defense and national security, user documentation plays a critical role in ensuring front-line operators know how to leverage the “arsenal of democracy.” Your mission is to make the process of learning how to operate systems as easy and seamless as possible, with exceptionally well written and presented artifacts.

You will identify relevant stakeholders and lead them through a documentation roadmap with established key milestones and targets. You will engage subject matter experts at the right time, and you will guide them towards a finished user-facing document that plainly meets customer needs. Finally, you will work with our account teams to ensure that contract deliverables are accurate, on-time, and in the right format.

Written content artifacts under this charter may include things like: technical manuals, operational manuals, maintenance manuals, procedures, checklists, templates, user guides, troubleshooting guides, and release notes. You will partner with account, product, and engineering teams across all phases of product development to ensure users have the right documentation available.

Along with our commercial offerings outlined above, Anduril is pursuing Programs with the GOV, which require documentation in standards such as MIL-STD-40051D, and S1000D, delivered via IADs. Familiarity with these standards and delivery methods, is highly desired.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Create, revise, and maintain IPD, WDM and ICA documents for aircraft interior products.
  • Develop illustrations and technical graphics to support documentation.
  • Analyze engineering drawings, blueprints, Bills of Material (BOM), and change orders to extract and organize component data.
  • Convert complex 3D CAD models or 2D engineering sketches into 2D line art, exploded views, and schematics.
  • Ensure proper sequencing of assemblies, list line-replaceable units, and update suitable interchangeable or substitute part numbers.
  • Partner with engineering, manufacturing, and supply chain teams to verify the accuracy of the parts data
  • Author and maintain manuals in compliance with S1000D.
  • Generate, review, and edit documentation that is user-focused. Work with engineering and operations to deliver task, conditions, standard-centric documentation
  • Evaluate and prioritize tasks required to successfully support product documentation efforts and keep them on track. Help drive the best decision for the company by using a data-driven approach and consider input from stakeholders to ensure well-informed decisions.
  • Manage multiple projects under tight deadlines.
  • Communicate and help manage expectations. Ensure risks are noted with adequate time, and shared with leadership.
  • Help build a culture of technical documentation by contributing to the living documentation process, ensuring that those that come after you learn from your acquired Anduril experience.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 5+ years of demonstrated excellence generating IPD technical documentation
  • Experience writing technical user-facing documentation
  • Experience reading and interpreting engineering documentation
  • Experience building content in a variety of formats (3D CAD: PTC Iso Draw SolidWorks or AutoCAD, Etc.)
  • Must be eligible for Secret and higher security clearance (US)

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Military exposure and experience, particularly with military technical documentation writing and formatting standards, guidelines, and verbiage (MIL-STD-40051, S1000D, Etc.)
  • Strong communication (written and verbal) and interpersonal skills, with emphasis on technical subjects
  • Passion for excellent documentation and user experience
  • Previous experience creating technical documentation in Aerospace and Defense (for DoD)
  • Experience delivering content on fast-paced, complex projects with multiple stakeholders

Anduril is seeking a driven Manager for the Test & Evaluation Team withing our Edge Command and Compute business line. The Test & Evaluation Engineering Team at Anduril works across the entire spectrum of products and business lines, as well as all flight operations and test range management. Our team conducts full system-level development testing, new production acceptance testing, sub-component qualification testing, and much more. If it involves test, we lead the way.

Overview

Anduril is seeking a Principal Test Engineer to serve as the senior-most individual-contributor technical authority for test and evaluation across Connected Warfare's portfolio, including Eagle Eye, NGC2, Menace family of systems, and more. Where Staff and Lead Test Engineers own the test program for a specific system or campaign, this role is accountable for technical coherence across Connected Warfare's applications — supporting teams in shaping sound verification strategy, resolving the hardest cross-system integration and test problems, and raising the bar for how the division's test engineers plan, execute, and document their work.

This role sits above individual program ownership and below formal people management: you'll support Staff- and Lead-level test engineers across multiple concurrent campaigns by reviewing their test approaches and documentation for technical adequacy and coaching them through the hardest problems — not by owning or executing programs yourself. Your primary value is deep technical judgment brought to bear on other teams' work, not headcount or personal execution output. You'll be the person program leadership and engineering call when a test problem is genuinely hard, ambiguous, or spans more than one Connected Warfare system.

What you’ll do

  • Serve as the senior technical authority on test strategy across most of Connected Warfare's applications, providing technical oversight and support to the teams running the division's most complex, highest-risk, or multi-system test campaigns.
  • Review and help program teams strengthen verification strategies — requirements-based, scenario-based, and operationally relevant — ensuring they scale across CW's software-enabled hardware and pure-software systems and properly incorporate customer-required standards and metrics.
  • Act as connective tissue across Connected Warfare's individual test programs: identify where one program's test infrastructure, tooling, instrumentation, or lessons learned should be reused elsewhere in the division, and work with program teams to drive that reuse.
  • Provide technical mentorship and escalation support to Staff and Lead Test Engineers running individual program test campaigns — reviewing test plans, execution approach, and reporting across developmental test, system integration (HIL/SIL), and operational assessment events (from lab integration through field validation), unblocking hard technical problems, and raising the technical rigor of test execution across the division. Step in hands-on only on the most technically demanding events where a program team needs direct help.
  • Directly support T&E Test Process execution (e.g. Test Readiness Reviews (TRRs), technical milestone reviews, and customer acceptance events), representing CW's test posture with credibility to government and program stakeholders.
  • Work with teams to confirm traceability from requirements through verification and validation results across CW programs, and help define and monitor test coverage, requirements verification, and defect closure metrics at a division level, not just program level.
  • Support root-cause investigation on the hardest test findings and system anomalies, partnering directly with engineering to resolve issues that cross system or program boundaries.
  • Represent Connected Warfare T&E in engineering design reviews (PDR/CDR) and technical exchanges with government customers and partner organizations as needed.
  • Contribute to the technical hiring and onboarding of test engineers across Connected Warfare.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Systems Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical discipline (advanced degree preferred); equivalent relevant experience considered.
  • 10-14+ years of experience in system-level test and evaluation of integrated hardware/software systems, with 8+ years operating in a technical leadership or test lead capacity.
  • Demonstrated technical depth across multiple Connected Warfare-relevant systems (e.g., tactical C2, sensor/mission autonomy platforms, networked datalinks) — not limited to a single program.
  • Proven track record across the full test lifecycle — requirements development, HITL lab integration, developmental test, operational validation, and reporting — including experience reviewing and strengthening other teams' test approaches and documentation, not just running your own program.
  • Strong experience with RF communications, tactical datalinks, and networked C2 systems in DoD operational environments.
  • Demonstrated ability to mentor and technically direct other test engineers across concurrent programs without formal management authority — influencing through technical credibility.
  • Deep familiarity with DoD and industry test processes, including MIL-STD test protocols and government verification practices.
  • Skilled in assessing and reporting on test metrics at a program and cross-program level.
  • Excellent communication and technical presentation skills, with demonstrated ability to brief senior internal leadership and government customers.
  • Ability to travel periodically (up to 50%) for test execution at ranges and field sites.
  • Active or immediately eligible for a U.S. Secret security clearance; eligibility for Top Secret/SCI strongly preferred.
  • In this role, you will be subject to pre-employment and randomized substance screening, as required by the Company.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master's degree in Systems Engineering or a related technical field.
  • Prior experience as Test Lead across multiple DoD programs (ACAT I/II or equivalent), including cross-program or cross-system responsibility.
  • Knowledge of EMI/EMC testing, environmental testing (MIL-STD-810), and power/avionics standards (MIL-STD-1275, MIL-STD-1553/1760).
  • Experience helping teams build or scale test automation frameworks, data analysis tooling, or test instrumentation used across multiple programs.
  • Hands-on experience with CI/CD pipelines, software integration, and hardware-in-the-loop test environments.
  • Experience conducting test activities in remote, austere, or tactical operational settings.
  • Active Top Secret/SCI clearance.
