Microsoft Silicon, Cloud Hardware, and Infrastructure Engineering (SCHIE) is the team behind Microsoft's expanding Cloud Infrastructure and is responsible for powering Microsoft's Intelligent Cloud mission. SCHIE delivers the core infrastructure and foundational technologies that support Microsoft Azure and other online services globally. Our focus is on smart growth, high efficiency, reliability, and a trusted experience for customers and partners worldwide. 

The Platform Systems Engineering (PSE) team is seeking a Principal AI Back-End Network Systems Lead to serve as the technical lead and end-to-end product development owner for Back End Network across both scale-up and scale-out. The role will lead the product from requirements and architecture through design, integration, validation, manufacturing readiness, deployment, and fleet learning - spanning silicon, network adapters, switches, interconnects, optics/electrical channels, and the fabric as a complete system. 

The successful candidate will bring deep expertise in one or more AI/ML scale-up or scale-out networking domains and the product-level thinking to connect decisions across the full system. This lead will work from physical and data-link technologies through network and transport behavior to collectives, workloads, modeling, observability, and datacenter deployment, creating clarity across architecture, execution, quality, performance, reliability, power, cost, and schedule. 

#azure #MAIA #AI/ML #Networking #ScaleUp #ScaleOut 



Responsibilities

End-to-End Product Ownership & Architecture 

  • Own the Back End Network product definition and execution plan across scale-up and scale-out, from customer/workload needs and product requirements through architecture, development, qualification, deployment, and fleet learning.
  • Translate AI training and inference requirements into measurable system targets for bandwidth, latency, scale, collective efficiency, reliability, availability, serviceability, power, thermal behavior, cost, security, and schedule.
  • Make and drive cross-system architecture decisions, interface contracts, feature priorities, and risk tradeoffs; maintain clear ownership, milestones, entry/exit criteria, and product readiness metrics.
  • Lead NUDD (new, unique, different, and difficult) technology assessments, prototypes, make/buy/partner decisions, and mitigation plans for the highest product risks. 

Scale-Up/Scale-Out Systems, Silicon, Switch & Fabric 

  • Lead architecture and integration across accelerator and networking silicon, NICs/DPUs, PHYs/retimers, switch ASICs, switches, cables/backplanes, optics, and fabric topology.
  • Define scalable scale-up and scale-out architectures, including topology, radix, reach, link speeds, routing, path diversity, oversubscription, failure domains, and resiliency.
  • Drive silicon, board, switch, firmware, network operating system, and fabric requirements so that components operate as one high-performance and serviceable product.
  • Partner with silicon, switch, optical, cable, connector, system, manufacturing, and supplier teams to deliver designs from concept through production and datacenter integration. 

Optical/Electrical & Cross-Layer Integration 

  • Oversee electrical and optical technologies for high-speed links, including signal integrity, SerDes/PHY, link training, FEC, reach, power, thermal, mechanical, manufacturability, and interoperability tradeoffs.
  • Drive end-to-end behavior across the relevant OSI layers - physical, data link, network, and transport - and the system/runtime interfaces above them.
  • Define and validate Ethernet/RDMA or other scale-up/scale-out protocol behavior, including flow control, congestion control, QoS, routing, packet loss/recovery, telemetry, and security.
  • Ensure hardware, firmware, drivers, network operating systems, management software, orchestration, and datacenter operations are aligned to common specifications and concepts of operation. 

Collectives, Workloads, Modeling & Performance 

  • Connect network architecture to distributed AI workloads, parallelism strategies, traffic patterns, and collective operations such as all-reduce, all-gather, reduce-scatter, and all-to-all.
  • Establish analytical and simulation models for topology, bandwidth, latency, congestion, failure behavior, collective efficiency, workload scaling, power, and cost.
  • Use models, emulation, prototypes, and lab/fleet data to predict bottlenecks, guide design choices, set performance budgets, and validate architectural assumptions.
  • Partner with workload, collective-communication, compiler/runtime, and application teams to co-optimize the network and improve job completion time and cluster efficiency. 

Validation, Reliability, Deployment & Operations 

  • Own the end-to-end validation strategy covering functionality, interoperability, performance, scale, stress, resiliency, reliability, security, serviceability, and upgrade/recovery behavior.
  • Lead bring-up and root-cause analysis across silicon, electrical/optical links, switch, fabric, protocol, system software, collective, and workload layers using telemetry, packet captures, counters, diagnostics, and lab characterization.
  • Define production qualification, manufacturing test, deployment, monitoring, rollback, and fleet-health requirements; use operational learning to drive corrective actions and next-generation improvements.
  • Drive product readiness reviews and ensure the solution can be safely and repeatably deployed, operated, serviced, and scaled in hyperscale datacenters. 

Technical Leadership & Ecosystem Execution 

  • Create clarity and technical alignment across architecture, silicon, hardware, optics, firmware, networking, software, validation, manufacturing, datacenter, and workload teams.
  • Influence internal roadmaps and external partners, including silicon, switch, optical, interconnect, ODM/OEM, and open-source ecosystems; resolve cross-team gaps and ambiguous ownership.
  • Communicate product status, architectural decisions, risks, tradeoffs, and executive asks clearly while mentoring engineers and raising the quality of end-to-end systems engineering.

The Observability SRE organisation is specifically tasked with enabling other teams to better understand their infrastructure and services, providing world-class observability capabilities. Keeping Apple services up and running 100% of the time is a challenging job. Accurately monitoring the health of every application and infrastructure that comprises the Apple ecosystem 100% of the time is an order of magnitude more challenging. As a Site Reliability Engineer on the Observability Team, you will champion the availability, performance, and scaling of customer-facing production services, ensuring customers worldwide experience seamless, lightning-fast, and uninterrupted service. Our monitoring, alerting, and visualisation platform analyses billions of metrics per minute and comprises the central nervous system of Apple's architecture. You will work shoulder-to-shoulder with engineering teams to design and build the next generation of cloud and systems monitoring infrastructure, focusing on automation, availability, performance, and efficiency at "reach every user on the planet" scale.

Description

Apple Services Engineering infrastructure is BIG. Operating at our scale, across multiple geographically dispersed data centers (including AliCloud regions serving China-mainland and global markets) and servicing hundreds of millions of users presents unique challenges. As an SRE at Apple, you'll solve these problems using data, teamwork, and your own expertise. SREs at Apple own the full infrastructure stack — from device driver performance debugging to content delivery network traffic management — our responsibilities are both broad and deep. ASE runs the majority of its systems on Linux, using a mix of open source, vendor-licensed, and internally developed tools for system configuration management, provisioning, software deployment, logging, and monitoring. You'll learn these tools and have opportunities to improve them.

Responsibilities

* Customer SLA/SLO Delivery: Own, monitor, and defend the availability, latency, and performance metrics (SLIs/SLOs) of customer-facing production services.
* Production Management: Maintain and optimise customer-serving production environments, including AliCloud services (ACK Kubernetes, ECS, Serverless, RDS) alongside Apple's own infrastructure.
* Global Traffic Routing: Manage external-facing networking, content delivery, and load balancing (SLB/ALB, Global Traffic Manager, AliCloud CDN) to ensure minimal latency for users worldwide.
* Deployment & CI/CD: Maintain zero-downtime deployment pipelines so new features ship safely and continuously without disrupting customer workflows. Spinnaker experience a plus.
* Proactive Observability: Build customer-centric dashboards and alerting frameworks using Prometheus, Grafana, and Splunk (or similar Log Service) to catch and resolve user-facing issues before they generate support tickets.

This role will be part of the Marketing Science team supporting our North America In-Market businesses, leveraging data and science to support client growth on Meta's platforms. The person in this role will work both reactively and proactively with clients, using Meta's industry-leading data science tools and datasets. They will drive measurement with advertisers, designing experiments (conversion lift, brand lift, attribution, etc.) and conducting analysis or research to help clients understand and improve the effectiveness of their advertising across digital platforms and across media. This work involves direct engagement with clients and media agencies, as well as collaboration with third-parties for the setup and running of studies. The ideal candidate also demonstrates an AI-native mindset, approaching work with curiosity and a bias toward experimentation. They instinctively reach for AI tools, adapt quickly to new workflows, and view AI as a lever for greater impact by rethinking how work gets done.

Responsibilities

  • Engage with clients and agencies to share research-based best practices and measure true business value by building and operationalizing "learning agendas" that highlight how a client can improve business outcomes
  • Partner closely with sales to manage a set of accounts and prioritize measurement and analytics strategy for client engagement
  • Support client engagement with third-party vendors responsible for setting up and conducting measurement studies
  • Drive client, vertical, and industry adoption of preferred measurement methodologies, best practices, products, and approaches in support of the "learning agenda."
  • Design tests to showcase the power of measurement using client data and Meta or third-party tools
  • Conduct in-depth standard and custom ad effectiveness studies for Meta advertisers to understand the relative impact of different marketing strategies across digital platforms and across media
  • Translate complex or technical research results for a general audience
  • Consult with clients and agencies on business hypotheses to test, measurement design and feasibility and insights interpretation
  • Operate internal and external education and training workshops to raise awareness and advocacy of measurement solutions and analytical best practices (auction, use of lift tools)
  • Partner with Product and Partnerships teams to customize existing functionalities, inform roadmap development and pilot new, scalable solutions
  • Build AI tools and workflows that facilitate measurement, attribution, and client recommendations to scale and improve quality of guidance.
  • Use AI to improve ad-effectiveness research while ensuring statistical rigor and adherence to principles of causality.
  • Apply scientific judgment to validate AI outputs before they reach advertisers.
  • Deconstruct complex, cross-functional client measurement and analytics problems into actionable parts that address a larger goal by identifying where to use AI to make work more effective and where people should lead.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in a directly related field, or equivalent practical experience
  • 8+ years of consulting, research, or analytics experience using data and numbers to formulate insights
  • Direct experience scoping and executing research projects with clients and/or cross-functional stakeholders
  • Demonstrated success in building trusted relationships with clients and leadership experience at an industry level
  • Experience communicating technical content to all types of audiences (technical and non-technical) and influencing at executive levels
  • Client-facing experience (internal or external), including experience driving meetings and/or influencing through adoption of new products or research methods
  • Experience analyzing and manipulating datasets to understand patterns and provide insights
  • Experience working with large datasets and using SQL or similar tools
  • Experience with digital advertising measurement methods and technologies, including field experiments, experimental design, survey sampling, and/or panel data
  • Experience applying AI with advertising measurement context and judgement, maintaining high attention to detail for AI-augmented output so that it meets the client needs

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience managing a complex set of client relationships
  • Experience working with structured and unstructured data-sets using statistical methods and software such as R, SPSS, SAS
  • Experience adhering to and implementing responsible, ethical AI practices (e.g., risk assessment, bias mitigation, quality and accuracy reviews)
  • Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies
  • Demonstrated ability to integrate AI tools to optimize/redesign workflows and drive measurable impact (e.g., efficiency gains, quality improvements)
  • Advanced degree in a quantitative field or a Masters of Business Administration

Meta is seeking Research Interns to join our AI Search research team. We are committed to advancing the field of artificial intelligence by making fundamental advances in how AI agents learn from their own experience — improving their search and reasoning workflows, retaining useful knowledge, and transferring those gains to unfamiliar tasks. A central research challenge is making repeated self-improvement reliable when feedback is sparse or noisy. The intern will work in one of three directions, scoped closer to the start date together with the intern manager: -Learning to improve research workflows — agents learn better search, tool-use and verification strategies from prior attempts by improving their harness: the workflow, memory, tools and feedback loop around the model. Topics include meta-learning across tasks, automated agent design, and learning from natural-language feedback. -Persistent memory and continual learning — agents retain useful lessons and update knowledge across tasks, whether in context, in compressed memory, or in weights, without forgetting what they already know. Topics include long-context modeling, context compression, continual learning, and test-time training. -Learning from imperfect feedback — turning noisy judgments and failed attempts into useful learning signals, and improving the strategy an agent uses to learn, including how it selects and evaluates its next improvement. Topics include reward learning, credit assignment, and learning to learn. Across all three directions, the key test is whether improvements transfer to new tasks. The goal is to develop novel methods and experiments toward a first-author submission at a leading ML/NLP venue. Meta Robotics Studio builds consumer humanoid robots that bring Meta's AI into the physical world. Our robots run on NVIDIA Jetson Thor with Meta-designed carrier boards and JetPack OS. The Robotics OS team owns everything between the silicon and the robot learning stack. On one chip, our robots run real-time control loops over EtherCAT while large vision-language-action (VLA) models run on the GPU. Our job is to make that computer do both, deterministically, every time it boots. We are hiring a software engineer to help architect and evolve the robotics OS, Meta's build of NVIDIA Jetson Linux for Thor-class robot compute. Working with the team, you will help shape the multi-year technical direction for the robot's operating system, including how we build, release and update it, how it shares one computer between real-time control and AI workloads, and how it scales from a lab of prototypes to a large fleet of production robots. You will work closely with hardware, firmware, controls, and AI engineers across Meta, and with NVIDIA's Jetson engineering teams as one of several technical points of contact on the platform. This is a hands-on role: when a new board spin won't boot or the control loop misses a deadline, you will be in the kernel log alongside the rest of the team.

Responsibilities

  • Contribute to the technical strategy and multi-year roadmap for the Robotics OS. This covers the board support package (BSP), kernel, OS image, update system, real-time behavior, GPU platform, and fleet tooling across every robot program and compute platform (AGX Thor, IGX Thor, and future NVIDIA silicon)
  • Architect the next-generation OS image, including the move to a Yocto / meta-tegra based build. Make it reproducible, hermetic and secure, and make it fast for many engineers to iterate on
  • Define and drive the production update strategy: atomic A/B and over-the-air updates, rollback, secure and verified boot, fusing and signing, and factory provisioning, so we can ship to a growing fleet safely
  • Shape the platform's real-time architecture. Help define how CPU cores, interrupts, memory and the GPU are divided between control loops at kilohertz rates and large AI models. Set the latency budgets and the measurement infrastructure that proves we meet them
  • Collaborate with NVIDIA's Jetson engineering teams alongside other Meta engineers: share requirements, push fixes upstream, and help plan how we adopt new Jetson Linux / JetPack releases with minimal fork debt
  • Partner with electrical, firmware, and mechanical engineers on new compute and carrier-board designs. Weigh in early on SoC configuration, interfaces, power and thermal so boards are easier to bring up and software stays simpler
  • Drive bring-up of new boards and modules end to end: boot chain (MB1/MB2, UEFI), BPMP and device tree, pinmux, PCIe/USB/Ethernet, power profiles, and the drivers for robot hardware (EtherCAT, USB-C power delivery, Wi-Fi/Bluetooth, sensors, cameras)
  • Help set the quality bar for the RT kernel and out-of-tree drivers: kernel configuration, ABI compatibility, and a plan to upstream changes or align with Meta's kernel instead of carrying long-lived patches
  • Build the reliability and observability foundation: crash and kernel-log capture, symbolization, boot-time tracing, health telemetry, and fleet triage tooling, so that any robot failure can be diagnosed remotely
  • Raise the bar for the engineers around you through design reviews, mentorship, and technical hiring. Grow OS and embedded talent on the team, and help shape on-call and operational practices

  • Deep experience with C and Linux kernel internals, including device drivers, device tree, scheduling, interrupts, and memory management
  • Proficient in at least one of C++, Rust or Python
  • Experience driving new-SoC or new-board bring-up on ARM64, from boot chain through kernel to a production OS
  • Experience designing OS image build and release systems, such as Yocto/OpenEmbedded, Buildroot, Debian packaging or AOSP, including the strategy for updates and release management
  • Experience debugging hard cross-layer problems spanning hardware, firmware, kernel and user space

  • Experience designing secure boot, verified boot and OTA / A/B update systems for a large device fleet
  • Experience with EtherCAT, CAN-FD or other robotics fieldbuses, and with host-to-microcontroller architectures (FreeRTOS, Zephyr)
  • GPU platform experience: CUDA, NVML/MIG, TensorRT, or deploying ML inference on edge devices alongside real-time workloads

Meta designs and deploys its own AI systems. MTIA, the Meta Training and Inference Accelerator, is Meta's family of in-house AI accelerator ASICs, deployed in production across Meta's data centers and expanding workload coverage from ranking and recommendation to generative AI. The MTIA Software team is part of the AI & Compute Foundation organization. Because the hardware is ours, the software is ours too: we build the entire stack a chip vendor would normally supply: compiler and toolchain, runtime, kernel libraries, developer tooling, and deep PyTorch integration, co-designed with the silicon teams generation over generation. The GenAI Frameworks org owns the layer where a model meets the machine. We take frontier models, including large language, multimodal and diffusion models, and make them run efficiently on MTIA. Our work determines how fast those models respond, how much context they can afford to hold, how many of them a given amount of silicon can serve, and how quickly a newly released model can be running and trusted in production. We are hiring a Software Engineer to own a key area of GenAI inference on MTIA, spanning serving frameworks, distributed inference, graph-mode execution and compilation, and core PyTorch integration. This is a domain-expert role: you will set technical direction for your area, drive ambiguous multi-quarter programs across team boundaries, and own the quality bar for accuracy, stability, performance, and test coverage on custom silicon.

Responsibilities

The Meta Reality Labs Research Team brings together a world-class team of researchers, developers, and engineers to create the future of virtual and augmented reality, which together will become as universal and essential as smartphones and personal computers are today. And just as personal computers have done over the past 45 years, AR, VR and MR will ultimately change everything about how we work, play, and connect. We are developing all the technologies needed to enable breakthrough AR glasses and VR headsets, including optics and displays, computer vision, audio, graphics, brain-computer interfaces, haptic interaction, eye/hand/face/body tracking, perception science, and true telepresence. Some of those will advance much faster than others, but they all need to happen to enable AR, VR and MR that are so compelling that they become an integral part of our lives. In particular, the Meta Reality Labs Research audio team is focused on two goals; creating virtual sounds that are perceptually indistinguishable from reality, and redefining human hearing. See more about our work here: https://tech.fb.com/inside-facebook-reality-labs-research-the-future-of-audio/. The Meta Reality Labs Research Team brings together a world-class team of researchers, developers, and engineers to create the future of virtual and augmented reality, which together will become as universal and essential as smartphones and personal computers are today. And just as personal computers have done over the past 45 years, AR, VR and MR will ultimately change everything about how we work, play, and connect. We are developing all the technologies needed to enable breakthrough AR glasses and VR headsets, including optics and displays, computer vision, audio, graphics, brain-computer interfaces, haptic interaction, eye/hand/face/body tracking, perception science, and true telepresence. Some of those will advance much faster than others, but they all need to happen to enable AR, VR and MR that are so compelling that they become an integral part of our lives. In particular, the Meta Reality Labs Research audio team is focused on two goals; creating virtual sounds that are perceptually indistinguishable from reality, and redefining human hearing. See more about our work here: Inside Facebook Reality Labs Research: The future of audio and Filter Out the Noise With Conversation Focus. These two initiatives will allow us to connect people by allowing them to feel together despite being physically apart, and allow them to converse in even the most difficult listening environments. Meta Reality Labs Research is looking for an intern who is passionate about speech perception and audio quality to investigate why processed speech sometimes sounds degraded or robotic. The project focuses on identifying systematic phonemic errors as causal factors in perceived quality degradation, and linking these errors to human quality and intelligibility judgments. A core method is to explore the capabilities of audio vs video LLMs. This is fundamentally a speech-perception research role; multimodal/LLM methods are a supporting tool rather than the central focus. Meta Reality Labs is building custom silicon to power the next generation of augmented and virtual reality devices, including headsets and wearables. As a Design Verification Engineer on the silicon team, you will be responsible for ensuring the functional correctness and quality of complex custom chips that enable immersive AR/VR experiences. In this role, you will develop and execute comprehensive verification strategies for digital logic blocks and subsystems, working closely with design, architecture, and software teams to bring high-performance, low-power silicon from specification to tape-out.

  • Define and close functional coverage models and code coverage metrics to ensure thorough verification of design intent
  • Collaborate with cross functional teams to define verification plans and close coverage
  • Develop and maintain simulation infrastructure, regression frameworks, and automated test frameworks to support continuous integration of design changes
  • Perform formal verification and property checking on critical design blocks to complement simulation-based verification
  • Debug failing simulations and regressions by analyzing waveforms, log files, and RTL code to root-cause design or testbench issues
  • Partner with post-silicon validation and firmware teams to develop pre-silicon test content that transitions to hardware bring-up
  • Contribute to verification methodology improvements, including reusable verification collaterals and shared infrastructure across the silicon team
  • Track and report verification progress, coverage closure status, and risk areas to design and program management stakeholders

  • 6+ years of experience in digital design verification, including development of UVM-based constrained-random testbenches for RTL blocks, subsystems or SoCs
  • 6+ years of experience with hardware description and verification languages including SystemVerilog and/or VHDL
  • Experience with defining and closing functional coverage models and code coverage metrics for complex digital designs
  • Experience with debugging RTL simulations using waveform analysis tools and log-based root-cause analysis
  • Experience with scripting languages such as Python or Perl for test automation, regression management, or coverage analysis

  • Experience with HW/SW interoperability verification and firmware validation
  • Experience with post-silicon validation, hardware bring-up, or transitioning pre-silicon test content to physical hardware
  • Experience verifying silicon for mobile, wearable, or consumer electronics SoCs, including low-power design verification techniques and performance
  • Familiarity with formal verification tools and methodologies
  • Familiarity with agentic AI flows

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the Role

You will run the external audit calendar for our SOX 404 program as we scale toward an IPO. That means coordinating with our external auditors across the year, aligning testing windows with control owners, educating our control owners, and keeping requests and deliverables on schedule. You will also own SOX scoping and risk assessment cycles, deficiency tracking, and status reporting, and help roll out our GRC platform so the program runs from one system of record instead of spreadsheets. You will scale the program through AI-enabled workflows that reduce manual effort and speed up our SOX program.

This role reports to the Head of Business Controls and works closely with everyone on the SOX and Internal Audit team. This is an individual contributor role for someone who keeps a complex program on schedule, writes clearly, and makes the program simpler each cycle.

Key responsibilities

  • Own the annual SOX audit calendar, including interim and year-end testing windows, walkthrough schedules, and key deliverable dates agreed with external auditors.
  • Serve as the day-to-day point of contact for external auditor requests. Triage, route, and track each request to closure, including PBC (provided-by-client) lists and evidence deliveries.
  • Coordinate auditor walkthroughs and fieldwork with process owners, control owners, and the SOX Testing team, so each control owner is asked for the same evidence once.
  • Track auditor findings, management responses, and deficiency follow-ups, and report status to Internal Audit leadership.
  • Prepare control owners and process owners for auditor sessions, and get evidence delivered on time without direct authority over them.
  • Lead the annual SOX scoping and risk assessment, including quarterly refreshes, and support the annual Fraud Risk Assessment, so the program has appropriate scope and coverage under COSO.
  • Monitor BP and IT SOX testing and report status to leadership and share status with external auditors
  • Lead work with the business to improve control documentation, including education of templates and SOX guidance.
  • Find optimization and automation opportunities across the SOX lifecycle through the use of AI.
  • Support the rollout of the GRC tool for SOX, including control libraries, workflows, evidence requests, and testing templates.
  • Define the data and reporting requirements the platform must meet, and test that it produces what the program needs.
  • Run the quarterly sub-certification process and report results to leadership
  • Own SOX program status reporting: dashboards and metrics for leadership, audit calendar progress, and deficiency and remediation status.
  • Own status reporting for the full SOX lifecycle: scoping and risk assessment, testing, deficiencies and remediation, segregation of duties (SOD), SOC 1 report reviews, the fraud risk assessment, and audit calendar progress.

Minimum qualifications

  • Big 4 audit firm experience on SOX 404 or ICFR engagements, including managing audit calendars, PBC requests, and fieldwork with external audit teams.
  • Experience working directly with external auditor teams on requests, testing schedules, and findings, from the company side.
  • Several years of hands-on SOX 404 experience, including scoping, risk assessment, control documentation, testing, and deficiency evaluation.
  • Working knowledge of the COSO framework, ICFR, and PCAOB standards.
  • Experience developing or maintaining Risk and Control Matrices and process documentation or flowcharts.
  • Experience implementing or administering a GRC systems
  • Experience reporting program status, metrics, and issues to senior leadership.
  • Ability to get control owners to deliver on time without authority over them.
  • Clear writing and calm coordination under deadline pressure.
  • A Bachelor's degree in a related field or equivalent experience.

Preferred qualifications

  • In-house SOX experience at a pre-IPO or newly public company.
  • Experience running a fraud risk assessment.
  • CPA, CISA, or similar certification.
  • Comfort with SQL or data tools for reporting, and experience building lightweight automations, including with Claude.

We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

ABOUT THE JOB

The Sourcing Engineer drives the strategic supply network development and cost management of Anduril’s product hardware, across their lifecycles, by collaborating with suppliers and cross-functionally, including folks in engineering, quality, and manufacturing.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

    • Conduct supplier selection for a specific product, leveraging our approved supplier list
    • Partner with strategic suppliers to accelerate product development via activities such as:
    • Concept scoping to quickly solidify requirements
    • Feature trade-off / trade tables
    • Should cost / Clean sheet models
    • Joint design development, via clear statements of work
    • Simulation of mechanical & electronics designs
    • Drive the development and consolidation of a manufacturing BOM, working with Quality & Manufacturing, to ramp production internally and with our suppliers with high flexibility
    • Accountable for all NPI component procurement, on-time and correctly, to scale
    • Manage the CAPEX throughout NPI
    • Conduct value-stream mapping to optimize supply network lead time and flexibility
    • Complete the BOM risk assessment, include alternate component sourcing, etc.
    • Ensure completion of all component qualifications, ahead of production
    • Reduce complexity: commonality optimization & component/supplier rationalization
    • Lead all cost engineering activities to converge the bottoms-up cost curve to product cost, maximizing the total cost of ownership (TCO) across the product lifecycle
    • Manage ad-hoc cost issues e.g., tariffs / import export cost, and cost inflation

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

    • 5+ years of experience, ideally has background within:
      • Design & development of electronics and/or mechanical devices
    • Advanced sourcing activities, including stints as commodity/sourcing managers
    • Supplier development (technology, process, supply chain, etc.)
    • Early supplier engagement, ahead of product/engineering requirement realization
    • Domain expertise must include value/procurement engineering or TCO-related work at the component & product level.
    • Familiarity with developing high-tech products in a high-mix, low-volume environment
    • Some exposure working in a start-up environment
    • Bachelor’s degree in engineering (BSME, BSEE) or other related technical degree preferred. Advanced technical degree or MBA strongly preferred
    • U.S. Person status is required as this position needs to access export controlled data

ABOUT THE JOB 

We are looking for an  Associate, Business & Revenue Operations to join our rapidly growing team in Irvine, CA. In this role, you will be responsible for partnering across the business to design scalable processes, drive operational excellence, and optimize tools and systems that support our growth and business operations teams. You will own the data hygiene that backs our growth pipeline and generate critical analyses that directly impact the Business Line’s economics. 

This will require strong analytical skills, a knack for process improvement, and experience working with cross-functional teams. You will be expected to take ownership of workstreams, form a point of view, and back it up with data. If you are someone who wants real responsibility early, takes initiative, and thrives in a high-growth, fast changing environment, then this role is for you. 

WHAT YOU'LL DO 

  • Build and iterate on planning, forecasting, and operational processes that support how the Business Line runs. 
  • Develop bespoke analyses and associated operating rhythms to support improvement in data accuracy and reporting. 
  • Partner directly with Business Development, Production, and Mission Operations to manage dynamic changes to forecast. Iterate and improve process for data management and hygiene. 
  • Work directly with large, imperfect datasets to surface insights that inform leadership decisions. Turn unclear or messy problems into structured insights and clear recommendations. 
  • Prepare concise, high-quality materials for leadership reviews. 

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 

  • You have 2+ years of experience in an investment banking, management consulting, or internal strategy & operations role. 
  • High ownership and low ego, approaching everything with strong outcome orientation and high humility. 
  • Excellent analytical skills and comfort working with imperfect or incomplete data. 
  • Ability to move between details and the big picture as needed.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills, including presenting to senior leaders.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

  • Experience with Salesforce data environments.
  • Experience with Palantir Foundry, Looker/Tableau, or similar analytics platforms.

The Factory Services team is part of the Shared Services, Systems & Infrastructure (3SI) organization within the Maritime Division. This team owns the technical shared services that every production business line depends on - machining, hydrostatic testing, tooling, 3D printing, and calibration. ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Senior Factory Services Supervisor to join our rapidly growing team in Quonset, RI. In this role, you will be responsible for standing up and leading the technical shared services function at our multi-product manufacturing site. Reporting directly to the Factory Manager, you will be responsible for the coordination and prioritization of all shared technical resources - including the machine room, hydrostatic test chamber, tooling room, and 3D printing capabilities. Your first priority will be designing and implementing a scheduling methodology that ensures fair, transparent, and efficient allocation of these shared resources across multiple business lines. This role requires someone with a strong understanding of manufacturing support services who over-indexes on communication and cross-functional coordination. You will be the person in the middle when two business lines need the same resource at the same time, and you need to be the type of leader who can navigate those conversations, build trust with production stakeholders, and keep the site running smoothly. If you thrive in environments where you are building processes from scratch, managing competing priorities, and serving as the operational backbone for production teams, this role is for you.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Technical Services Leadership: Oversee all shared technical services including machining, hydrostatic testing, tooling fabrication, 3D printing, and future capabilities such as calibration. Ensure each function is staffed, equipped, and operating to meet the needs of all business lines on site.
  • Scheduling and Resource Allocation: Design, implement, and own the scheduling methodology for shared technical resources. Build a system that provides visibility into capacity, demand, and prioritization across business lines. Ensure scheduling decisions are transparent, data-informed, and aligned with site production priorities.
  • Cross-Business Line Coordination: Serve as the primary point of coordination between production business lines and shared technical services. Proactively identify scheduling conflicts and capacity constraints, facilitate prioritization discussions, and ensure equitable access to shared resources. Build strong working relationships with production leads across all programs.
  • Team Development: Supervise and develop technical services staff, including machinists, test technicians, and tooling specialists. Set priorities, assign work, and build a culture of responsiveness and accountability. As the team grows, hire and integrate new roles including a dedicated scheduling coordinator.
  • Process Buildout: Establish standard operating procedures, work request intake processes, and performance metrics for all shared technical services. Build these processes from the ground up in a way that scales as new business lines and capabilities are added to the site.
  • Capacity Planning: Monitor utilization and throughput across all shared resources. Forecast future demand as new programs come online and recommend staffing, equipment, or facility investments needed to stay ahead of production requirements.
  • Communication and Reporting: Provide regular status updates to the Factory Manager and site leadership on shared resource utilization, scheduling performance, and any risks to production timelines. Participate in site battle rhythm meetings and serve as the voice of technical services in cross-functional planning.

  • 2+ years of experience in a supervisory or coordination role managing shared resources or cross-functional support teams
  • Demonstrated ability to build and manage scheduling or resource allocation processes in a multi-program or multi-customer environment
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills with a track record of working across organizational boundaries and managing competing priorities
  • Experience standing up or significantly improving operational processes in a scaling environment
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

  • Familiarity with machining operations (CNC, manual), hydrostatic or pressure testing, and rapid prototyping/3D printing
  • Experience with scheduling tools, MES platforms, or ERP systems used for shop floor resource management
  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing Technology, Industrial Management, or a related field
  • Lean, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement certification or experience
  • Experience working in a shared services or matrix organizational model where resources serve multiple internal customers

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE SITE

Anduril, a leader in autonomous systems and weapons manufacturing, is building Arsenal-1, its first hyper-scale manufacturing facility, just south of Columbus, Ohio in Pickaway County. Arsenal-1 is redefining the scale and speed that autonomous systems and weapons can be produced for the United States and its allies and partners. This is a monumental and essential step toward rebuilding America’s defense industrial base, strengthening America’s warfighting capabilities, and enhancing deterrence amid rising international threats.

ABOUT THE PRODUCT

The future of defense is being built right now, and Anduril’s Barracuda product is at its leading edge. Barracuda is a family of air breathing autonomous air vehicles (AAVS) purpose-built for hyper-scale production and mass employment. The Barracuda family of AAVs consist of Barracuda-100, Barracuda-250, and Barracuda-500. Each increment offers increasing size, range and payload capacity, but all barracudas are compatible with a host of payloads and employment mechanisms, support a variety of different missions, and provide warfighters with an adaptable and upgradeable capability to counter evolving threats.

As a Manufacturing Process Development Engineer, you will design, optimize, and implement manufacturing processes with a focus on manual assembly operations, dispense applications, and technical documentation creation. The right person for this role has strong process engineering skills, experience creating detailed work instructions, expertise in manufacturing process optimization, and the ability to provide real-time production support. If you are someone who thrives in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, can adapt quickly to changing requirements, and is passionate about developing innovative manufacturing solutions to support cutting-edge defense technology production, then this role is for you.

  • Design and optimize manual assembly processes to maximize efficiency, quality, and repeatability in a high volume, low-mix production environment
  • Develop comprehensive manufacturing work instructions and process documentation with clear visual aids that enable consistent production quality

  • Provide active lineside support during production, quickly addressing process deviations and implementing solutions to maintain production flow
  • Drive issue resolution through root cause analysis, corrective actions, and preventive measures to continuously improve manufacturing processes
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams including design engineering, quality, and production to ensure manufacturability of new and existing products
  • Evaluate and implement process improvements to reduce cycle time, minimize defects, and increase overall manufacturing efficiency
  • Develop and validate process parameters, establishing clear control limits to ensure consistent quality
  • Support new product introductions by developing robust manufacturing processes that can scale from prototype to production
  • Participate in design reviews to provide manufacturing feedback and ensure designs are optimized for assembly
  • Utilize AS9100 standards to drive process development and drive issue resolution

  • 5+ years of experience in manufacturing process development, preferably in a high-reliability industry
  • Demonstrated expertise in creating clear, detailed work instructions and manufacturing process documentation
  • Experience optimizing manual assembly operations and establishing standardized work
  • Proven ability to analyze and improve manufacturing processes using lean manufacturing principles
  • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills with ability to implement effective solutions quickly
  • Experience with dispensing technologies and manual application optimization for adhesives, sealants, or similar materials
  • Proficiency with CAD software for creating assembly documentation and tooling design
  • Excellent communication skills and ability to work effectively in cross-functional teams
  • Experience with manufacturing execution systems and digital work instructions
  • Currently possesses an active U.S. Secret security clearance

ABOUT THE JOB
As a Propulsion Test Engineer, you will develop, build, and execute the test campaigns that qualify mission-critical air vehicle propulsion systems and micro-turbojets for production. In this role, you will take ownership of the physical and software test setups that validate engine performance, reliability, and operating limits, working directly with propulsion development engineers to adapt test capabilities as engine designs evolve.
Every Propulsion Test Engineer is responsible for the full lifecycle of engine testing. You will design and fabricate physical test racks and instrumentation suites, write Python-based test software on Linux/Unix platforms, and control and monitor engine sub-assemblies over CAN bus networks. Crucially, you will act as the Test Director during live engine and micro-turbojet hot-fire runs—owning test cell safety, command execution, real-time data monitoring, and emergency abort sequences to ensure safe, repeatable, and high-fidelity testing.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Serve as Test Director during engine and micro-turbojet hot-fire runs, managing test stand operations, console communication, go/no-go criteria, and emergency abort procedures
  • Design, build, and maintain propulsion test hardware infrastructure, including instrumented test racks, sensor harnesses, engine test stands, and thrust measurement fixtures
  • Author comprehensive propulsion test plans, run procedures, redline limits, and acceptance criteria in close collaboration with development engineers
  • Develop robust, automated test and data acquisition software in Python running on Linux/Unix systems to control engine profiles and record telemetry
  • Implement and debug CAN bus communications to interface with Engine Control Units (ECUs), smart actuators, fuel pumps, and test stand controllers
  • Integrate and calibrate propulsion test instrumentation, including load cells, pressure transducers, thermocouples/RTDs, mass flow meters, and vibration sensors
  • Configure, operate, and troubleshoot Linux/Unix test systems using terminal command-line tools, SSH, and network debugging utilities
  • Perform rapid root-cause analysis (RCCA) on unexpected engine behaviors, instrumentation dropouts, or hardware anomalies observed during test execution
  • Analyze post-test steady-state and transient telemetry (thrust, fuel flow, turbine inlet temperature, spool response) and generate detailed test summary reports
  • Maintain and scale propulsion test cell facilities, driving improvements in turnaround time, automated checkout procedures, and facility safety

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field
  • Demonstrated experience in managing control room operations, coordinating complex test schedules, and maintaining accurate inventory tracking systems.
  • 3+ years of hands-on experience in propulsion testing, hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) test setups, or engine test cell operations
  • Direct, hands-on experience with micro-turbojet engine testing (mandatory)
  • Proven experience serving as a Test Director, console operator, or lead test engineer during live engine runs or hazardous hot-fire operations
  • Demonstrated experience designing, building, and wiring test racks, instrumentation boxes, and benchtop DAQ systems
  • Proficiency writing automated test, control, and data acquisition software in Python within a Linux/Unix environment
  • Strong Linux/Unix systems knowledge, including terminal command-line proficiency, SSH, and network configuration/debugging
  • Hands-on experience with CAN bus hardware interfaces and messaging protocols for control and data logging
  • Experience selecting, wiring, and calibrating sensors: pressure transducers, thermocouples, load cells, and flow meters
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Broader turbine, rocket, or internal combustion engine test experience
  • Experience with fluid systems, high-pressure plumbing, fuel delivery lines, valves, and regulators (e.g., Swagelok)
  • Familiarity with CAD tools (such as Siemens NX or SolidWorks) for engine test stand and mounting fixture design
  • Experience with high-speed data acquisition platforms (e.g., National Instruments cDAQ/cRIO) and hardware-level signal conditioning
  • Familiarity with AS9100 or aerospace quality standards as applied to flight hardware testing and validation
  • Active U.S. Secret or Top Secret security clearance

ABOUT THE TEAM

As a Software Manufacturing Test Engineer, you will build, scale, and maintain the software that drives our manufacturing test systems. In this role, your primary focus will be developing production software that directly tests complex hardware systems, integrates with laboratory instrumentation and DAQs, and manages the data these stations produce. You will bridge low-level hardware control with high-level test automation by writing robust, reliable production code in Python and C# targeting Linux/Unix (and ideally NixOS) runtime environments.
To ensure our hardware meets mission-critical quality and production throughput demands, every Software Manufacturing Test Engineer is expected to derive software test requirements from hardware schematics and system specifications, author automated test sequences, and deploy complete software suites to factory test racks. You will work closely with development and firmware engineers to refine test coverage as product designs evolve, resolve complex hardware-software integration failures on the floor, and ensure deterministic software deployments across our manufacturing line.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Maintain ownership of software manufacturing test activities in production, ensuring test station uptime, operator usability, and smooth factory throughput
  • Develop and maintain PLC-integrated station control software — commanding industrial controllers over Modbus TCP for rig actuation, interlocks, and sensor acquisition — and maintain the tag/address index as PLC programs evolve, including tooling that imports controller tag exports and validates them against the station's expected schema
  • Build hardware-free simulation environments (containerized station images, virtual CAN replay, device simulators) so test software is developed and regression-tested without occupying hardware
  • Design, build, and maintain production software manufacturing test suites primarily in Python (for hardware control, test sequencing, and instrument automation) and C# (for test executives, operator interfaces, and background services)
  • Integrate software manufacturing test applications directly with sensors, DAQs, programmable power supplies, electronic loads, and vehicle compute hardware
  • Implement low-level hardware communication using embedded protocols including UART, CAN, and RS-485 / RS-232 to command, flash, and validate devices under test (DUTs)
  • Deploy, configure, and debug software manufacturing test systems running on Linux/Unix platforms using terminal command-line tools, SSH, and network debugging utilities
  • Leverage Nix and NixOS to manage reproducible software manufacturing test environments, eliminating dependency drift between engineering development benches and production line stations
  • Collaborate with hardware and firmware engineers during early-stage product development (NPI) to define software manufacturing test requirements, coverage, APIs, and pass/fail limits
  • Automate software manufacturing test execution across various levels of assembly, from PCBA-level functional test (FCT) up to full-system and Environmental Stress Screening (ESS) checkouts
  • Provide hands-on troubleshooting and root-cause analysis (RCCA) for complex electrical, firmware, and software manufacturing test issues found on the line
  • Log parametric test data and integrate software manufacturing test stations with database systems (using SQL queries as needed) and Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES) to maintain complete hardware traceability
  • Develop clear operator interfaces, error-handling mechanisms, and software manufacturing test troubleshooting logs to assist technicians during hardware failures
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives to optimize software manufacturing test sequences, shorten cycle times, and increase test coverage without sacrificing quality

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or related fields
  • 3+ years of relevant industry experience as a Software Manufacturing Test Engineer, or in an equivalent role with an emphasis on software development for hardware test automation, lab automation, or manufacturing environments
  • Strong proficiency writing production code in Python for software manufacturing test automation, device control, and data handling
  • Working knowledge of C# (.NET) for developing software manufacturing test applications, operator UIs, or system services
  • Strong Linux/Unix systems knowledge, including terminal proficiency, shell scripting, SSH, and network configuration/debugging
  • Demonstrated hands-on experience interfacing software manufacturing test suites with embedded communication protocols: UART, CAN, and RS-485 / RS-232
  • Familiarity with controlling standard test equipment (programmable power supplies, DMMs, oscilloscopes, electronic loads, and DAQ devices) via software
  • Strong root-cause analysis skills for diagnosing hardware-software boundary issues using log files, terminal outputs, and basic bench tools
  • Experience integrating software manufacturing test platforms with Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES) and database backends
  • Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills to collaborate with hardware, software, and operations teams
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with Nix and NixOS for declarative software manufacturing test environment management and deployment
  • C programming knowledge
  • Familiarity with SQL for direct database querying and test record validation
  • Basic familiarity with HTML/CSS for formatting internal software manufacturing test run reports or local dashboard views
  • Experience working with contract manufacturers in software manufacturing test execution for PCBA and electronic assemblies
  • Familiarity with hardware protocols such as Ethernet, USB, PCIe, and SPI/I2C
  • Experience developing software manufacturing test solutions for aerospace, defense, or automotive hardware under environmental stress conditions (Thermal, Vibration, Burn-in)
  • Active U.S. Secret or Top Secret security clearance

Anduril is seeking a Mission Systems Lead to join the Omen team at our Costa Mesa HQ. Omen is Anduril’s hover-to-cruise autonomous air vehicle (AAV) that packs the endurance, payload, and mission flexibility of much larger airplanes into a novel runway-independent Group 3 platform. Omen can operate from ship decks, beaches, or remote island clearings, providing true runway independence and freedom of maneuver across defense and civilian domains. Omen is the first tail-sitter aircraft with a mass-production contract, with an order of 50 systems representing a decisive investment that anchors production and accelerates the development of future systems.

You will work on new aircraft development in a lean, high-ownership culture where you directly shape the product and operate at a velocity to fly new designs within months, not years

ABOUT THE JOB
You will lead a technical team in the development and integration of Omen’s Mission Systems, from initial concept through delivery. This encompasses mission perception, mission autonomy, and payload systems. You will work closely with program leadership, teams from other Anduril products, and third party system vendors to develop fully integrated Mission Systems based on requirements that are tied to customer inputs, with traceability to program office technical decisions.

Your spectrum of support will be diverse in nature and require you to leverage your technical expertise as well as leadership skills to set objectives, build cross-functional teams, and rapidly drive tasks to completion. The ability to leverage your intuition and prior experience will be key in making sure the right design, analysis, and test steps are completed to ensure success. The ideal candidate will leverage their experience executing and successfully completing prior highly optimized multi-disciplinary projects.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own customer success through the design and delivery of fully operational mission systems for a new Anduril platform, covering Mission Perception, Mission Autonomy, and Payloads.
  • Build and lead the Mission Systems team. Hire and manage multi-disciplinary engineers, mentor Junior and Senior Software Engineers from differing backgrounds, and set the team norms, technical standards, and review practices that let the team move quickly while delivering a fieldable solution.
  • Define and own the technical roadmap for Omen Mission Systems across short, medium, and long term horizons, balancing delivery against the current production commitment with the architecture investments that carry the platform forward.
  • Mission Autonomy: Own the software stack that enables Omen to autonomously execute customer defined missions. Includes a lifecycle toolchain covering mission design, planning, operation, and debrief, along with operator command and control.
  • Mission Payloads: Own integration of payload modules with the host vehicle mission system stack, including power, bandwidth, timing, and autonomy interfaces. Integrations to include passive and active sensor modalities along with launched effects, electronic warfare payloads and more.
  • Mission Perception: Own sensing and world model development, and safe and assured navigation, including operation in GPS-denied conditions and recovery to moving or austere landing sites.
  • Lead demonstrations of Autonomy, Payload operations, and Perception kits in increasingly representative environments from the lab to surrogates to Omen.
  • Partner with the Vehicle Software team on interfacing requirements between the Vehicle Management System and Mission System stacks.
  • Drive architecture selection and design for robotic mission systems, including hardware selection, compute, storage and network architecture, with explicit consideration of modular open systems approaches.
  • Define and own the payload interface control documents (ICDs) governing integration with third-party and government-furnished payload vendors.
  • Travel to support test events, vendor collaboration, end-user engagements and/or co-locate with other teams up to 25% of the time.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience as a Senior or staff robotics or software development engineer
  • Experience managing engineering teams within a high performing technology organization
  • Experience with the development and sustainment of distributed software platform and application architectures, running under dynamic network topologies
  • Experience with Python and modern systems/application programming languages (e.g., C++, Rust)
  • Deep understanding of autonomous systems, inclusive of perception and payload capabilities across commercial and military mission sets
  • Experience within the product delivery lifecycle including manufacturing, system acceptance, deployment, and sustainment
  • Familiarity with vehicle management systems and Systems Engineering concepts, including requirements traceability and ICDs
  • Familiarity with modular open systems approaches and standard interface protocols for air vehicle mission systems
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

  • Bachelor’s degree in Robotics, Mechatronics, Computer Science, Engineering, a relevant field, or equivalent experience
  • Experience with high assurance safety critical software, modeling and simulation, and comprehensive unit, integration, and regression test suites
  • Experience delivering perception, world modeling, or assured navigation capability for autonomous vehicles in GPS-denied environments
  • Experience building mission planning, operator control, or post-mission debrief tooling for uncrewed systems
  • Experience integrating third-party or government-furnished payloads into a new host platform, including ICD negotiation with external vendors
  • Experience troubleshooting and analyzing remotely deployed software systems
  • Track record of mentoring senior engineers, building team cohesion and capacity
  • Operational experience with autonomous air systems, ideally Group 3 or shipboard/expeditionary launch and recovery

ABOUT THE TEAM
Anduril's Maritime Division is transforming American sea power to meet the defining national security challenges of our era and secure our future of maritime dominance.

We are scaling at an historic pace, anchored by Arsenal-2, our new software-defined shipyard being built in Baltimore County, Maryland. It's part of a new $6.6 billion investment in America's submarine industrial base.

Arsenal-2 is purpose-built to break long-standing industrial bottlenecks and scale production of critical components for the Navy's Virginia-class attack submarines to support fleet requirements. At the same time, it will build the industrial muscle to field our next-generation AUVs at scale.

In Anduril's Maritime Division, we are actively building America's next decisive advantage at sea—and this is the moment to join us.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a highly motivated Network Engineer to join the Anduril Industries Network Team with a focus on factory systems and operational technology (OT) infrastructure.

In this role, you will design, deploy, and maintain the network systems that support Anduril’s manufacturing environments. You will work directly within production spaces and partner with Manufacturing Engineering, Facilities, Security, and IT teams to ensure that all factory networks are reliable, secure, and aligned with ISA-95 and Purdue Model standards.  This role is highly hands-on. You will regularly conduct site walks, site surveys, and hardware installation at Anduril facilities. You will also participate in inventory management, procurement planning, and coordination of hardware for factory deployments. The ideal candidate combines strong networking expertise with practical field experience in industrial, air gapped, or manufacturing environments.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Perform detailed site walks and site surveys to assess network needs, validate capacity, and plan installations in manufacturing spaces
  • Design and implement secure, segmented network architectures for factory and OT systems based on ISA-95 and Purdue Model principles
  • Install, configure, and support routers, switches, firewalls, wireless infrastructure, and industrial networking devices
  • Support manufacturing buildouts including new production lines, machine onboarding, and integration of control systems
  • Conduct hands-on cabling validation, equipment racking, hardware placement, and physical layer troubleshooting
  • Manage network equipment inventory across facilities including tracking, forecasting, and ordering hardware
  • Handle procurement activities for networking components and coordinate with vendors, suppliers, and subcontractors
  • Maintain accurate documentation for network topology, cabling, VLAN and IP assignments, and inter-zone communication flows
  • Implement and manage network security controls including segmentation, ACLs, firewalls, and intrusion detection or prevention
  • Monitor network performance and perform proactive maintenance to ensure stability of production and automation systems
  • Provide on-call support and escalation assistance for production and OT network incidents
  • Travel to remote facilities for surveys, installations, and infrastructure upgrades

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 5 to 7 years of Enterprise or OT network engineering experience with the ability to lead deployments with minimal guidance
  • Hands-on experience performing site surveys, field installations, and factory or industrial network buildouts
  • Familiarity with ISA-95 and Purdue Model segmentation for operational technology environments
  • Proficiency with Cisco, Arista, and Palo Alto platforms including Panorama and NGFW
  • Experience with Layer 2 and Layer 3 networking, wireless systems, and firewall policy management
  • Understanding of industrial protocols such as Modbus/TCP, Ethernet IP, and PROFINET with awareness of how to secure them
  • Experience with datacenter or private cloud networking such as EVPN VXLAN
  • Strong communication, documentation, and troubleshooting skills
  • Ability to lift 50 pounds and work in production or construction environments as needed
  • Ability to travel to remote sites for installation and support
  • Must be eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. TS clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with industrial networking platforms such as Rockwell Stratix, Hirschmann, or Moxa
  • Experience in environments that blend IT and OT security practices
  • Familiarity with Arista or Aruba hardware
  • Experience with AWS, Azure, GCP, or OCI
  • Experience with Python, Nornir, Jinja, Ansible, or Terraform for automation
  • Background supporting rapid-growth factory or manufacturing operations

ABOUT THE JOB

You will own payload integration within Mission Systems for a maritime autonomous vehicle, owning integration of Anduril and third-party payloads from concept through deployment. Reporting to the Mission Systems Lead, you will own payload interfaces, interoperability, mission development, and reference mission kits. You will ensure payloads meet customer mission requirements and integrate with the vehicle platform and autonomy stack.

Your spectrum of support will be diverse in nature and require you to leverage your technical expertise as well as leadership skills to set objectives, build cross-functional teams, and rapidly drive to completion. The ability to leverage your intuition and prior experience will be key in making sure the right design, analysis, and test steps are completed to ensure success. The ideal candidate will leverage their experience executing and successfully completing prior highly optimized multi-disciplinary projects.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own payload architecture: mechanical, electrical, and software interfaces for all mission payloads
  • Drive integration of Anduril payloads and government-furnished equipment onto the platform
  • Drive interoperability standards for payload modularity across vehicle configurations
  • Develop reference mission kits that package payloads with autonomy behaviors for specific mission sets
  • Define payload interface requirements and work with Vehicle Systems on accommodation
  • Manage payload integration schedule and cost across prototype and production phases
  • Coordinate with third-party vendors on payload qualification and integration
  • Provide technical mentorship to engineers across payload disciplines
  • Support testing and field deployment of payload systems
  • Represent the payload subsystem in technical and customer meetings
  • Interface with Mission Systems Lead and autonomy team on mission system integration
  • Travel up to 25% to test sites, vendor facilities, and customer locations

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent
  • 5+ years of experience in payload integration, weapons systems, or mission systems
  • Experience delivering payload integration in defense or aerospace environments
  • Demonstrated experience with sensor integration, weapons systems, or C4ISR payloads
  • Experience with the full product delivery lifecycle: design, test, manufacturing, deployment
  • Deep understanding of military mission sets and payload capabilities
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Top Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with maritime or undersea payload systems
  • Working knowledge of payload certification and weapons safety (MIL-STD-882E)
  • Experience with autonomous systems payload integration
  • Familiarity with modular open systems architecture (MOSA)
  • Prior Navy or defense operational experience
